[p. 62] **Sūrat Yūnus (Peace be upon him)**

It is the first of the *mi'īn* (surahs of about a hundred verses or so, the second group of long surahs) if one counts Barā'ah together with al-Anfāl as one long surah. Otherwise, Barā'ah is the first of them. Its central theme is describing the Book as coming from God, from God, because of the wisdom it contains, and that it is nothing but from Him, glory be to Him, since no one else is able to produce anything like it. This clearly indicates that He is one in His dominion, with no partner in any of His affairs. The complete proof of this is the story of the people of Yūnus (peace be upon him): when they believed at the sign of the approaching punishment, the punishment was lifted from them. This decisively shows that the One who sent it is God, in whom they believed. Had it been other than Him, their belief in Him would have required that they be struck. And had they been punished like others, it would have been said, "This is the custom of the age," as they said, "Adversity and prosperity have touched our fathers." This also shows that the punishment of other nations is only from God, because of their disbelief. What is consistent in this, by way of concomitance, with the circumstances of all other nations, is that whenever persistence in denial exists, punishment exists. And by way of converse, whenever it is absent at a time when repentance is accepted, punishment is absent. And God is the Granter of success.

"In the name of God" (*bismillāh*), meaning the One to whom no command belongs but Him, so no speech resembles His speech and there is no equal to Him. "The Most Merciful" (*al-Raḥmān*), who by His speech encompassed all His creation and made the explanation clear. "The Most Compassionate" (*al-Raḥīm*), who completed for His obedient servants the blessing of grace.

﴿Alif. Lām. Rā.﴾ Ibn Kathīr, Nāfi' and Ḥafṣ on the authority of ʿĀṣim pronounce the *rā'* with *tafkhīm* (heavy, full pronunciation). Warsh on the authority of Nāfi' pronounces it with *imālah* (the raising of the vowel toward *i*) *bayn bayn* (an intermediate degree). The rest pronounce it with pure *imālah* (*al-imālah al-maḥḍah*). The original form in such cases is *fatḥ* (the open vowel, i.e. *a*). The same applies to similar cases where the *alif* does not derive from a *yā'*, such as *mā* and *lā*. Its *imālah* serves to indicate that these are names of letters and not letters themselves. This was reported from al-Wāḥidī.

When, at the beginning of al-A'rāf, He had urged the conveying of counsel through this Book, and had finished with what the context required of warning against the like of the events of the earlier peoples and the fates of those who passed away, and with what follows from that, namely presenting the account of this noble Prophet with his people at the beginning of his mission, in the middle, and at the end, in the two surahs al-Anfāl and Barā'ah, and concluded that the surahs of the Book increase each person in what suits him and is prepared for his acceptance, and distance him from what is incompatible with him and far from accepting it, and that the Messenger (ﷺ) has, by all this, gathered the attributes, adornments and lofty character that necessitate turning to him and hastening towards him, and the report that their turning away from him does not harm him at all, because his Lord is sufficient for him, since He has no like and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne: when all this was so, He, glory be to Him, repeated the discourse concerning the Book with which He had opened al-A'rāf and closed the surah of al-Tawbah. He added to it the description of being *ḥakīm* (wise), and indicated by the demonstrative of distance that its rank therein is far to attain and wondrous in its likeness. So He said: ﴿Those﴾, meaning the very great signs contained in this surah, or the surahs that preceded this surah, or these disjointed letters, which point to the Qur'an being the speech of God; otherwise it would not have rendered incapable those who are able to pronounce these letters.

﴿The signs of the Book﴾, meaning the Reminder that gathers every good, which is this Qur'an. Every narrative in it agrees with all that is in the Torah and the Gospel concerning those narratives. This indicates the truthfulness of the one who brought it, decisively, because he did not know anything of what is in the two Books and did not sit with anyone who taught him. ﴿The wise﴾. Earlier, the fact that it is from God was sufficient for the obligation to follow it. Here the obligation is emphasized by its being, in addition to that, wise. An *āyah* (sign) is a mark that reports the end of speech from a particular aspect. *Ḥakīm* (wise) means one who speaks with wisdom (*ḥikmah*), which is known as that by which is gathered what prevents action from corruption and deficiency. This word is applied figuratively to the Qur'an because it is a guide, like one who speaks with wisdom, since it leads to the knowledge by which the path of salvation is distinguished from the path of destruction. It is also a judge that makes clear the truth from falsehood in the fundamentals and the derivatives, and rules with justice in which there is no injustice in any way in every event; and it is *muḥkam* (firmly made), what it brought being fixed and preventing it from corruption, not erased by water, nor burned by fire, nor changed by the ages. This is what became clear to me in its linkage with what precedes it. Imam Abū Ja'far Ibn al-Zubayr said: when the surah of Barā'ah contained His saying, ﴿If you do not help him, God has already helped him﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40], and His saying, ﴿God pardon you! Why did you give them permission?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 43], and His saying, ﴿And mercy for those of you who believe. As for those who abuse the Messenger of God, for them is a painful punishment﴾ [al-Tawbah: 61], and His saying, ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128], to the end of the surah, and what intervened within the verses of this noble surah of testimony to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) by singling him out with the privileges of precedence, nearness, special favour, gentleness in address, and describing him with kindness and mercy, all this, together with al-Anfāl, encompassed his subduing of his enemies, his being supported and aided against them, the manifestation of his religion, the elevation of his call, and the exaltation of his word, and other blessings of God, glory be to Him, upon him. All this was a cause for the wonder of the doubter and the hesitation of the skeptic, and a stirring of the dormant envy of the great enemy at what he (peace be upon him) had been granted. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Is it a wonder to people that We revealed to a man from among them: "Warn the people"﴾ [Yūnus: 2], up to His saying: (p. 65) ﴿Indeed, this is clear magic﴾ [Yūnus: 76]. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is God﴾ [Yūnus: 3], and so on through the verses. He thus made clear that He alone is Lord, Creator, Originator and Governor. So how could His actions be objected to, or how could humans comprehend the wisdom in everything He does and manifests? Since all is His dominion and creation, He does in His dominion what He wills and judges in His creation as He desires.

﴿That is God, your Lord, so worship Him﴾ [Yūnus: 3]. ﴿God did not create that except in truth﴾ [Yūnus: 5]. Then He, glory be to Him, threatened those heedless of reflecting upon His great signs, to the point that heedlessness led them to the same error of their predecessors, in wonder and denial, until they said: ﴿What is wrong with this Messenger? He eats food and walks in the markets﴾ [al-Furqān: 7]. They also said: ﴿Why have angels not been sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?﴾ [al-Furqān: 21]. These are the sayings of the earlier nations: ﴿They said, "You are only human like us"﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 15]; ﴿So they said, "Shall we believe two humans like us?"﴾ [al-Mu'minūn: 47]; ﴿This is only a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship﴾ [Saba': 43]. So He, the Exalted, said, threatening the heedless: ﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us and are satisfied with the worldly life﴾ [Yūnus: 7]. Then He promised those who take heed, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will guide them by their faith﴾ [Yūnus: 9], and the verses that follow. All of this shows clear interconnection and beautiful harmony; the verses of the surahs are woven together. End.

And when it was the case that its being from Allah, together with its being wise, necessitated its acceptance from the outset and rejoicing in it, because of what is established in minds and what natural disposition has been created to recognise, namely that He, exalted is He, is the Creator, the Provider, the Remover of harm, and the Administrator of affairs, that was the place for someone to ask: What was the condition of those to whom it was recited? So it was said: They did not believe. Then it was asked: What was their doubt? Were they able to oppose it and to find fault with its wisdom? It was said: No. Rather, they wondered at its being sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), though he was neither the richest of them in wealth nor the oldest of them in years. So the outcome of their wonder returned to what He, exalted is He, said, as a rebuke to them. For if He had sent someone older, they would have said the same thing. Yet is such a thing a cause for wonder? ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind?﴾ [that is, in any respect whatsoever] ﴿for mankind﴾, that is, those among them who have the capacity to strive towards lofty matters. Wonder ('ajab) is the soul's being moved by something whose cause is not known, of what departs from custom. Then He mentioned what prompts the wonder, which is the name of "kāna" (is), and said, after a longing for it had arisen in them: ﴿that We revealed﴾, that is, We cast Our commands, with the greatness that belongs to Us, through Our messengers, in secrecy, [addressing] ﴿to a man﴾, that is, [one who is] in the utmost degree of manhood, and who, despite that, is ﴿of them﴾, such that they know all of his affairs, just as We did with those before them. And the King, the Great in Sovereignty, the Possessor of complete dominion, against whom there is no objection in what makes His distinction apparent, by exalting whomever He wills.

And since revelation contains the meaning of speech, He explained it by His saying: ﴿Warn mankind﴾, that is, in general, namely those whose address was mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, of what lies before them of resurrection and other things, if they do not believe at all, or believe with a sincere faith that negates every minor or major disobedience and every grave or trivial lapse, according to the differences in ranks and the variation of stations. ﴿And give good tidings﴾, that is, single out ﴿those who believe﴾, that is, those who brought this attribute into being and acted, confirming their claim [to it] with ﴿righteous deeds﴾, that is, of the deeds of the tongue and others, with the good tidings of the acceptance of their good deeds, the covering of their bad deeds, the overlooking of their lapses, and the elevation of their ranks, just as the sending of the messengers before him was, and as justice requires in rewarding the obedient and rebuking the disobedient. Warning (indhār) is informing about what one should beware of, and giving good tidings (tabshīr) is making known what brings joy. He attributed "qadam" (footing), which is precedence in obedience, to truthfulness, in His saying, exalted is He, conveying the act of giving good tidings to what the good tidings concern without a preposition: ﴿that for them there is﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿a sure footing﴾, that is, true and established deeds which they put forward for themselves, being truthful in them and sincere in what they were made easy for, [because] they were created for it, and it was of what is pursued by the feet. And He added to the good tidings by His saying: ﴿with their Lord﴾. [In the attribution of "footing"] there is an admonition that obedience must be made sincere [for Him] as sincerity of truthfulness is free from the taints of falsehood. And in the expression by the attribute of excellence (iḥsān) there is an indication of multiplication.

And since it is established that the Messenger and what he was sent with are in accordance with custom, it is negated that this should be a wonder from this respect. Thus the situation became suitable for them to be wondered at, so it is asked: What did they say when they showed wonder, and from what standpoint did they see it as a wonder? It was said: ﴿The disbelievers said﴾, that is, those firmly rooted in this attribute [among them, and others followed them], emphasising what the denial in their saying [deserves]: ﴿Indeed this﴾, that is, the saying and what it contains of information about what is not known, of resurrection and other things, ﴿is certainly a magician﴾, that is, Muhammad is certainly a magician, as in the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī, ﴿clear﴾, that is, manifest in himself, and by the intensity of its manifestness it makes everything manifest that it is so. Yet they came with what is at the utmost remove from his description, for it has been established for every person of intellect that magic, while being a deception with no reality, is pure evil, containing nothing of wisdom, let alone reaching its summit. Moreover, in that they claim a contradictory matter: that it is from human speech, as is the custom with magic, and that they are incapable of it, because magic is an act in which the trick is hidden so that the miracle is imagined through it. Thus they have acknowledged incapacity regarding it and lied in claiming that it is magic; for the one who brought it did not ever leave them, nor did he mix with a scholar, neither in magic nor otherwise, so that a doubt might be mixed in for them regarding it. So they know that their saying is in utmost corruption,

So He, glorified is He, began to establish the proof against their claim that it (the Qur'an), together with what it contains of resurrection, is sorcery. He also established that it is truly from Him, beyond any doubt, and that there is nothing strange about prophethood. This is because He, glorified is He, created all existence, and His command is effective in it. He has also tested the rational beings within it, in order to return them to Himself and call them to account. He did not create them in vain, since He is All-Wise. Therefore there must be a messenger who informs them of what pleases Him and what angers Him, so that the proof may be established through this. So He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord﴾, that is, the One who brought you into being, nurtures you, and bestows good upon you, ﴿is Allah﴾, that is, the One who nurtures whatever deserves to be wise and capable of the means of its well-being. So awaken yourselves from the drowsiness of your heedlessness, that you may know with certainty that this Book is from the One to whom belongs all greatness, and that He is able to resurrect you, because He is your Lord, ﴿who﴾ began creation by ﴿creating﴾, that is, by decreeing and bringing into existence, ﴿the heavens and the earth﴾, despite their vastness and the abundance of benefits in them, ﴿in six days﴾, for a wisdom He willed. This indicates that this is a short period of time, and that no one does the like of this in such a period except the One whom nothing can overpower.

When Allah, glorified is He, had brought into existence this vast creation, widely dispersed in its regions and far-reaching in its spread, requiring great management and subtle disposition and measuring, He expressed His action in it by the action of kings in their realms. He said, pointing to His greatness by the particle of delay: ﴿Then He established Himself﴾, that is, He worked in its management, perfecting what is in it and making it firm, with the action of one who takes care of this, ﴿upon the Throne﴾, whose greatness has been mentioned earlier. The "then" (thumma) is not for sequence but is a kinayah (metonymy) for the loftiness of rank and the remoteness of attaining it. Then He explained that establishment by His saying: ﴿He arranges﴾, because management is the most just of the conditions of a king. So "establishment" is a kinayah for it. ﴿the affair﴾ entirely. Nothing of the affairs is hidden from Him, and by this security is achieved from anything being done without His knowledge. This is because management is placing matters in their proper ranks with firm regard for their outcomes. Yet He is, along with that, exalted above what you know of the conditions of kings, namely that in their realms there are those who decide some matters without their permission, even if they know of it, because they are unable to openly and continuously repel it. Rather, He is described as ﴿no intercessor﴾, that is, even if one were eloquent in that description.

Since the completeness of His dominion and the greatness of His authority do not benefit anyone in the presence of His permission, unless He grants permission to him as a general permission for all times and places, He brought the prepositional phrase and said: ﴿except after His permission﴾. If an intercessor cannot speak regarding intercession except by His permission, then how can anyone bring anything at all without His permission? How, then, could one bring a Book, wise, not from Him, which creation is unable to oppose? Thus security is achieved that it could be someone other than Him who said it, or who interceded for the one who conveyed it, and so conveyed it without His will, glorified is He. It is therefore established that it is nothing but from Him, and that he was commanded to convey it. It has been understood from this that ﴿no intercessor﴾ is in the position of indicating that no matter of the affairs departs from His management, and nothing overpowers Him at all. Thus what they used to say about the idols regarding intercession and other things is invalidated. The intercessor (shafi') is the one who asks on behalf of another, by making known his rank, for pardon or for an increase in rank.

The Book, the Messenger, and the Throne have been mentioned here in an order that corresponds to the order in which they were mentioned at the end of that (previous) passage. When His attributes of greatness, in which no one shares with Him, were established, it became necessary that He be worshipped with a worship in which nothing shares with Him. So He alerted them to this by His saying: ﴿That is﴾, that is, the One of great station and high ranks, ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, ﴿your Lord﴾, who has been established as possessing such greatness and beneficence through bringing into existence and nurturing, that no description can reach it, ﴿so worship Him﴾, that is, single Him out with worship. For your worship along with association is not worship. Had it not been for His bounty, no one who slips even the slightest slip would have any obedience.

When He, glorified is He, made the requirement of worship obligatory on the basis of His exalted attributes, the rebuke against them followed for their hesitation in it and their need, in regard to it, for the manifestation of a command to do it. He established by it the proofs of His entitlement to be worshipped alone, the evidences of which are within them. So He said: ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾, that is, even with the least kinds of remembrance, by what the idgham (assimilation of letters, here the doubling of the letter in tadhakkarun) indicates. He, glorified is He, has informed you of this and alerted you to it through what every person knows from himself: that no one can do everything he wishes, and does much of what he has no purpose in, and knows that it harms him, and other such matters. So that you may know with certainty that the true Agent is other than him, and that this existence necessarily has an effecting cause, which is in the utmost greatness, and that nothing can possibly share with Him in any way, even if it were the greatest of what is known among things. How then (could it be) with a lifeless object that neither harms nor benefits!

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 4:

When it was established that He is the One who originates creation, it was thereby established that He is able to repeat it. So He said: ﴿To Him alone﴾, that is, exclusively, ﴿is your return﴾, that is, your returning, the place of your return and its time, ﴿all of you﴾, with none of you exempted. His promise to you of this has preceded: ﴿the promise of Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses all perfection, ﴿in truth﴾ (p-٧٢). This is a justification for worshipping Him alone. So they will live after death and be gathered to the place of Allah's recompense, at the time He has appointed for it, and what they had of ability in this world will be removed. Thus it is known with certainty that there must be a Messenger, so prepare yourselves to meet this Greatest King by doing everything the Messenger (ﷺ) has commanded you.

Then he clarified the warning about His power, including within it the explanation of His wisdom. He said, giving the reason for the obligation of returning to Him, emphasizing it by counting them among those who deny the beginning, because of their denial of what follows from it of the complete power to resurrect and other things: ﴿Indeed, He originates creation﴾, that is, He brings it into being in the first production. This attribute is His, with continuously renewed connection, by way of continuity. ﴿Then He repeats it﴾, so that He may establish justice among His creatures by fulfilling for the one who worshipped Him His promise to honor him and humiliate his enemy. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿that He may reward﴾.

Since it is in the context of resurrection, He placed first the people of recompense and began with their nobles, so He said: ﴿Those who believed﴾, that is, brought into being this attribute, which is the firm foundation of every righteous deed, ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, that is, affirmed their faith by doing ﴿righteous deeds﴾, ﴿as recompense with justice﴾ [He restricted it to justice without bounty so that it would be understood that omitting filler (al-ḥashw) harms the deed, which is the locus of wisdom, the greatest of the benefits of the surah]. Recompense (al-jazā') is giving, in accordance with the deed, what it requires of good or evil. So if the giving were a beginning, it would not be recompense, and if it were what the deed does not require, it would not be recompense in an absolute sense (p-٧٣). Al-qisṭ (justice) means ʿadl (equity).

﴿And those who disbelieved﴾, that is, brought into being this attribute, ﴿for them﴾, that is, in recompense, on the basis of entitlement, ﴿is a drink of scalding water﴾, that is, heated by the fire to the utmost heating, ﴿and a painful punishment﴾, that is, reaching the utmost in causing pain, ﴿because they used to disbelieve﴾, that is, by nature and disposition. Their punishment is among the greatest of the blessings of the believers, who were hostile to them in it, glory be to Him: ﴿Today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 34] ﴿on couches, observing﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 35] ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 36]. It is as if He said: "yabda'u" in the present tense, unlike His saying in another verse: ﴿As He originated you, you will return﴾ [al-A'rāf: 29], narrating the state and depicting it, as an alert to contemplate what is continuously renewed in its origination, so that it would be more effective for them in conceiving the power to repeat. Al-Rummānī said: The verse has included an explanation of what empowerment (al-tamkīn) in this world requires of renewing the creation for recompense, because there must be, along with empowerment, good and evil, and encouragement and warning, with which punishment for eternity is not safe, so that the accountable person, by being restrained from evil, moves out of the state of permissiveness, which would remove responsibility from him. End of quotation.

Thus it has become clear from what has been mentioned that what was established throughout the surah, by its repetition for clarification and confirmation, is that its aim is to describe the Book in a way that certainly indicates it is from Him, glory be to Him, and by His permission, because nothing is hidden from His knowledge, nothing is near to His power in equality, and no one dares against His greatness. He is perfect in power, singular in creation and command, so He is able to repeat as He was able to originate (p-٧٤). The purpose of the Book is good tidings and warning, for success at the resurrection and salvation from the perils of the Day of Gathering, together with the fact that He, glory be to Him, has an executed decree, so the signs and clear proofs do not avail one who has been judged to wretchedness and decreed to misguidance. This is part of His wisdom and justice, so submission to His command is obligatory and the aspirations must be severed from anything else.

Then He, glory be to Him, proceeded to establish the matter of His originating creation and its return, in a context that reminds of the blessings that must be thanked, and one who turns away from giving thanks for them is called a disbeliever. So He said: ﴿He is the One who made﴾, i.e., none other than Him, ﴿the sun﴾, i.e., by means of the causes He prepared.

Since light is a quality that admits of intensity and weakness, He, glory be to Him, varied the names in a way that indicates this. So He said of the sun's light: ﴿a radiance﴾, i.e., possessing a strong, shining light, ﴿and He determined for it stations﴾. Thus is the determination: however, since in its movement it is slow relative to the moon, He mentioned the moon apart from it, and said: ﴿and the moon﴾, i.e., and He made the moon ﴿a light﴾, i.e., possessing light from its light, ﴿and determined for it stations﴾, i.e., He added to it over the sun by determining for it a course of ﴿stations﴾, swift, by which He turns it. And by the variation of its condition in the increase and decrease of its light, the conditions of moisture and heat vary, by which God ordered this existence, along with other secrets which are a branch of the existence of night and day. ﴿That you may know﴾ thereby, with an easy knowledge, ﴿the number of years﴾, i.e., those divided into the four seasons and what connects to that of months and others, (p-75) so that you may be able to arrange your livelihood according to the conditions of the seasons and otherwise, ﴿and the reckoning﴾, i.e., other than that of what indicates some of His arrangement, glory be to Him.

[Since that is observed without doubt] in it, He joined to it His saying: ﴿God did not create that except in truth﴾, i.e., He to whom belongs all perfection, ﴿that﴾, i.e., the very great matter, ﴿except in truth﴾, i.e., creating it connected with the truth, which is complete in its truthfulness, without doubt in it. Thus it is known that He is capable of bringing the Hour into existence in the same way, since there is no difference. And if His creation is thus, how could His command, from which creation arises, be other than creation, such as being of magic, whose basis is deception and imagination, which is pure falsehood? Or [it is] that He did not create it except by way of manifesting the truth of justice among the servants, by honoring the obedient and humbling the disobedient, for there is no bliss like triumph over the enemy and vengeance against the hater. And "making" (al-ja'l): the existence of that by which a thing becomes in a state it was not in. "The sun": a body of great light, for it is the brightness of the day. "The moon": a luminous body that spreads its light over all the visible part of the earth, and the light of the sun eclipses it. "Light" (nur): a ray containing what is contrary to darkness. "Reckoning" (hisab): a number by which the measure of a thing is obtained from another.

Since the consideration of these signs is so clear that it does not require much of the quality of readiness for knowledge, He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿He details﴾, i.e., God, (p-76) in the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, and Hafs from 'Asim with the yā' (third person), and by the shift to the style of majesty, glorifying the clarity in the reading of the rest with the nūn: ﴿the signs﴾, i.e., He makes clear the dazzling proofs one after another, detailed in a healing explanation. And since explanation for one who has no knowledge is as nothing, He said: ﴿for a people﴾, i.e., who have the strength of striving toward what they seek, ﴿who know﴾, i.e., this attribute belongs to them in a manner of renewal and continuity. And since they have complete knowledge and penetrating insight into the stations of the moon, it is counted among the evident matters.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 6:

When He, glorified be He, pointed to the inference of the annihilation of the world through its change, and to the power to resurrect through the bringing into existence of each of the two worlds (the upper and lower) after its annihilation, in His saying, emphasizing it because of their denial that there is any indication in that, ﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night﴾, meaning, showing the diversity of its attributes, ﴿and the day﴾, meaning likewise, ﴿and what﴾, meaning and in what, ﴿Allah has created﴾, meaning He to whom belongs complete encompassing, ﴿in the heavens and the earth﴾, of the conditions of the clouds and rains, and what occurs from that: the sinking of the earth, earthquakes, minerals, plants, animals, and other conditions of all things, which man cannot encompass in enumeration. When He pointed to that, He concluded it with His saying: ﴿are signs﴾, meaning clear indications in the extreme, ﴿for a people who fear [Allah]﴾, meaning that whoever looks into this alternation and reflects on the change of the great celestial bodies is deserving of fearing that his condition may be changed and his affairs thrown into turmoil, so that he fears Allah, knowing with certainty that the people of this abode are not left neglected, so there must be for them a command, a prohibition, a reward and a punishment. And ikhtilaf (alternation, difference) is the going of each of two things in a direction other than the direction of the other. So the alternation of the two worlds (night and day) is the going of one of them in the direction of light and the other in the direction of darkness. And al-layl (the night) is darkness from the sunset to the emergence of the second dawn; it is the plural of laylah, like tamr and tamrah. And al-nahar (the day) is the spreading of light from the emergence of the second dawn to the sunset. And al-khalq (creation) is the doing of a thing in accordance with what wisdom requires, and its origin is determination (taqdir). By what He created in the heavens and the earth He alerted to the aspects of indication, because indication in a thing may come from its creation, or the diversity of its form, or the beauty of its appearance, or the abundance of its benefit, or the greatness of its matter, or other than that.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verses 7–8:

When the verse had indicated the passing away of the world, that what is created has no permanence, and the decisive proof for the Return (ma'ad) had been established, it was fitting to follow it with the censure of those who were content with it, in a context that makes clear that the cause of contentment is the denial of contentment, either in belief or in state. And since that verse was concluded with ﴿they fear God (yattaqun)﴾ [Yunus: 6], it became evident that there are those who are mindful (of God) and those who are not. And since the deluded were the majority, he began with them, to warn against their condition, because the averting of harms (dar' al-mafasid) takes precedence over the securing of benefits (jalb al-masalih). So he said, emphasizing it because of their denial: ﴿Indeed, those who﴾. And since fear and hope are the source (ma'din) of happiness, and hope is closer to urging one toward turning (to God), he spoke explicitly of hope while alluding to fear: ﴿do not hope for Our meeting﴾, that is, the resurrection after death, ﴿and do not fear what is ours of greatness﴾, ﴿and are content﴾, that is, in exchange (ʿiwadan) (p-78) for the Hereafter, ﴿with the life of this world﴾ [that is], they acted for it as one who dwells in it permanently, together with what it contains that points to its worthlessness, ﴿and are at rest﴾ in it, along with contentment ﴿with it﴾, the rest of one who is not disturbed from it, along with what they witness of its swift passing away. ﴿And those who are﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿heedless of Our signs﴾, that is, of their greatness, not of other lowly and perishable states, ﴿heedless﴾, that is, drowned in heedlessness.

His saying, the Exalted, as a resumption (istinaf) includes: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the far-removed and the hated, ﴿their abode is the Fire, because of what﴾, that is, because of what ﴿they used to earn﴾, that is, by nature and disposition, for all of their earning is misguidance, namely that He does not hasten punishment upon them for delaying repentance. The encountering of what only God can determine is made into the encountering of God, to magnify its matter, just as the coming of the great signs of God is made in His saying: ﴿unless God comes to them in canopies of cloud﴾ [al-Baqarah: 210] and the like. Itmi'nan (rest/contentment) is leaning toward a thing with firm settling in it. So these made the states firmly established for the world, such that their joy and their anger became for it. Ghaflah (heedlessness) is the departure of meaning from the heart by what is contrary to its presence before it; yaqzah (wakefulness) is its opposite.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verses 7–8:

When the verse had indicated the passing away of the world, that what is created has no permanence, and the decisive proof for the Return (ma'ad) had been established, it was fitting to follow it with the censure of those who were content with it, in a context that makes clear that the cause of contentment is the denial of contentment, either in belief or in state. And since that verse was concluded with ﴿they fear God (yattaqun)﴾ [Yunus: 6], it became evident that there are those who are mindful (of God) and those who are not. And since the deluded were the majority, he began with them, to warn against their condition, because the averting of harms (dar' al-mafasid) takes precedence over the securing of benefits (jalb al-masalih). So he said, emphasizing it because of their denial: ﴿Indeed, those who﴾. And since fear and hope are the source (ma'din) of happiness, and hope is closer to urging one toward turning (to God), he spoke explicitly of hope while alluding to fear: ﴿do not hope for Our meeting﴾, that is, the resurrection after death, ﴿and do not fear what is ours of greatness﴾, ﴿and are content﴾, that is, in exchange (ʿiwadan) (p-78) for the Hereafter, ﴿with the life of this world﴾ [that is], they acted for it as one who dwells in it permanently, together with what it contains that points to its worthlessness, ﴿and are at rest﴾ in it, along with contentment ﴿with it﴾, the rest of one who is not disturbed from it, along with what they witness of its swift passing away. ﴿And those who are﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿heedless of Our signs﴾, that is, of their greatness, not of other lowly and perishable states, ﴿heedless﴾, that is, drowned in heedlessness.

His saying, the Exalted, as a resumption (istinaf) includes: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the far-removed and the hated, ﴿their abode is the Fire, because of what﴾, that is, because of what ﴿they used to earn﴾, that is, by nature and disposition, for all of their earning is misguidance, namely that He does not hasten punishment upon them for delaying repentance. The encountering of what only God can determine is made into the encountering of God, to magnify its matter, just as the coming of the great signs of God is made in His saying: ﴿unless God comes to them in canopies of cloud﴾ [al-Baqarah: 210] and the like.
