Ghaflah (heedlessness) is the departure of meaning from the heart by what is contrary to its presence before it; yaqzah (wakefulness) is its opposite.

When this division had concluded in both its state and its outcome, the Exalted followed it with the other division, emphasizing it in refutation of the disbelievers' denial of their guidance, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe﴾, meaning they brought this attribute into being through what they possess of theoretical faculty (al-quwwah al-nazariyyah), whose perfection is knowing things and whose authority is knowing God, the Exalted. ﴿And do righteous deeds﴾, meaning they fulfilled their claim of faith by doing ﴿righteous deeds﴾ through the practical faculty (al-quwwah al-'amaliyyah), whose authority is the servitude of God, the Exalted. The righteous (al-salih) is that which the prophets, peace be upon them, came urging. ﴿Their Lord will guide them﴾, meaning in a manner of continual renewal and persistence, ﴿Their Lord﴾, meaning the One who is good to them, ﴿by their faith﴾, meaning because of their assent and submission to recognizing the signs, which those who hope for permanence and do not expect the meeting neglected. So it led them to the Abode of Peace. This is like the case of many of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, after their conversion, who would greatly marvel at [what had been] their own slowness in embracing Islam. And as you see, you may become angry at some of the perfected ones, and the claims of the self do not let you see any good in him; then you may later be pleased with him and see him entirely as virtues.

When he mentioned that the outcome of the first division is the Fire, he mentioned the outcome of this division in the context of answering one who asks: what does their guidance bring them? So it was said to him: ﴿Flow﴾, and he indicated the nearness of the attainment of the waters and their being unveiled from everything that can be benefited from in other than that, by affirming the preposition, so he said: ﴿beneath them﴾, meaning beneath their chambers, their couches, and other of their desired things, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Your Lord has made beneath you a stream﴾ [Maryam: 24], and likewise the saying of Pharaoh: ﴿And these rivers flow beneath me﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 51]. ﴿The rivers﴾ being ﴿in Gardens of Bliss﴾ [meaning those in which there is nothing of other than that].

Since the duty upon the servants is first to declare God far exalted above deficiencies (*tanzih*), the greatest of which is associating partners with Him, and whoever does this is safe from the perils of error, gains his soul, knows his Lord, and triumphs in witnessing His presence by beholding the attributes of perfection, he indicated the guidance (*taslik*) in this by His words: ﴿Their call therein﴾, that is, their great, constant and abundant supplication which they say therein, [not] as an obligation, but they are inspired to it as the inspiration of the soul in this world, ﴿therein﴾. He indicated the comprehensive points of transcendence above every trace of deficiency, saying: ﴿Glory be to You, O God﴾, indicating the first matter, which is the foundation, and it is the ascent (*mi'raj*) in the Hereafter. ﴿And their greeting﴾, that is, to God, and among themselves, ﴿is peace therein﴾, indicating the first result of the foundation, that no ruin accompanies it in any way, and it is a descent from the ascent by looking at the conditions of creation. ﴿And the last of their call﴾, that is, their great supplication, which is the perfective ascent (*mi'raj kamali*), ﴿is that: all praise﴾, that is, perfection, ﴿belongs to God﴾, that is, who encompasses all attributes of majesty and beauty. This means that transcendence from deficiency made safety obligatory for them; and when they were safe from every deficiency and reached the presence, they were submerged in the seas of majesty and the marks of perfection were revealed to them. *Da'wa* is a saying by which one is called to a matter; *tahiyya* is honoring with a noble state, its origin being from their saying: "May God give you a good life." He indicated by His words ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾ the blessing of origination, guiding thereby to the power over the return, and in it is a descent from the perfective ascent to creation; and that is an indication that man is never free from need and deficiency.

In this verse, after He pointed to His transcendence, His exaltedness, and His being singled out for the attributes of perfection, and after concluding it with "Praise" which indicates His comprehensiveness, and with "Lord of the worlds" which indicates the completeness of His power and the excellence of His management in both the origination and the return of creation, He followed this with what indicates, from His gentleness in His dealings, that He does nothing before its appointed time, because hastiness is a mark of need. Abu Ya'la and Ahmad ibn Mani' also narrated from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Deliberateness is from Allah, and haste is from Satan." Our shaykh Ibn Hajar said: "On this subject there are also narrations from Sahl and Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with them both."

Then He, Exalted is He, said, linking it to His words ﴿He manages the affair﴾ [Yunus: 3], meaning: He acts as one who considers the final outcomes of affairs, so He does only what is in the utmost firmness. He does not hasten punishment upon the disobedient; rather He gives them respite and lavishes blessings upon them, while they, in their state of disobedience to Him, are more astray than cattle, seeking His good things and hastening them for them. ﴿And if Allah were to hasten﴾, meaning the One encompassing the attributes of perfection, ﴿for the people﴾ [meaning] those who have taken the Qur'an as a wonder, because of the state of agitation that is theirs, ﴿the evil, in hastening it for them﴾, meaning acting upon His will to bring evil upon them, like their own action in their will and their seeking to hasten, ﴿with the good, it would have been decreed﴾, meaning it would have been determined, finalized, and carried out. It is in the passive form in the reading of the majority, indicating its insignificance to Him, and because what is feared is merely its completion, not that it is from a specific source. Ibn 'Amir read it in the active form and put "the term" in the accusative. ﴿To them﴾, meaning to the people specifically, ﴿is their term﴾, meaning their lifespan, or the last moment that will be from Him, so that whoever is on the earth would be destroyed and the order He arranged would fall into disarray. But He does only what has preceded of His granting them respite until the appointed terms, which vary, and this is the cause of misguiding whoever He wills to misguide. Perhaps the expression with the plural of majesty in ﴿So We leave﴾ indicates that the matter is at the utmost clarity. The analogy would have been that He guide them, given the abundance of clear proofs on it; but He, Exalted is He, willed their misguidance, and He is of such majesty that nothing can overpower Him. [p. 82] It is also possible that it is linked to His words ﴿Those—their abode is the Fire﴾ [Yunus: 8], because its meaning is: those—Allah gives them respite until the end of the terms He set for them, despite their extreme aversion, and then their abode will be the Fire, and He does not hasten for them what they deserve of evil. ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for the people the evil﴾, meaning: if He were to will the hastening of evil for the people when they oppose Him, or when they hasten it upon themselves, as in their saying: ﴿Rain down upon us stones from the heaven﴾ [al-Anfal: 32], and a person's supplication against his child and his servant, ﴿like their hastening﴾, meaning like their desire to hasten good. He departed from saying "if Allah were to seek to hasten for the people evil", to ﴿their hastening with the good﴾, meaning: He hastens, to avert the appearance of deficiency, because one who hastens a thing may be seeking its speed out of inability, and to alert that the matter is only in His hand. ﴿It would have been decreed to them their term﴾, for when He wills a thing, it comes to be and does not fail at all.

Since the estimate is that "law" [in "lau"] is conditional (i.e., "if... then not"), the meaning is: but He, glorified is He, does not do that, because nothing escapes Him; rather He gives the wrongdoers respite, showers them with blessings, and afflicts them with some of the punishments until they say: "This is the custom of time; hardship and ease have touched our fathers." This is a consequence of His words ﴿So We leave﴾, meaning in whatever state they are, and the expression is placed in the position of the pronoun to single them out and to alert to what made them turn away and become bold.

His words: ﴿Those who﴾. By negating hope, He indicated the negation of fear in the most eloquent manner, saying: ﴿do not expect the meeting with Us﴾, [meaning] after death, with this respite, regarding what is ours of majesty, for whoever feels secure from it is more astray than cattle, ﴿in their transgression﴾, meaning: their going beyond the limits, a going beyond that no one with even a little reflection would do, ﴿wandering blindly﴾ [meaning] by the judgment of Our previous will from eternity, blind to seeing the signs, deaf to hearing the clear proofs. And "ta'jil" (hastening) means placing a thing before its time which is more appropriate for it; "sharr" (evil) means the appearance of that which contains harm, and its root is manifestation, from their saying: "sharartu the garment" when you displayed it to the sun, and from it "sharar al-nar" (sparks of fire), because of its manifestation by its spreading; "tughyan" (transgression) means excessiveness in wronging the servants; and "'amah" means intense bewilderment.

When God explained that their habit is to seek good hastily, and that seeking the removal of harm was part of it, He explained that their state in His presence is acknowledgment, while denying their thanks for deliverance from Him is [their habit: transgression and blindness]. This is in utter contradiction to what they claim of soundness of intellect, genuineness of opinion, and sound natures. The sum is that a person, when afflicted, is not patient, and when given hope, is not thankful. It is as if it were said: when good touches humankind among them, he is heedless, with exultation, pride, and exuberance. ﴿And when harm touches the human being﴾ among them ﴿he calls upon Us﴾ sincerely, acknowledging Our right, knowing Our perfect greatness, acting accordingly, turning away from what he claimed as a partner to Us, ﴿lying on his side﴾, that is, reclining while wishing for rest. It seems he expressed it with the particle "li" (for/on) to indicate that this is the most intimate of his states toward Him. ﴿Or sitting﴾, that is, in a middle state [in his conditions]; ﴿or standing﴾, that is, in utmost striving (p-84) in his affairs, nothing preventing him from that in any state of the states [but rather the time of touching by harm is the time of calling for its removal]. It is also possible that he expressed the three states as stages of harm, and said "lying on his side" to indicate the entrenchment and dominance of harm, such that he cannot even sit, as one says, "so-and-so is in what afflicts him." He indicated by the particle "fa" (then) the nearness of the time of removal, saying: ﴿So when We removed﴾, that is, by Our greatness, ﴿from him his harm﴾ [that is] for which he called upon Us. ﴿He passes on﴾, that is, in all that he wills, heedless of Us in every respect, ﴿as if﴾, that is, as if he ﴿had not called Us﴾, that is, despite what he acknowledged at the time of calling of Our greatness. Since the one called upon comes to the caller and does what he was called for, He said: ﴿to﴾, that is, the removal of ﴿harm that touched him﴾, that is, as if he had no knowledge of Us at all, let alone acknowledging that We are the One who removed his harm from him. So this verse explains human weakness and the evil of his servitude, while the one before it explains God's power and the goodness of His lordship. Touching (massu) is meeting without intermediary. Calling (du'a') is requesting an act from one able to perform it. Harm (durr) is the imposition of pain by an act or by a cause leading to it.

Since this act of humankind is among the most wondrous of wonders, it was as if it were said: why does he do that? It was said: because of what is made attractive to him of matters by which gradual lure (istidraj) occurs for his excess (israf). This is always Our practice. ﴿Thus﴾, that is, like this great-ranked adornment; and since the one who adorns is unspecified, He framed the verb in the passive: ﴿it was made attractive to the excessive﴾ (p-85), that is, all of them, those immersed in this quality, ﴿what they used to do﴾, that is, by their natures, ﴿they were doing﴾, that is, they are attached to it in a manner of renewal and continuity, [namely] disobedience through unbelief and other things, despite its corruption being evident and its harm clear. Excess (israf) is the abundance of departing from justice.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 13:

Since their gaze was fixed on the worldly life, and this was clearly a matter of granting respite to the wrongdoers and showing kindness to the criminals, He followed it with His saying, the Exalted, threatening them and restraining them from what they were engaged in of following adornment, emphasizing because they deny that their destruction was on account of their wrongdoing: ﴿And We did destroy﴾, that is, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿the generations﴾, that is, despite the strength and power they had. Since those destroyed were the people of the uprooting punishment, some of those who came before, He affirmed the preposition, so He said: ﴿before you when they did wrong﴾, that is, their wrongdoing was complete, and the destruction encompassed their last and first alike, as one soul, to repel the assumption that He, glorified is He, does not bring general destruction. And He, the Exalted, said, coordinating with ﴿We destroyed﴾: ﴿and their messengers came to them﴾, that is, to every nation its messenger, ﴿with the clear proofs﴾, that is, those by which the message was made clear. ﴿And they were not﴾ (wa-ma), that is, while the state was that they ﴿were not﴾, that is, by their natures, ﴿to believe﴾. He emphasized the negation with a form that rejects that their faith would be delayed after the clarification, so He said: ﴿to believe﴾, even if every sign had come to them, as an admonition for one who may suppose that He, glorified is He, would show them the first signs of punishment or the signs they proposed, so that they would believe. Thus He, glorified is He, made clear that this would not be a cause of faith for one whose disbelief He had decreed; rather, their condition is the same in denial before the coming of the signs and after them, so that it would be a cause of their destruction. It is as if it were said: Is that specific to the past nations? It is said: Rather, ﴿thus﴾, that is, like that great recompense, ﴿We recompense the people﴾, that is, those who have strength to attempt what they wish, ﴿the criminals﴾, because the cause is persistence in crime, which is severing what should be joined; wherever it is found, its recompense is found. And destruction is causing one to fall into a punishment from which there is no escape; and "qarn" is the people of an age, because some of them are contemporaneous with others.

Since he had explicitly stated that this applies generally to every sinner, he followed it with His saying: ﴿Then We made you﴾, meaning, O messenger sent to them, the most honorable of Our messengers, ﴿successors in the earth﴾, meaning not specifically in the places where they were, and since our time did not encompass everything after the time of those who were destroyed, he introduced the preposition and said: ﴿after them﴾, meaning after the destroyed generations, destroyed with the destruction of uprooting. ﴿That We may see﴾, and We, with the greatness that is Ours, are more knowing of you than yourselves, and that is only so that We may see it in the world of witnessing, to establish the proof, ﴿how you will act﴾, so that Our seeing is connected to your deeds as existing, as a warning to the addressees lest they commit crimes and there befall them what befell those before them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 15:

Since it has already been established that whoever has been decreed wretched will not come to faith through any of the signs until His punishment descends upon him and He makes him taste His might and His vengeance, and since the Qur'an is the greatest sign sent down to mankind, as is well known, He followed this, by way of conjunction with His saying ﴿The disbelievers say, "Indeed, this is clearly a sorcerer"﴾ [Yunus: 2], with His saying, as an elaboration of that: ﴿And when Our verses are recited﴾. He made the verb passive to indicate their denial whenever any reciter recites. He expressed it in the present tense (p. 87) to indicate that they say this even if the recitation is repeated. ﴿to them﴾, that is, to these people. ﴿Our verses﴾, that is, with the greatness that belongs to them by their being attributed to Us. ﴿clear﴾. For, despite what it contains that obliges them to acknowledge its truth, they say about it what has no meaning except trickery and obstinacy. It is also permissible for this to be conjoined to ﴿Then We made you successors﴾ [Yunus: 14], and so on, and the shift to the third person indicates that they turn away because of their misuse of the succession. The relative clause with its complement in His saying ﴿Those who do not expect to meet Us say﴾ stands in the place of a pronoun, to draw attention to the fact that this attribute is the cause of their saying. Perhaps He expressed it by "expecting" as an encouragement for them, because expectation is the basis of their concern in seeking to hasten the good and to repel harm. It would therefore have been fitting for them to expect to meet Him, desiring what He has prepared for those who respond to Him. He alluded to fear by using the plural of majesty, so that this would be more inducing to them to turn towards Him. ﴿Bring﴾, that is, from yourself, ﴿a Qur'an﴾, that is, a speech that is collected and comprehensive of what you intend, ﴿other than this﴾ in its arrangement and meaning, ﴿or change it﴾, that is, with other words while the meanings remain. They knew that he (ﷺ) was like them in incapacity for that, but they intended that he would undertake the alteration out of eagerness to fulfil their demand, so that his claim would be nullified or he would be destroyed.

Since it was as if it had been said, "What then shall I say to them?", He said: ﴿Say: It is not for me﴾, that is, it is valid and conceivable in any way at all ﴿to﴾ me. Since changing it covers both of the two previous cases, He said: ﴿to change it﴾, and He said: ﴿of my own accord﴾, that is, from my own side or on my own initiative. (p. 88) This indicates a refutation of them in their denial of the alteration of what He sent down by way of abrogation (naskh) according to what is beneficial, just as He sent down its origin for the benefit of the servants, along with the abrogation of the earlier laws by it. Thus this definitively yields His saying: ﴿I only follow﴾, that is, with the utmost of my effort, ﴿what﴾. Since it was known that the One who reveals to him is God, He said: ﴿is revealed to me﴾, [that is] whether it is a substitute or an original. Then He gave the reason for that by His saying, emphasizing it in response to their denial of its content: ﴿Indeed I fear﴾, that is, by way of constant renewal and continuity, ﴿if I disobey my Lord﴾, that is, the One who is good to me, who brought me into being, who nurtures me and manages me, by doing other than what He has legislated for me, ﴿the punishment of a great day﴾. For I believe in it, not denying it nor doubting it, unlike others who speak nonsense without fearing its consequence on that Day. And if I fear it, along with keeping in mind the attribute of beneficence, this fear, then how would my fear be with keeping in mind the attribute of majesty?

[p. 89] When al-Biqa'i had completed what repelled their scheming in their slander, he followed it with his excuse (ﷺ) for conveying the message, in a manner that clearly indicates that it is the speech of Allah and that he recited it only by His permission. This cuts off their slander at its root and removes it entirely. So He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to them, teaching them that He, glory be to Him, either wills the act or wills its non-occurrence, and that there is no state of silence at all between these. ﴿If Allah had willed﴾, that is, He to whom belongs all greatness, ﴿that I would not recite it to you﴾, ﴿nor would He have made you know it through me﴾, that is, He, glory be to Him, would have made you know it by way of treatment (mu'alajah) through my tongue. Since the mention of this was made, he followed it with the cause that makes it known, and said: ﴿I had remained among you a lifetime﴾ [p. 89] Since his life did not extend over the whole period before it, he said: ﴿before it﴾, about forty years, without any of the two matters (reciting or making known) because Allah did not will either of them at that time. Then I brought you this Book, the most judicious, which comprises the realities of the science of principles ('ilm al-usul), the subtleties of the science of branches ('ilm al-furu'), the refinements of the science of ethics ('ilm al-akhlaq), and the secrets of the stories of the former peoples, in a eloquence of which you were unable, though you are the most eloquent and articulate of people, to produce the like of even one verse. Thereby the definitive knowledge, which is very evident, came about that it is from Allah. Therefore, on this basis, He made the denial of reason a consequence, and said: ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾, as an indication that it suffices, in knowing that the Qur'an is from Allah and that others are incapable of producing its like, that the one who considers his matter and my matter is a person of reason. That is, will you not have intellect, so that through it you would recognize the reality of the Qur'an by the proof that He has guided you to in this verse, the manifest evidence and the overpowering authority, which establishes that it is not valid for me in any way to alter it on my own account, because I am like you, and you know that you are incapable of that even when you band together. So I, alone, despite being unlettered, am incapable; and [I am incapable] also because He, exalted is He, had He willed, would not have conveyed it to you; and because I dwelt among you for a long time before bringing it, not reciting anything to you, not claiming any knowledge among you, and not frequenting any scholar. You would then know that the one who said what you said is a denier of the signs of Allah, and the one who does what you request is a liar against Allah, and each of these is the greatest injustice. ﴿Who then is more unjust﴾, that is, it is the cause for saying: who is ﴿more unjust than one who fabricates﴾, that is, who deliberately ﴿against Allah﴾, that is, He who possesses all greatness, ﴿a lie﴾, that is, any lie whatsoever. The original wording would have been "from me", on the assumption that this Qur'an is not from Allah as you claim; but this apparent wording was placed in its stead as a generalization and as attaching the ruling to the attribute. [p. 90] ﴿Or denies His signs﴾, as you have done, and that is among the greatest lies.

Since the implied meaning was: no one is more unjust than him, and therefore he will not prosper because he is a criminal, He explained this by saying, emphasized because of their denial: ﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed﴾, that is, in any way whatsoever. It has become clear [that] the intent is to negate lying from himself (ﷺ) and to attach the threat, since they denied the signs after it was established that they are from Allah, and by informing that no one is more unjust than they, because they lied against Allah in everything they attribute to Him that He has forbidden, and they denied His signs. Bringing something else may occur while the first remains, whereas substitution (tabdil) occurs only by removing the first and placing something else in its place. Al-Tilqa': the direction facing a thing. He followed it with his coming after it. Al-Mashi'ah (will), specifically, is a cause that leads to the occurrence of a thing, and is ordered toward it in a way in which its opposite could possibly occur; al-Iradah (volition) is similar to it. Al-'Aql (reason): the innate knowledge by which one can infer the absent from the present. It is permissible that ﴿and they worship﴾ [Yunus: 18] be a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to ﴿those who do not expect to meet Us﴾ [Yunus: 15], that is, they said that while worshipping ﴿besides Allah﴾ [Yunus: 18], that is, the Supreme King who possesses all the attributes of perfection, the one for whom it was established among them that this Qur'an is His speech, due to their inability to produce the like of any part of it, and He forbids them from worshipping other than Him, while they know His power to harm and to benefit.

[p. 89] When al-Biqa'i had completed what repelled their scheming in their slander, he followed it with his excuse (ﷺ) for conveying the message, in a manner that clearly indicates that it is the speech of Allah and that he recited it only by His permission. This cuts off their slander at its root and removes it entirely. So He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to them, teaching them that He, glory be to Him, either wills the act or wills its non-occurrence, and that there is no state of silence at all between these. ﴿If Allah had willed﴾, that is, He to whom belongs all greatness, ﴿that I would not recite it to you﴾, ﴿nor would He have made you know it through me﴾, that is, He, glory be to Him, would have made you know it by way of treatment (mu'alajah) through my tongue. Since the mention of this was made, he followed it with the cause that makes it known, and said: ﴿I had remained among you a lifetime﴾ [p. 89] Since his life did not extend over the whole period before it, he said: ﴿before it﴾, about forty years, without any of the two matters (reciting or making known) because Allah did not will either of them at that time. Then I brought you this Book, the most judicious, which comprises the realities of the science of principles ('ilm al-usul), the subtleties of the science of branches ('ilm al-furu'), the refinements of the science of ethics ('ilm al-akhlaq), and the secrets of the stories of the former peoples, in a eloquence of which you were unable, though you are the most eloquent and articulate of people, to produce the like of even one verse. Thereby the definitive knowledge, which is very evident, came about that it is from Allah. Therefore, on this basis, He made the denial of reason a consequence, and said: ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾, as an indication that it suffices, in knowing that the Qur'an is from Allah and that others are incapable of producing its like, that the one who considers his matter and my matter is a person of reason. That is, will you not have intellect, so that through it you would recognize the reality of the Qur'an by the proof that He has guided you to in this verse, the manifest evidence and the overpowering authority, which establishes that it is not valid for me in any way to alter it on my own account, because I am like you, and you know that you are incapable of that even when you band together. So I, alone, despite being unlettered, am incapable; and [I am incapable] also because He, exalted is He, had He willed, would not have conveyed it to you; and because I dwelt among you for a long time before bringing it, not reciting anything to you, not claiming any knowledge among you, and not frequenting any scholar. You would then know that the one who said what you said is a denier of the signs of Allah, and the one who does what you request is a liar against Allah, and each of these is the greatest injustice. ﴿Who then is more unjust﴾, that is, it is the cause for saying: who is ﴿more unjust than one who fabricates﴾, that is, who deliberately ﴿against Allah﴾, that is, He who possesses all greatness, ﴿a lie﴾, that is, any lie whatsoever. The original wording would have been "from me", on the assumption that this Qur'an is not from Allah as you claim; but this apparent wording was placed in its stead as a generalization and as attaching the ruling to the attribute. [p. 90] ﴿Or denies His signs﴾, as you have done, and that is among the greatest lies.

Since the implied meaning was: no one is more unjust than him, and therefore he will not prosper because he is a criminal, He explained this by saying, emphasized because of their denial: ﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed﴾, that is, in any way whatsoever. It has become clear [that] the intent is to negate lying from himself (ﷺ) and to attach the threat, since they denied the signs after it was established that they are from Allah, and by informing that no one is more unjust than they, because they lied against Allah in everything they attribute to Him that He has forbidden, and they denied His signs. Bringing something else may occur while the first remains, whereas substitution (tabdil) occurs only by removing the first and placing something else in its place. Al-Tilqa': the direction facing a thing. He followed it with his coming after it. Al-Mashi'ah (will), specifically, is a cause that leads to the occurrence of a thing, and is ordered toward it in a way in which its opposite could possibly occur; al-Iradah (volition) is similar to it. Al-'Aql (reason): the innate knowledge by which one can infer the absent from the present. It is permissible that ﴿and they worship﴾ [Yunus: 18] be a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to ﴿those who do not expect to meet Us﴾ [Yunus: 15], that is, they said that while worshipping ﴿besides Allah﴾ [Yunus: 18], that is, the Supreme King who possesses all the attributes of perfection, the one for whom it was established among them that this Qur'an is His speech, due to their inability to produce the like of any part of it, and He forbids them from worshipping other than Him, while they know His power to harm and to benefit.

(p-91) Since the context is one of threat and intimidation, he (Allah) placed harm first for this reason, and as a reminder to them that they are immersed in His blessings, over which no one else has the power to prevent anything. Therefore they should bind them with gratitude. So He said: ﴿What neither harms them﴾, i.e., at all, from the idols and others, ﴿nor benefits them﴾ in opposing the Qur'an by altering it or otherwise, nor in anything at all. It is the right of the one worshipped to reward obedience and punish disobedience; otherwise his worship would be in vain. [They are] turning away from the clear signs that have come to them [from] the One whom they know harms and benefits them, and that no one other than Him possesses any of that. He has established the proofs for this more than once. In this there is the utmost rebuke to them for rejecting reason, while they claim to be firmly rooted in it and to have a firm standing in it. And worship (ʿibadah) is submission of the heart in the highest degrees of submission. Then He marvelled at them with another marvel, saying: ﴿And they say﴾, i.e., their saying that once was not enough for them throughout time, so they renew their saying, persisting in it: ﴿These are our intercessors﴾, i.e., the idols or others, ﴿with Allah﴾, i.e., the Greatest King, from whose presence no one can draw near except by His permission. The refutation of what this claim contains has already passed in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿There is no intercessor except after His permission﴾ [Yunus: 3]. In this there is a humbling of them in their incapacity to alter the Qur'an or to produce anything like it, since their eloquence did not avail them in that, nor did their rhetoric suffice them at all, their eloquent ones failed them regarding its matter, and their intercessors went astray from them. This therefore clearly shows that there is no intercessor except after His permission (p-92), subsequently. It is as if He said: "How shall I answer them?" So He said: ﴿Say﴾, disapproving of this knowledge of theirs: ﴿Do you inform⁠﴾, i.e., do you tell with a great telling, ﴿Allah﴾, who is the Knower of everything, encompassing every perfection, ﴿of what He does not know﴾, i.e., of which there is no knowledge for Him at any time, ﴿in the heavens﴾. Since the situation required the utmost clarification, he repeated the negation explicitly, saying: ﴿nor on the earth﴾. In this there is a belittling of their minds of a kind that would humble inanimate matter, for they cannot criticize it in any way. Whatever is not known to Allah has no existence at all, so there is no more emphatic negation than this, just as when you exaggerate in denying something of yourself you say: "This is something Allah does not know of me."

When He, Exalted, had here explained what they were upon of feebleness of minds and weakness of opinions, He concluded this by declaring Himself free of it, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, i.e., He is exalted above every trace of deficiency, a transcendence that cannot be encompassed, ﴿and exalted is He﴾, i.e., He acted, with His encompassing of the attributes of perfection, the act of one who greatly exceeds in transcendence, ﴿above what they associate﴾, i.e., what they make as partners with Him.

When he had shown their evil in worshipping other than Allah, and concluded with His transcendence and perfection, he showed that this false religion is newly invented. He also showed His purity and perfection by explaining that people were at first united in obeying Him, and then they opposed His command. Yet He did not cut off His favour to them. He continued, in granting them respite despite their persistence in evil deeds, to carry out what had preceded in His knowledge (*'ilm*) and what His decree (*qada'*) had determined. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And mankind was not but one community﴾, i.e., all of them, despite the turmoil they had. ﴿Except a single community﴾. Since this implied their unity in purpose, he confirmed and emphasised it, saying: ﴿one﴾ [i.e.] upright (*ḥunafā'*), agreeing upon the obedience of Allah. ﴿But they differed﴾ concerning that during the time of Noah, peace be upon him, as narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, after their unity, because of the disorder they had. So their disbelievers deserved immediate punishment. ﴿And had it not been for a word﴾ i.e., a great word, ﴿that preceded﴾ i.e., in pre-eternity (*al-azal*), ﴿from your Lord﴾ i.e., the One who is good to you, through the mercy shown to your community by granting them respite. He clarified the emphasis with what indicates an oath, because of their denial that their delay was for this reason, so He said: ﴿it would have been decided between them﴾ i.e., swiftly, by the easiest matter, ﴿concerning that wherein they differ﴾ i.e., not concerning anything else, by hastening their recompense for it.

[Since the speech did not clarify the taking (of partners), which is the focus of the command that requires dealing with the inner state, it did not mention the pronoun, unlike in az-Zumar, so He said]: ﴿wherein they differ﴾.

This indicates that the matter to which they were called is not a newly arising matter, such that it would need to be held in suspense for examining its outcomes and reflecting on its sources and origins. Rather, with its evident proofs, the soundness of its methods, the correctness of its doctrines, and the submission of the natural disposition (*fitra*) to it, it is the original state the servants were upon. What they are in now is the newly arising innovation, with its corruption evident and its sickness clear. This refers to His saying: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people?﴾ [Yunus: 2], because His saying ﴿The disbelievers said, "Indeed, this is clearly a magician."﴾ [Yunus: 2] indicates that they are two groups: disbelievers and believers. The *ummah* is a group sharing one meaning and one character, as if they were heading (*taummu*), i.e., aiming at, one thing.

Then Allah the Exalted said, coordinating with His statement "and they worship" [Yunus: 18]: "and they say" — meaning: when the clear signs came to them, they said, "Bring a Qur'an other than this," disbelieving in the One who sent it down, worshipping besides Him what no intelligent person would be content to equate with Him, let alone worship [saying, out of their extreme obstinacy and persistence in rebellion]: "Why is it not" — that is, "why not," and "why does it not" — "a sign sent down to him" [meaning in any manner whatsoever] "from his Lord," that is, from the One who is good to him, other than what he has brought. This is either because they demanded a sign that would compel them to faith, or because they did not count what had been sent down to him among the signs, let alone regard it as clear proofs. Yet the Qur'an alone suffices as a sign that remains for all time, unique among the signs and subtle in its path among the miracles, while they are unable to produce its like, whether by alteration or otherwise. So what obstinacy could be greater than this?

Since this statement carried a tinge of interrogation, He said [as a consequence of their words]: "So say," restricting it in a true restriction: "The unseen belongs only" — that is, the unseen of which Jesus, peace be upon him, spoke in his words: "and I know not what is in Your soul" [al-Ma'idah: 116] — and it is that which no created being has ever been made aware of.

"To Allah," that is, to the One who alone has complete encompassing knowledge. I have no knowledge of the cause of the non-sending of what you desire, nor whether you will be answered in it or not.

Since He, glorified be He, specified the knowledge to Himself, and since the sending down of signs is among the possible matters, He made His statement a consequence of it: "So wait." Then He answered one who might ask Him, "What then are you doing?" with His statement: "Indeed, I am with you" — that is, in this matter, not opposing you in longing for a sign through which your guidance may be attained — "among those who wait," then He affirmed and emphasised the meaning, saying: "among those who wait," that is, for whatever sign or other thing may come upon me.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 21:

When their request was a stirring of the souls of the righteous toward hoping for the answer to their demand, Allah, glory be to Him, followed it with what makes clear that this is of no benefit to them, since it is pure obstinacy (ta'annut). So He, exalted is He, said, linking it to His saying ﴿And the disbelievers say, "Indeed, this is clear magic"﴾ [Yunus: 2], or to His saying ﴿And when harm touches mankind﴾ [Yunus: 12], making clear that His mercy is certain in existence and frequent in its arrival to them [making clear that they have a great sign from their own selves, with which they have no need for obstinacy in seeking a sign; and it indicates the intended result of the surah, which is the Oneness (tawhid), and that their association of partners is only due to the deficiency of their natural dispositions, which necessitates ingratitude for favour. That is because they, generally, when they are blessed with a favour, meet it with disbelief, making its time proportionate to the time of that favour, as indicated by the expression "when" (idha). Then, when harm touches them, it compels them to the Truth, and they become sincere, and their state in this never differs at all. This unanimity from both sides is a clear proof of both matters: disbelief is wrongdoing, in what it leads to of insolence; and Oneness is truth, in what it calls to of the upright natural disposition that is in the best of forms, which is not removed from it by the infliction of harm, by the appetites, passions and lethargy. This is as occurs in Surah al-Rum, which accords with this one in indicating Oneness. Therefore, in each of the two, He expressed it with "mankind" so that their unanimity would be a sufficient proof of it and a magnificent authority compelling to it. And Allah is the Guide.]: ﴿And when We let mankind taste mercy﴾, i.e., by what We have of greatness, ﴿mankind﴾, i.e., those who have the attribute of fluctuation, ﴿mercy﴾, i.e., a favour with which We showed mercy to them without their deserving it.

Since the existence of a favour does not occupy the whole time that follows a calamity, He brought in the preposition, saying: ﴿after adversity has touched them﴾, i.e., drought and other things, ﴿behold, they have a scheming against Our signs﴾, i.e., they quickly devise deception, which is the meaning of ﴿idha (behold)﴾; ﴿scheming﴾, i.e., great, through the sins they commit in secret, most of them acting as schemers do, ﴿against Our signs﴾, indicating that they are never free from His great signs. If they were benefiting from the signs, they would be guided by them. So when mercy comes to them after calamity, they do not count it as a sign indicating the One who sent it to them, because it breaks the habit they were in of calamity; yet they acknowledge that none can send it or remove the severity except Him, glory be to Him. Rather, they act in it as schemers do, by turning it away from that through various kinds of diversions, such as attributing it to causes, like the attribution of rain to the seasonal stars (anwa'), and the like, not fearing a repetition of the same adversity or something worse.

Since this sentence indicates their haste in scheming from three aspects—the expression "taste" (dhawq), which is the first contact; the particle "min" (from), which is for beginning; and the sudden "idha" (behold)—it was as if it were said: They hasten with all their effort in scheming. So it was said: ﴿Say, "Allah is swifter in scheming"﴾, i.e., He to whom belongs complete encompassment of everything. The description of Him with swiftness means that He decreed their punishment before their planning of their plots. [Abu Hayyan drew attention to this.] Since scheming is concealing a plot, He, glory be to Him, made clear to them that they are unable to scheme at all against Him, exalted is His majesty and sovereignty, because He knows the secret and what is more hidden; rather, they do not scheme any scheme except that His messengers, glory be to Him, are aware of it—so how about Him, glory be to Him! He, exalted is He, said, emphasizing to deny their claim: ﴿Indeed, Our messengers﴾, i.e., with what they have of greatness through their attribution to Us, ﴿record﴾, i.e., a continuous recording in the manner of continuity with the continuity of what is recorded, ﴿what you scheme﴾, because they were appointed over you before you were drops of semen, and they were appointed over you only after their appointer's knowledge of everything you do, and they do not record your scheme except after their being informed of it. As for Him, glory be to Him, when He decrees, His messengers cannot be informed of it except by His being informed of it, so how about others! When it is made clear that He knows their affairs while they are ignorant of His affairs, He knows that He will not leave them to plan a plot except that He has already prepared for Himself what will turn it back upon their own necks. Scheming (makr) is turning a thing away from its proper course by way of a stratagem in it; and swiftness (surr'a) is doing a thing at the time when it is most fitting for it. The verse has included an explanation of what the state of the ignorant requires: wasting the right of a favour, and scheming with it, even though its rank is great and it comes at a time of poverty toward it and intense need for its descent, along with a warning that the harm returns upon the schemer in it.

Then He, glorified is He, began to explain what makes evident the swiftness of His scheming, through an example that illustrates what the preceding verse mentioned: His transferring His servants from harm to blessing, and the speed with which they change. So He said: ﴿He is the One﴾, that is, none other than Him, ﴿who enables you to travel﴾ [that is], at every time in which you travel a great journey from which you cannot disengage, ﴿by land and sea﴾, that is, He causes for you the means that necessitate your travel in them, enables you to do so, and guides you, out of all the other animals, to what in them is of various kinds of benefit, while He is able to overtake you on land by sinking into the earth, and whatever is short of that, and at sea by drowning and the like.

Since ruin by the conditions of the sea is more apparent, although travel on it is among the greatest signs and clearest proofs, He mentioned it while turning away from mentioning the land. So He said: ﴿until, when you are in the ships﴾, that is, in a state from which there is no escape for you, ﴿the ships﴾, that is, the boats, which may be singular or plural. He turned away from them after addressing them directly, because of what will come. So He said: ﴿and they sail﴾, that is, the ships, ﴿with them﴾. When He mentioned their sailing while they were in them, He mentioned its cause, saying: ﴿with a favourable wind﴾. Then He made clear to them their lack of knowledge of the outcomes by His saying: ﴿and they rejoice in it﴾, that is, in that wind and in the ships sailing by it. ﴿There comes to it a violent wind﴾, which unsettles their ships and distresses them. ﴿And the waves come upon them﴾, that is, the waves known to everyone by sight or description, ﴿from every place﴾, that is, from every place from which they are customarily expected to come, so that it terrifies their hearts. ﴿And they think that they are encompassed﴾. Since what is feared is destruction, not its coming from a specific source, the verb was put in the passive form, which is a metaphor for it, because when an enemy surrounds his enemy, the latter is certain of destruction. So He said: ﴿they are encompassed﴾.

Since what preceded of their strange condition, which makes hearts tremble and powers weaken, required that one ask what they would do at that moment, the discourse came in accordance with the requirement of this question, reporting their abandoning obstinacy and their sincerity, which indicates their anxiety at His assaults and the dissolving of their resolve while witnessing His blows. The phrase of al-Rummani (ʿAbd Allah al-Rummānī): the connection of the answers' claim, as if it was said: when they thought that they were encompassed, ﴿they called upon God﴾, that is, the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, with desire for Him for deliverance and worship of Him with sincerity, ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾, that is, free from every association, ﴿to Him the religion﴾, that is, the tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) and the affirmation with outward and inward sincerity. The verse has included an explanation of what the immediate reason of the intellect requires of fear in severity, turning to the Bestower of safety and the Lavisher of blessing, to remove that calamity. Then, glorified is He, followed that with a narration of their condition in their promise to give thanks for deliverance, and then their lying in that, despite their claim that they are the most clear of the people's garments from lying, the most disdaining of it, and the furthest of people from ingratitude for kindness. So He, exalted is He, said, relating their statement, by whose emphasis they showed that they said it with utmost desire, denying what is supposed of them regarding returning to what they were in before that state of disbelief: ﴿If You deliver us﴾, that is, O King, to whom no sovereignty belongs but His, ﴿from this﴾, that is, this grievous calamity, ﴿we will surely be﴾, that is, in a state we will never leave, ﴿among the thankful﴾, that is, those who constantly persist in thanking You, and are firmly established in being characterised by it.

[p. 100] When He, glorified is He, informed them that they had confirmed this promise with such emphasis, He followed it with a statement that they hastened to break it with the utmost haste, saying: ﴿So when He delivered them﴾. Since the particle *fa'* (الفاء, the connective "then/so") indicates haste in breaking the promise, He emphasized their whisper of rebellion with His words: ﴿behold, they commit injustice﴾, i.e., they exceed the limits, ﴿in the earth﴾, i.e., its kind, ﴿without right﴾, i.e., without complete right. The transgressor remains blameworthy until he stands upon complete right, one in which there is no falsehood in any respect.

The address first came in ﴿He makes you travel﴾ [Yunus: 22] so that it would include the believers, because *al-tasyir* (التسيير, causing to move) is suitable for an expression of favor. Then He turned to the third person (al-ghaybah) when there appeared what does not befit them. Abu Hayyan noted this shift. A better explanation than his is that He, glorified is He, turned toward them to indicate that by the faculties He had prepared in them He had made them fit to be addressed, then turned away from them as a sign that they deserved to be turned away from, because of their turning away, deluded by the good wind that had been granted them, in a situation where one must turn to Him and be independent of everything else, because of the greatness of the danger and the severity of the matter. It is as if He is mentioning to others their condition, which pleases Him, in order to disapprove of them and to make their condition appear ugly.

*Al-tasyir* (التسيير) is causing movement in a direction that extends, like travel. *Al-barr* (البر) is the wide land that is crossed from one city, and from it comes *al-barr* (goodness), because of the breadth of good in it. *Al-bahr* (البحر) is the place where wide water rests, such that its two shores cannot be seen from its midst. *Al-fulk* (الفلك) are the ships that move on the water; its root is turning, whence comes *falakat al-mighzal* (the whorl of a spindle), and *al-falak* (the celestial sphere) in which the stars revolve. *Al-najah* (النجاة) is deliverance from destruction. *Al-baghy* (البغي) is the intention of domination through oppression; its root meaning is seeking. *Al-haqq* (الحق) is placing a thing in its proper place as the intellect calls for.

[p. 101] Then He explained that what they are in, of respite, is only the enjoyment of the worldly life and that it is an abode of passing away. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O mankind﴾, i.e., those among whom the state of disorder has prevailed. ﴿Your rebellion is only﴾, i.e., every rebellion that comes from you, ﴿against yourselves﴾, because its harm returns only upon them, and that, even if you benefit from it, is a passing accident, ﴿a fleeting enjoyment of the life of this world﴾. Then its shame and disgrace remain after death. ﴿Then to Us is your return﴾, i.e., exclusively, ﴿after resurrection﴾. ﴿Then We will inform you﴾, according to our greatness, of a mighty informing, ﴿about what you used to do﴾, i.e., a state that became like a disposition, ﴿and We will recompense you for it﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 24:

Since the context is for establishing the resurrection (al-ba'th) and warning them with it, and they denied it and believed that the world endures, and that it is only wombs that expel and earth that receives, always without ending [so it is an abode in which one is content and feels at ease], and for the warning against rebellion (al-baghy) and seeking strength through what is not right, and since parables are clearer for resolving difficulties, He, exalted is He, said, presenting an example of its enjoyment, restricting its matter to extinction, as a refutation of them in their belief in its permanence without resurrection: ﴿Indeed﴾ [this is a restriction of reversal (qasr qalb)] ﴿the example of the worldly life﴾ in which you compete, in the swiftness of its ending and the vanishing of its bounty after its great approach, ﴿is like water that We sent down﴾ [i.e.] with what We have of greatness, [and He confirmed its matter and clarified it by His saying]: ﴿from the sky﴾, so He likened it to the matter of plants, and that it is little, reaching its limit, so the earth becomes barren after that greening and lushness. In that is an indication of the resurrection, and that He, exalted is He, is able to strike it before its end or after it (p-102) with some calamities, as occurs in some years, so they become destitute of it and in need of it. In that is a great warning. ﴿Then there mingles﴾ i.e. because of Our sending it down ﴿with it﴾ i.e. because of its softness and fineness ﴿the vegetation of the earth﴾ generally, in its belly ﴿of that which men eat﴾ i.e. all of them ﴿and livestock﴾ of grains, fruits and herbs, so it appears on its surface ﴿until﴾ and it continues to grow thus, increasing in beauty and bulk. Since abundance is the origin, he expressed it with the particle of confirmation, so he said: ﴿when﴾. Since the splendor of plants follows abundance, and the water is as if it gives it to them and they take it, He said: ﴿the earth takes its adornment﴾ [i.e.] that which has the capacity for plants ﴿and becomes beautified﴾ with kinds of those plants, an adornment, some of it evident and some of it hidden, by what the assimilation (idgham) conveys ﴿and its people think﴾ i.e. a very emphatic thought, by what the turning away from "their power" to ﴿that they are able﴾ i.e. their ability is established ﴿over it﴾ by gathering the fruit from that vegetation, and the knowledge of the outcome was absent from them because of their ignorance. When that was so, ﴿Our command came to it﴾ [i.e.] which is not turned back, of excessive cold or heat ﴿by night or by day, so We made it﴾ i.e. its crop and its adornment, with its greatness, because of that command and its consequence of destruction ﴿as a harvest﴾, and he expressed by what the form fa'il conveys of intensity and permanence with his saying: ﴿as though﴾ i.e. as though it ﴿had not flourished﴾ i.e. it had not been flourishing, i.e. being pleasing, beautiful, rich, possessing abundance, desired, something wanted, i.e. its crop and its adornment ﴿yesterday﴾, so the state of the world in the swiftness of its ending and the vanishing of its bounty after its great approach was like the state of the plants of the earth in its drying up and its going away as debris, after it had covered and adorned the earth with its greenness, its colors and its splendor.

Since this parable is in the utmost correspondence to the Hour, it shook the listener, so his wonder increased at the beauty of its detailing after its rooting, and it was said in reply to him: ﴿Thus﴾ i.e. like this remarkable detailing ﴿We detail﴾ i.e. a great detailing ﴿the signs for a people﴾ i.e. people who are strong, having the strength of striving for what they want ﴿who reflect﴾ i.e. they renew thought in a manner of continuity and intensity; and the parable (mathal): a widely circulated saying in which the second state is likened to the first; and the intermingling (ikhtilat): the mixing of things with one another; and the zukhruf (adornment): the beauty of colors.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verses 25–26:

When He (glorified is He) had established these verses in which He warned against the various kinds of calamities, He made clear that the abode to which they are content and at rest, the house of afflictions and the source of destructions and ruins, and that it is a passing shade, as a warning against it and a repulsion from it, He (exalted is He) made clear that the abode to which He invites is safe from every fatigue, grief and ailment, and is established without end. So He said, exalted is He, connecting it to His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [Yunus: 3], as an encouragement toward the Hereafter and an exhortation to it: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belong majesty and honor, ﴿invites﴾, that is, He attaches His calling, in a manner of renewal and continuity, to those who are called, ﴿to the Abode of Peace﴾. From Qatadah: He (glorified is He) attributed it to His own name, magnifying it and encouraging toward it, meaning that there is no harm in it at all, and safety in it is everlasting, and greeting (al-salam) is widespread in it among them one to another and from the angels and others. And the du'a' (invitation/supplication) is the request for an act by that which occurs on account of it; and the incentives toward the act are the opposite of the deterrents from it.

When He informed, through the calling, of guidance through clarification, and the ending of the verse, with His saying: ﴿and guides whom He wills﴾, that is, by what He creates in his heart of guidance, ﴿to a straight path﴾, made understood that among people are those whom He guides and among them those whom He misguides, and that all are doers of what He wills, it was fitting to say: Are they one in their recompense as they are one in submission to His will? It is said: No, rather they are two groups: ﴿For those who did good﴾, that is, the deeds in this world, among them those whom He guided, ﴿is the best (al-husna)﴾, that is, the quality that is at the utmost of goodness of reward, ﴿and an increase﴾ [that is, a great one] from the bounty of Allah. So people are: one who desires, whose guidance proceeded from striving, ﴿And those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69]; and one who is desired, whose guidance proceeded from will. So the invitation to Paradise through clarification is general, and the guidance to the path is specific, because it is the way to the Benefactor.

When bliss is not complete except by permanence and security from harms, He said: ﴿And there will not cover their faces any dust (qatar)﴾, that is, it overtakes and reaches them, ﴿nor humiliation﴾, that is, dejection and gloom which shows humbling and abasement.

When this was clear in that they are the people of happiness, He followed it with His saying:
﴿Those are the companions of Paradise﴾, that is, the exalted in rank. And since companionship is worthy of constancy, He stated it in His saying: ﴿They therein﴾, that is, none other than them, ﴿abide eternally﴾, that is, remaining, not departing, because they do not desire otherwise for its goodness, and it is not desired for them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verses 25–26:

When He (glorified is He) had established these verses in which He warned against the various kinds of calamities, He made clear that the abode to which they are content and at rest, the house of afflictions and the source of destructions and ruins, and that it is a passing shade, as a warning against it and a repulsion from it, He (exalted is He) made clear that the abode to which He invites is safe from every fatigue, grief and ailment, and is established without end.
