It is said: No, rather they are two groups: ﴿For those who did good﴾, that is, the deeds in this world, among them those whom He guided, ﴿is the best (al-husna)﴾, that is, the quality that is at the utmost of goodness of reward, ﴿and an increase﴾ [that is, a great one] from the bounty of Allah. So people are: one who desires, whose guidance proceeded from striving, ﴿And those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 69]; and one who is desired, whose guidance proceeded from will. So the invitation to Paradise through clarification is general, and the guidance to the path is specific, because it is the way to the Benefactor.

When bliss is not complete except by permanence and security from harms, He said: ﴿And there will not cover their faces any dust (qatar)﴾, that is, it overtakes and reaches them, ﴿nor humiliation﴾, that is, dejection and gloom which shows humbling and abasement.

When this was clear in that they are the people of happiness, He followed it with His saying:
﴿Those are the companions of Paradise﴾, that is, the exalted in rank. And since companionship is worthy of constancy, He stated it in His saying: ﴿They therein﴾, that is, none other than them, ﴿abide eternally﴾, that is, remaining, not departing, because they do not desire otherwise for its goodness, and it is not desired for them.

And when he (God) explained the state of excellence (al-fadl) regarding those who did good, He explained the state of justice regarding those who did evil, saying: ﴿And those who earned evil deeds﴾, meaning from among them, ﴿evil deeds﴾, meaning those that encompass them, ﴿the recompense of an evil deed is its like﴾, meaning from among them, ﴿by its like﴾, by the justice of God without any increase, ﴿and humiliation will cover them﴾, meaning as part of their recompense. It is as if it were said: Is there no escape for them from this? So the answer came: ﴿They have no protector from God﴾, meaning from the Supreme King, and he went to the extreme in negation, saying: ﴿from any protector﴾, meaning one who would prevent them from anything He wills for them.

Since it is well known that this changes their conditions, he connected to it His saying: ﴿as if﴾. Since the disliked matter is the absolute state of their faces being in a wretched appearance, His saying ﴿their faces were covered﴾ is in the passive form, meaning: something covering them has covered them, because of the intensity of their blackness and the evil they are in, ﴿in pieces﴾. Since the word qita' (قِطَعًا), on the pattern of ʿinab, is shared between the darkness of the last part of the night and the plural of qit'a (piece) of a thing, he clarified and emphasized it, saying: ﴿of the night﴾, meaning of this kind, in the state of being ﴿dark﴾. Since this is evident that they are the people of wretchedness, he connected to it His saying: ﴿Those﴾, meaning the far-removed and the hateful, ﴿are the companions of the Fire﴾. And since companionship implies constant attachment, He explained it by His saying: ﴿They will abide therein forever﴾, meaning they will not be permitted to leave it.

Ar-rahaq (الرَّهَقُ): the overtaking of a matter; from it comes rahiqa al-ghulam (راهَقَ الغُلامُ), meaning when a boy reaches the state of men. Al-qatar (القَتَرُ): dust; from it comes al-iqtar (الإقْتارُ) in spending, meaning its scarcity. Adh-dhillah (الذِّلَّةُ): the smallness of the self through humiliation. Al-kasb (الكَسْبُ), meaning acquisition (a technical term in theology and exegesis): the action taken to bring benefit to the self or to ward off harm.

When He, glorified is He, had made clear the end of the two groups, He drew attention to some of the preliminaries that prevent anyone from interceding without His permission, by His saying: ﴿And [mention] the Day﴾, meaning: and We will separate them, because there are no kinship ties there and no means of connection, so there is no helping one another. [mention] the Day ﴿We gather them﴾, that is, the two groups: the saved and the destroyed, the worshippers among them and those they worshipped, ﴿all together﴾. Then the bond between the polytheists and their associates will be severed, so that nothing they believe in as intercession will intercede for them, and nothing will benefit them. Rather, they will show enmity and openly declare hostility. In this he has in view His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who originates creation, then repeats it﴾ [Yunus: 4], and His saying: ﴿They worship, besides God, what neither harms them nor benefits them﴾ [Yunus: 18]. Al-hashr (gathering) is the assembling by compulsion from every direction to one place of standing. He, glorified is He, indicated the length of their standing by His saying: ﴿Then We will say to those who associated [others with God]﴾, that is, by Us, [We say] to whoever did not share in creating them. And His saying: ﴿Stay in your place﴾. Abu Hayyan transmitted from the grammarians (al-nahwiyyun) that they made it a noun (ism, noun) meaning "remain!", and he refuted al-Zamakhshari's estimation of it as "keep to" (alzamu), because it is transitive, and the noun and the named (musamma) must be equal in transitivity and intransitivity. That is, We say to them: "Stand, the standing of abasement," ﴿you and your associates﴾, until Our command is carried out upon you, as a demonstration of the weakness of the deities they used to hope in, and as a humiliation for them, so they cannot oppose that.

Since the estimate was: "So they stood, in compliance with the command, according to the will," He conjoined to it, as a consequence of it, His saying: ﴿Then We separated﴾, that is, We removed, with a great and divided removal, what was ﴿between them﴾ in the world of connection and affection, until it became enmity and aversion. The disbelievers will say: "Our Lord, these are the ones who led us astray, and we used to call upon [others] besides You." ﴿And their associates will say﴾ to them, disowning them, by the speech that He, glorified is He, created for them: ﴿You were not﴾, that is, O polytheists, and He attributed the associates to them because they are the ones who set them up without command or proof, and because they assigned to them a share of their wealth. ﴿You used to worship us﴾, that is, you singled us out for worship, because we do not deserve that. This is an indication that only one who deserves sincere devotion in that should be worshipped, by being worshipped alone without partner. Whoever does not deserve that does not deserve worship at all and is not fit for it. Every act of worship that contains association is not counted as worship at all, and an inanimate object would not accept it even if it could speak. So when what is restricted by sincerity is negated, the absolute is negated too, because it is not counted at all. It is known that what has this description is not presented to anyone. So we think that no worshipper has worshipped us, let alone singled us out for that. A person may deny what he thinks is to be denied, and we did not know anything of that.

When they denied that, they followed it with a clause that states its cause, saying: ﴿So Allah suffices as a witness﴾, that is, the One whose knowledge and power encompass all things, ﴿as a witness﴾, meaning: He is sufficient for us, with a great sufficiency, as a witness who is not absent in any respect and not partial at all, ﴿between us and you﴾ concerning this matter. He testifies for us and against us. Then they began a new statement that confirms their denial, saying, emphatically, because they believed in their own knowledge: ﴿Indeed, we were﴾, that is, we were, in a state that is our innate nature, ﴿unaware of your worship﴾, whether it was directed at us or at others, whether sincere or mixed. Since ''inna'' here is the lightened form of the heavy ''inna'', it is preceded by the ''lam'' of distinction (al-lam al-fariqah), which distinguishes it from the negating ''in'', so it is said: ﴿unaware﴾ (ghafilin), because we have no spirits within us. We were therefore not in a position to command the worship or to approve of it, so the blame is upon you, not us. This is a disavowal from a position of humiliation. Alternatively, when they imagined in the partners attributes for which they worshipped them, and those partners were devoid of those attributes, the negation is valid, because they worshipped entities described by attributes that have no existence in reality. Also, they worshipped only the devils, who used to adorn that for them and mislead them. The implied sense, as the context indicates, is: ﴿Then We separated them﴾ [Yunus 28], that is, We prevented them from what they were engaged in of mutual association and affection, which required mutual support in worshipping idols. Then the polytheists said to their partners, when their help was delayed from them: "Indeed, we used to worship you besides Allah, so relieve us as we used to defend you and support your religion." ﴿And their partners will say: You did not used to worship us﴾ [Yunus 28], that is, it was revealed to us today, through Allah's enlightenment, that the matter is not as you claimed, and that you did not single us out for worship, such that we would be obligated to prevent you. Moreover, even if you had singled us out, we would not have been able to do that, as the Devil said: ﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me﴾ [Ibrahim 22]. ﴿So Allah suffices﴾, that is, as a consequence of our negation of that, in light of the knowledge revealed to us, we say: sufficient is ﴿Allah as a witness between us and you﴾ in this matter, He who testifies that you did not single out any one of Him or of us for worship, but rather you were wavering. All of this points to the fact that worship mixed with other things is not counted, and that a lifeless object would not approve of it even if it could speak. And whoever deserves worship deserves sincerity in it and that none be associated with Him. And none deserves that except the One capable of removing distress and of preventing anyone from severing the bond between Him and His worshipper and devotee. Since the purpose of a witness is to preserve what the two parties to a testimony might forget, they gave as the reason for their contentment with the testimony of Allah their saying: ﴿Indeed, we were unaware of your worship﴾ in those times, ﴿unaware﴾. Thus they acknowledged what is true, which everyone with sound reflection knows: that they had not been aware of their own worship for a moment of time before this moment. Therefore they are the most deserving of all creation of being content with the testimony of the Witness, because they are in a worse state than one who knows what is attested to and fears forgetting it. Or it may be said: the polytheists said to their partners, "Indeed, we used to worship you; so will you help us, or intercede for us, and save us from what we have fallen into?" ﴿And their partners will say: You did not used to worship us﴾ [Yunus 28] (p. 110), that is, alone. ﴿You used to worship﴾ [Yunus 28], that is, you did not devote the worship to us sincerely such that we would be obligated to devote you (to Allah). As our Lord and your Lord, who encompasses all things in knowledge, has informed us of this. ﴿So Allah suffices﴾, that is, as a consequence of that, He suffices ﴿as a witness between us and you﴾ concerning this. It is as if the polytheists said: "Your speech has implied that we worshipped you not in the manner of sincerity. Did we not then worship you? Will you not then avail us anything?" The partners answered with their saying: ﴿Indeed, we were unaware of your worship﴾, whether it was sincere or mixed, ﴿unaware﴾. So we do not acknowledge to you any worship at all, even if we were certain of its sincerity, because knowledge has been removed from us, given our state of inanimate matter, let alone that we would command you or approve of your worship, on the basis that we have no ability to help under any circumstance. Or it may be said, and this is better than what came before: ﴿And their partners will say﴾ [Yunus 28], when they became certain of the punishment, seeking that it be lightened for them by distributing it upon them and upon everyone else they had worshipped: ﴿You did not used to worship us﴾ [Yunus 28], O worshippers of us, ﴿us﴾ [Yunus 28], that is, exclusively ﴿you used to worship﴾ [Yunus 28]; rather you also used to worship others besides us. This, by Allah, encompasses every person whom someone else makes a show of by his deed while knowing that he is making a show of it, and that other person approves of it and does not deny it to him. Since they conveyed through the negation of worship restricted by exclusivity that they used to worship others along with them, and since a created being has limited knowledge and does not encompass in any respect the states of its own self, how then could they worship with the states of others? They therefore based on that their saying: ﴿So Allah suffices as a witness between us and you that﴾, that is, concerning the fact that ﴿we were﴾, that is, in general, ﴿unaware of your worship﴾. The summary is that this is a rendering of the speech of the disbelievers. It arises from them out of pure overwhelming, bewilderment, extreme grief, regret and anxiety (p. 111). It is not required that its meaning be in the most correct form and the most eloquent path; the miraculous quality lies in its composition. Their aim by it was that the punishment be lightened for them, even by sharing it with those they used to worship along with them. This belongs to the same category as the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿So will you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?﴾ [Ibrahim 21], ﴿So will you avail us a portion of the Fire?﴾ [Ghafir 47], ﴿So give them a double punishment of the Fire﴾ [Al-A'raf 38], and similar to it: ﴿Then you have no superiority over us, so taste the punishment﴾ [Al-A'raf 39]. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 30:

When he had informed about the state of the polytheists, the soul became eager to learn about the state of others, so he said, beginning a new statement and informing about both groups: ﴿There, every soul will be tested for what it sent before﴾. That is: in that station, in that place and time of great terrors, with its continuous tremors, ﴿every soul will be tested﴾, that is, it will be informed and will be dealt with in a manner that makes it know and reveals, ﴿obedient and disobedient alike﴾, ﴿for what it sent before﴾, that is, what deeds it had put forward, so that it will know whether they were good or bad, and whether [they] led to happiness or misery.

Since the bare term "return" (radd), which means turning a thing back to the place from which it began, is sufficient to instill awe in one who has understanding, he used the passive form in his saying: ﴿And they will be returned﴾, that is, by resurrection, by being brought back to life as they were at first, ﴿to God, their true Master (mawlahum al-haqq)﴾, that is, the greatest King. So they will have no ability to intend other than Him or to turn to anyone else among those falsehoods. Rather, their hope will be cut off from everything they used to invoke ﴿in the world﴾ (p-112), and this is what is meant by his saying: ﴿And what they used to fabricate will vanish from them﴾, that is, it will be nullified, will go away, and will be lost, ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾, that is, the state that was their natural disposition of deliberately lying that their objects of worship were partners. And in that station they will be certain that their turning to other than God was false and not true. Al-tazyil means separation by which each thing is removed from its place, and it is from the separation of corpses; it is not from the waw-root but from the ya'-root; one says: "I removed him from the thing (ziltuhu 'an al-shay' uzīluhu)" when you separate him from it. Al-kifaya means reaching the measure of need in repelling harm or obtaining benefit. Al-isläf means putting one matter forward before what follows it. Al-radd means going back to a thing after having departed from it, like al-raj'. Al-mawla is one who has the authority to manage the affairs of his mawla.

Commentary of al-Biqāʿī (Naẓm al-Durar) on Sūrah 10, verse 31:

When He, glory be to Him, had first established that their associates are things that are lorded over and subjugated, having no power except what Allah empowers them to have, and that He alone is the true Master (al-Mawlā al-Ḥaqq), and by this their disgrace became evident, He followed it with mention of the proofs against the corruption of their doctrine. He rebuked them by putting the question to them about matters they acknowledge belong exclusively to Him, and which definitively indicate His sole control over the whole affair, which necessitates, without any pause, the belief in His sole divinity (ilāhiyya). So He said: ﴿Say﴾ [i.e., O the most noble of our creation and the most gentle of them toward the servants] ﴿Who provides for you﴾ [i.e., brings you good things] O you who deny the Resurrection and claim partners for Allah, ﴿from the heaven﴾ [i.e.] with rain and other benefits, ﴿and the earth﴾ with plants and other things, ﴿so that you may live.﴾ ﴿Or who controls hearing﴾ [i.e.] by which you hear the signs, and He made it singular because it is generally shared equally, ﴿and sight﴾ by which you see, with what He has bestowed upon you in creating them, then in preserving them over long periods despite the abundance of afflictions, so that He pours them upon you, that your sensory life (ḥissiyya) may be completed through the continuance of the spirit, and your intellectual life (maʿnawiyya) through the existence of knowledge. ﴿Those are the ones you see with.﴾

It is reported from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Glory be to the One who gave sight through fat, hearing through bone, and speech through flesh."

When He asked them about what is clearest and closest to them in their own situation, He alerted them to what precedes it from the beginning of creation, saying: ﴿And who brings forth the living﴾ from animals and plants, ﴿from the dead﴾ i.e., from the sperm-drop and the like, ﴿and brings forth the dead﴾ i.e., [from] the sperm-drop and the like, which does not grow, ﴿from the living﴾ [i.e., so that it is transferred from deficiency to perfection]. Then He generalized, saying: ﴿And who arranges the affair﴾ i.e., all of it, with general management (tadbīr).

Since they acknowledged provision and what accompanies it of creation and management, He informed about their answer if they were asked about it, by His saying: ﴿They will say, "Allah."﴾ i.e., the named One to whom belongs all perfection through life and self-subsistence (qayyūmiyya), unlike what will come later concerning return and guidance. ﴿So say﴾ i.e., as a consequence of that, We say to you: say to them, as a consequence of this answer of theirs, this denunciation against them for lacking taqwā: ﴿Will you not then fear Allah?﴾ i.e., will you not make a shield between yourselves and His punishment, despite your acknowledgment of His oneness in lordship (rubūbiyya) and your associating others with Him in divinity (ilāhiyya)?

Then he gave a reason for the denunciation of their not being God-fearing, with his saying: ﴿Then that is God﴾, i.e., the one of great station, ﴿your Lord﴾, i.e., the one who brings you into existence and manages your affairs, to whom none of you has any benefaction besides Him, ﴿the Truth﴾, i.e., whose lordship is established with a firmness that admits no doubt [because the attributes mentioned previously are gathered in Him and not in any other, for lordship is not truly realized in one in whom those attributes are not gathered]. ﴿Then what﴾, i.e., so it follows from that that it is said to you: what is there ﴿after the truth﴾, i.e., He for whom is the most perfect establishment, ﴿except error﴾; for there is no intermediary between the two, as indicated by the omission of the preposition. No rational person turns away from the truth toward error, so how ﴿are you turned away﴾? That is, how, and from what direction, are you ﴿turned away﴾, i.e., from whatever turner, whatever it may be, from the truth toward error? For this reason he made his saying ﴿how﴾ follow from this: ﴿how﴾, i.e., how, and from what direction, ﴿are you turned away﴾ [i.e.] you, by any turner whatsoever, from the truth toward error.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 33:

When they were worthy, at the affirmation of this verse and their acknowledgment of its content, by saying: "We have submitted, so we have submitted, and we will never turn away from the truth," but they did not say it, they were deserving that it be said to them: "The word of Allah has come due against you for your wickedness and your deviation from the truth." It was asked: "Were they singled out for this?" It was answered: "No, rather ﴿Thus﴾, that is, like that great judgment, ﴿the word of your Lord has come due﴾, that is, of Him who does good to you by destroying your enemies: the single, effective word in which there is no hesitation. The plural sense in the reading of Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir is that no part of His words contradicts the word that made their punishment obligatory, rather all of them agree with it, so the intended meaning is one. Or this may be a metaphor (kinayah) for the fact that their punishment is perpetual, for His words do not take effect ﴿upon﴾ every ﴿of those who﴾ did as they did, because ﴿they transgressed﴾, that is: they committed abandonment of Allah's command, brought about His disobedience, did the going out from the path of truth, and the going out from the circle of righteousness, [which is their being one community upon the religion of their father Adam, the chosen one of Allah, peace be upon him]; (p-115) Then he gave the reason for that judgment in his words: ﴿that they do not believe﴾, that is: no faith will ever renew from them at all. [He expressed it by "transgression," meaning disbelief, because the context concerns going out from the circle of the true religion in His words: ﴿And mankind was not but one community, then they differed﴾ [Yunus: 19], and this meaning is more deserving of being expressed by fisq (transgression), whose root meaning is going out from an enclosure, as in their saying: "The date fasaqat from its skin," i.e., it came out]. Or the meaning is: lordship has become due to Him, glorified is He, by this order, namely the doing of these matters, which are concluded with the governance that necessitates His oneness, [glorified is He], definitively, for if there were a capable one who equaled Him in what He can do, it would be possible for him to oppose Him, and his being capable would be nullified; and it is due that whoever turns away from the truth is in misguidance, just as this is due. ﴿Thus has become due﴾ [that is, it was established with great establishment] ﴿the word of your Lord upon﴾ every ﴿of those who﴾ He decreed their transgression from among them. [And] ﴿that they do not believe﴾ is an explanation of His word that became due; and "al-rizq" is making the flowing gift.

When it became known that they acknowledge the matter of guidance and what follows from it of provision and governance, He (glorified is He) repeated the question about these, joined with the return (of creation), as a reminder to them of what they commonly recognize: that bringing back is easier. Denying it despite this is either obstinacy or stubborn opposition, and denying all the established matters is like this. Putting it in the form of a question is more forceful and has a greater effect on the heart. So He said: ﴿Say﴾ [i.e.] as a rebuke and reproach directed at them (p-116), ﴿Is there any of your associates﴾ [i.e.] those whom you claimed to be partners to Me, and whom you associated with Me in your wealth, in your livestock and your crops, ﴿who originates creation﴾ as I originated it, so that what you claim of partnership might be valid for them, ﴿then brings it back﴾.

Since the answer was certain and without hesitation, that none of them does any of that, and since their stubbornness in denying the return and their opposition would not leave them to answer with the truth, He commanded him to answer them by saying: ﴿Say, "Allah"﴾, that is, the One to whom all command belongs, ﴿originates creation﴾, that is, whenever He wills, ﴿then brings it back﴾. Here He used both parts of the question, and likewise what comes in the question about guidance, for emphasis on the matter, unlike what they had acknowledged, for He sufficed there with one of the two parts in His saying: ﴿They will say, "Allah"﴾ [Yunus: 31], and did not say, "He provides for us," and so on to the end. Then He increased their reproach for not submitting to this by expressing amazement at them in His saying: ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾, that is, how, and from what direction, are you turned away, with the vilest of lies, from the way of what is right, from any turner, when all directions have been made clear? He arranged these sentences in the finest order, for He first asked them about the cause of the continuation and completeness of their lives through provision, hearing, and sight, and about the beginning of creation in bringing the living out of the dead and what follows it. All of this was a reminder to reflect on the states of their own selves, arranged in order from the most evident to the more evident [then the more evident.

Then, when they had acknowledged all of this, He repeated the question about the beginning of creation, so as to join to it the return (to life). This was a reminder that both are, with respect to His power, on equal footing. When He had finished with what pertains to the states of the body, He commanded him to ask them about the purpose of that and what was intended by it, namely the states of the soul in the guidance which is the cause of happiness, pursuing the proof from the created thing to the Creator in a manner that points to its superiority. So He said: ﴿Say﴾ [i.e., O most discerning of the servants and most knowing of the One worshipped]. ﴿Is there any of your partners﴾ meaning those you claimed to be partners of God, whose partnership was only for your sake, since you assigned them a share of your wealth and your children. ﴿Who guides﴾ meaning: by clarification or by granting success, even after a time, ﴿to the truth?﴾ [much less guiding to the truth in the closest possible manner to existence, by way of informing].

Since they were ignorant of the true answer to this, or obstinate, He commanded him to answer them himself, without waiting for their reply, bringing both parts of the question as well, and so he said: ﴿Say, "God"﴾ meaning He who has complete encompassing knowledge ﴿guides﴾; and since He is able to do so with the utmost speed, He expressed it with the preposition lam, saying: ﴿to the truth﴾ [if He wills, and He guides whom He wills to the truth], and not any of those you claimed as partners. Therefore, occupying oneself with any of them, whether by worship or otherwise, is pure ignorance and a great derangement of disposition. [The verse is of the type of ihtibak: He mentioned ﴿to the truth﴾ first as an indication of its omission in the second place, and ﴿to the truth﴾ second as an indication of its omission in the first place.] Consequently, He denounced their followers' acceptance of them, saying: ﴿Then is He who guides﴾ meaning: reaching the utmost in His guidance, even from afar, ﴿to the truth﴾ meaning the perfect truth in which there is no deviation in any way [even in the most remote respects] ﴿more worthy to be followed﴾ meaning: with utmost effort, ﴿or he who cannot find guidance﴾ meaning: he who is not himself guided, much less able to guide others, to anything at all, altogether and entirely. The assimilation of the tā' of the ifti'āl form indicates the negation of all causes of guidance, to the point of approaching them, for the tā' in the understanding of the people of hearts signifies the reaching of causation to its lowest degree. ﴿Unless he is guided﴾ meaning: unless another guide guides him, whoever he may be. This encompasses everything worshipped besides God, whether rational or not. When He had completed this argument in this upright manner, it was as though it had been said: Will you answer, or will you remain silent? And if you answer, will you prefer the truth so that you return from error, or will you be obstinate? Consequent upon this, He asked them in a rebuking manner, saying: ﴿What then is wrong with you?﴾ meaning: what thing is established for you in doing other than the truth, whether by speech or by silence? Then He resumed with another rebuke, saying: ﴿How do you judge?﴾ concerning what we asked you about, which is something that should not be hidden from any intelligent person: is it by falsehood or by truth? Indeed, right guidance has become clear from error. And "the beginning" is the first intellect; "the return" is bringing a thing into existence a second time; and "guidance" is informing about the path of rectitude apart from error.

When he had reported their admission regarding some of what they were asked about, and then followed it with what hinted at their denial or silence regarding part of it, concerning their associates, he turned to what he had stated explicitly in their saying ﴿They will say﴾ [Yunus 31], and what he had hinted at with "they will deny" or "they will be silent," to His saying: ﴿And most of them follow nothing but conjecture (ẓann)﴾, meaning with the utmost effort. ﴿Most of them﴾ means in their speaking or their silence in worshipping the idols and in their saying that they are intercessors, and other than that. (p-119) ﴿Nothing but conjecture﴾ is a reminder that they are merely imitators and followers of their desires.

Since conjecture (ẓann) cannot be denied as a method used in the sacred law (sharī'ah), He drew attention to the fact that its proper place is only where there is no explicit text on the matter in question, so that analogy (qiyās) is then applied to the texts by its method. But when a definitive proof (qāṭi') exists regarding a ruling, it is not permissible to深 deviate from it in any way. So, in answer to one who says, "Is conjecture not used in many rulings?", He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾, meaning not at all, ﴿the truth﴾ meaning the complete truth, ﴿anything﴾, meaning as a substitute for it. It can substitute for the truth only if its follower is opposed in it by a definitive proof that he acts upon.

When the distinction had become self-evident, He placed the threat against one who persists in his error in response to "those who," as if He had said: that is not hidden from them, but they are arrogant and so they do not turn back. So He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, meaning the One who encompasses everything, ﴿is Knowing﴾, meaning with perfect knowledge, ﴿of what they do﴾. So be patient, for they will soon know.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 37:

When, in this surah, he (Allah) had presented their statement, "Why has not a sign been sent down upon him from his Lord?" (Yunus 10:20), and had given in reply to them, and as admonition to them, signs that are extremely far-reaching in wisdom, surpassing the powers of mankind, before which the capacities of creation are humbled, and the final part of that was an alert that their partners do not guide, except if the Guide guides them, let alone that they be guided, and the establishment of proof that their doctrines are not based on knowledge but are rather following desire, he followed that with a definitive proof regarding the matter of the Qur'an, that it is not at all valid that it be brought from other than His command, glorified is He, in refutation of their saying that it is fabricated (muftara), because it belongs to the category of what these verses concluded with, namely their following of conjectures (zunun), since they have no basis for that, indeed not even a shubha at all. It is merely desire. Rather, most of them know the truth regarding its matter. So He negated that with what removes conjectures, refutes adversaries, and leaves no doubt for one who is deluded, and He established that it is [the greatest sign] and the one deserving to be followed, because it is guidance. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it is not [possible]﴾, conjoining it to His saying: ﴿It is not for me to change it﴾ (Yunus 10:15) to the end of it. Thus it is then the object of the saying, meaning: say to them that statement, and say to them "it is not" (ma kana), that is, never, in any way whatsoever. He specified it with a specification such that no ambiguity is possible with it, so He said: ﴿This Qur'an﴾, that is, the one that gathers every good together with the conveyance through the methods of wisdom that are miraculous for all creation, ﴿that it be fabricated﴾ [that is] that it occur at any time [the deliberate attribution of it as a lie to Allah] from any one of creation, whoever he may be; and it was made known, by the diminishing of their rank beneath the lofty rank of Him, glorified is He, by His saying: ﴿besides Allah﴾, that is, the One Who is established as managing the whole affair, so there is no intercessor except after His permission, and nothing escapes Him. So glory be to the One who bestows favour upon His servants by making the proofs clear and removing doubts and calling to the path of right guidance, while He is free of need of them and able over them. And iftira' (fabrication) is announcing with certainty a lie, because it derives from fari al-adim (cutting the hide), and it is its cutting after its scraping (tafzir).

And since the coming of the unlettered one (ummi), the one who had not sat with a scholar, with reports and past narratives in a precise manner was a definitive proof of the truthfulness of the one who came with it in his claim that he has no teacher except Allah, he expressed it with the particle of contradiction, saying: ﴿But [it is]﴾, that is, it is an existence that cannot be otherwise, ﴿a confirmation of what was﴾, that is, had preceded, ﴿between its hands﴾, that is, before it, of the books. The evidence of its agreement with them is the witness of existence, together with the fact that the people were at the utmost hostility towards him (ﷺ), and the People of the Two Books were, among them, in the Arabian Peninsula, in the utmost proximity to them, together with the fact that they used to trade to the lands of Syria, [and they] being able to ask about everything he brought. So had they found any point of attack, they would have struck with it. Thus their not striking indicates agreement with certainty.

And since that was an overpowering authority upon his truthfulness (ﷺ), He increased its manifestness by what the Book that he brought comprised of detailed explanation, which is the very limit of knowledge, so He said: ﴿and a detailed explanation of the Book﴾, that is, the gathering in which wisdoms and rulings and comprehensive speech from all the heavenly books are assembled, in clarifying their general statements and elucidating their difficult matters. So it looks to His saying: ﴿Is one who guides to the truth...﴾ (Yunus 10:35), to the end of the verse. So it is a proof that He alone is the Guide, so He is the one deserving to be followed. And the detailed explanation is by making clear the separation between the ambiguous meanings until each meaning is shown in its right place. Its counterpart is division, and its opposite is confusion and obfuscation. And the explanation of its detail is that it came with the scientific sciences of belief, of knowledge of the Essence and the Attributes in their divisions, and the practical sciences of obligation related to the outward, which is the science of jurisprudence (fiqh), and the science of the inward and the discipline of the souls, with what has no addition to it and no equal to it in any book; and the science of ethics, which is abundant in the Qur'an, such as ﴿Take what is easy in forgiveness﴾ (al-A'raf 7:199) - to the end of the verse,

﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice﴾ (al-Nahl 16:90) - to the end of the verse, and similar to these two.

And since it was, together with the testimony to truthfulness through the confirmation of what was established in reality, miraculous through the gathering and detailing of all the sciences, [the noble ones]: its rational and its transmitted ones, a miraculousness that has not been established for anything else, it was established that it contradicts fabrication, while it is ﴿without doubt in it﴾, and that it is ﴿from the Lord of the worlds﴾, that is, the Creator of them, the Manager of their affair, and the Benefactor to them, because it, together with gathering all of that, has no disagreement in it in any respect, and that is beyond the capacity of mankind.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 38:

Since this is the place where they should submit, because this Qur'an is nothing but from Allah and by His command, with certainty, it is as if it were said: "Will they turn back from their error, believe and stand firm?" ﴿Am﴾ (or) do they persist in their misguidance, ﴿saying﴾ repeatedly and continuously, out of obstinacy, ﴿"He has invented it"﴾ [i.e., they deliberately attributed it to Allah as a lie]. So it is as if it were said: they persisted in their rebellion and said that, and they were like one who seeks his own death with his own hoof, because they established a corrupt foundation, from which it necessarily follows \ with certainty the possibility that they could produce its like, since they are Arabs like it. Indeed, some of them read and wrote, mixed with scholars, and their care for the various kinds of eloquence in verse and prose, and in sermons, and their practice in them, was intense, unlike him ﷺ in all of that. Therefore, in answering them, He commanded him with His words: ﴿Say﴾, i.e., to them, O most eloquent of Our creation and the most knowing of them of the positions of speech in all its kinds. He brought the causal ﻓ (fa, "so") in His words: ﴿then bring﴾, i.e., you yourselves, as confirmation of this statement of yours which has become clear, and that you are obstinate in it. Since they had definitively asserted in this surah that he had invented it, and it was divided into surahs, each of which has a specific aim by which it is proven, and whose ending is linked to its beginning and unified with it, He sufficed in their challenge with bringing one single piece not divided into surahs, but being like the whole Qur'an in length, clarity, orderliness of expression, and harmony of meanings. Therefore He said: ﴿a surah﴾. Al-Rummani said: "The surah is a revealed unit enclosing verses, from the beginning to the end, like the enclosure of the walls of a building." This is with regard to the fact that the challenged thing is a surah in the technical sense, but the correct view is that it is in the linguistic sense, and it is—as al-Harrali said—the completion of a group of what is heard, enclosing a complete meaning, like the enclosure of walls around a city. He described it by His words: ﴿like it﴾, i.e., in eloquence, beauty of arrangement, soundness of meanings, agreement with previous books, and detailed explanation of sciences; because you are like me in Arabic, and you exceed me in writing and in mixing with scholars—without the use of ﻣِﻦ (min, "from"), because of what has preceded, that the intended meaning is that it be like the whole Qur'an. For this reason, He allowed them to seek help from all whom they were able to reach and whose capacity extended to them, and He did not restrict them to those present with them. So He said: ﴿and call upon﴾, i.e., for your assistance, ﴿whomever you can﴾, i.e., whom you are able to obey, even by exerting effort, from the jinn and mankind and others, for assistance. And He established that this Qur'an is from Him, glory be to Him, by the exception in His words: ﴿other than Allah﴾, i.e., the One to whom all perfection belongs. He drew attention to the fact that they deliberately attributed it to Him—and He is far above deliberately lying—and that they are obstinate by His words: ﴿if you are﴾, i.e., by nature and disposition, ﴿truthful﴾, i.e., in claiming that he brought it from himself. For the intelligent person does not assert anything unless he has a way out of it, and that does not happen except by clear evidence and an overpowering, dazzling authority. What has passed in al-Baqarah and what will come in Hud, if Allah the Exalted wills, clarifies this meaning. And "istita'ah" (capacity) is a state by which the limbs and faculties are made obedient for the act, because it is derived from "ta'w" (obedience).

Then it was as if it were said: he told them that, and they brought their people no doubt that would necessitate skepticism, let alone a confirmation, because it is inimitable, being speech at the highest level of eloquence in its fine arrangement and its sublimity, sent down from God, Who encompasses all in knowledge and power. Thus it includes, in every meaning, what rises far above every lowly thing ﴿Nay﴾. And more excellent than this: when He established the proof that the Qur'an is His speech, and proof is by its nature established only against one who is subject to error or doubt, and their saying ﴿"He has forged it"﴾ [Yunus: 38] was not based on doubt but was merely obstinacy, He, glorified be He, drew attention to this, and to the fact that He established the proof only to manifest their obstinacy, not because they had any doubt about its being true. By turning away from their saying, He said: ﴿Nay﴾, meaning: they did not say "He forged it" out of any belief of theirs in that; rather ﴿they denied﴾, meaning: they committed the denial, which is no denial more shameful than it, hastening in that without comprehending it, scorning ﴿that which they did not encompass in knowledge﴾, meaning, in its arrangement or its meaning, without any doubt at all, rather (p-125) out of obstinacy, transgression and aversion from what opposes their religion, and fleeing from it. This falls under the saying "whoever is ignorant of a thing becomes its enemy." And ihata (encompassing) means intending what is like a wall around a thing; so the encompassing of knowledge of a thing is knowing it from all its aspects.

Since its ta'wil (fulfilment, i.e., the actual occurrence of what it contains of reports of unseen matters as they are) must inevitably come about, He said: ﴿And its ta'wil has not yet come to them﴾, meaning: up to the time of their denial ﴿its ta'wil﴾, meaning: Our returning its reports to their referents and ultimate ends, until they know whether they are true or false. For it is inimitable both in its arrangement and in the truthfulness of its reports; and ta'wil (interpretation/ultimate meaning) is the meaning to which tafsir (exegesis) leads, and it is the furthest point of explicit statement from implication.

Since it was as if it were said: "Indeed their act is astonishing, so what impelled them to persist in it?" It was answered: they followed those before them in this, because they agreed with them in evil disposition. He said, threatening them and consoling him ﷺ: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning: like their denial of this, that great denial in its enormity, before the arrival of the inimitable's ta'wil ﴿those before them denied﴾. Since the deniers were some of the earlier peoples, He stated the preposition, saying: ﴿from before them﴾, meaning: from the unbelievers of the bygone nations, so they did wrong and We destroyed them for their wrongdoing. And since denial is a danger because of the joy it produces, He made a consequence of it, as a warning from it, the looking into the outcome of their affair, saying: ﴿So look﴾, meaning: with your eye at their dwellings and with your heart at their reports.

Since whoever looks in this way finds in it the most magnificent lesson and the highest deterrent, He directed the question to him, saying: ﴿how was the end of﴾, meaning: the final outcome of ﴿the wrongdoers﴾ (p-126), that is, those whose feet were firmly planted in placing things in other than their proper places, to the extent that they denied One who cannot in any way be subject to falsehood. And it is certain that the one asked would say, without hesitation or doubt: a dire end, crushing and blameworthy. The "end" (aqibah) is a cause to which the beginning leads; so what led to their destruction by the punishment of annihilation was what preceded of their wronging themselves and their insolence in their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 40:

When He, glory be to Him, mentioned their denial, that might have caused him (ﷺ) to despair of their submission and acceptance, and it signaled their annihilation so that the resemblance to the earlier peoples would be complete. The Prophet (ﷺ) was extremely compassionate toward them and keen for their faith, so God, exalted is He, followed this with His saying, as an explanation that His knowledge of their divisions required that they not be annihilated [linking it conjunctively to ﴿they denied﴾ (Yunus: 39)]: ﴿And among them﴾, i.e., your people, ﴿are those who believe in it﴾, i.e., in the future, ﴿and among them are those who do not believe in it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, at all, even if they saw every sign. ﴿And your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is good to you by being gentle with your community, ﴿knows best the corrupters﴾, i.e., those who are deeply immersed in corruption, so He will deal with them in a way that will soothe your heart.

When this verse divided them into two groups, and the second group was introduced with the conjunction *wa* (and), it became known that it is coordinated with the elided part of the first group. So it is as if it had been said: "If they deny you, then say: God is the Guardian of your guidance and the Guardian of your rewards, by my being a means to them through His bounty." Then: ﴿And if they deny you, say﴾ — that is, the words of one who is fair and relies on the All-Powerful, the All-Knowing — ﴿"To me is my work"﴾ through faith and obedience, ﴿"and to you is your work."﴾ (p. 127) Neither one owes the other any favour, and neither bears any of the other's recompense. Then he stated the purpose of this explicitly, warning them with the words: ﴿"You are free from what I do"﴾, meaning: if it is good, nothing of it is yours, and if it is other than good, nothing of it is upon you. ﴿"And I am free from what you do"﴾: I bear no blame for any part of it, because I cannot prevent you from it. *Al-bara'a* (disavowal) is the severing of the tie that necessitates the claim being pursued. There is no need to claim that this verse was abrogated (*naskh*) by the verse of the sword, for there is no contradiction between them, since this verse concerns the removal of liability for sin, and that does not conflict with *jihad*.

When he divided them into these two groups, he divided the last group into two, saying: ﴿"And among them"﴾, that is, among the deniers, ﴿"are those who"﴾. Since listening to him was more common (because they were the most eager of people to learn his condition), and since the way to that is hearing and sight, and since staring at him does not go unnoticed, most of them would abandon it, both to show their hatred and out of fear of the denunciation of anyone who sees them doing it. Since casting the ear with utmost effort can be concealed, unlike looking, he expressed it here with the *iftial* form (*yastami'una*), and used the plural in the listening, in consideration of the meaning of *man* (who), and used the singular in the looking, in consideration of its wording, and to indicate the fewness of those who look, for the reason mentioned. So he said: ﴿"listen"﴾, and he included in *al-istima'* (listening) the sense of *al-isgha'* (lending the ear), so that it would perform the function of both verbs. He indicated lending the ear by the complement attached to it, placed in the state of a circumstantial clause derived from it, as if he had said: ﴿"attentive"﴾ ﴿"to you"﴾, that is, during the recitation of the Qur'an and its explanation through the Sunnah. However, although they form two groups with respect to listening and looking, they are (p. 128) one group with respect to misguidance. So the mention of their gathering after restricting guidance to Him, glorified is He, is like the mention of their gathering earlier after dividing them into two groups, following His saying: ﴿"And He guides whom He wills to a straight path"﴾ [Yunus: 25].

Since he (ﷺ) wished, by making them hear what God had sent down, to guide them through it, the consequence of their listening was a denial of their hearing what would bring guidance. So he said: ﴿"Then can you"﴾, that is, by yourself, ﴿"make the deaf hear"﴾, that is, in the ears of their hearts? For they listen to you, yet He has set a seal upon their hearing, so they do not benefit from their listening, because they seek to hear only in order to reply, not to understand. *Al-sam'* (hearing) is the perception of a thing by that by which it becomes heard. Because of their failure to benefit, they were as if they were madmen, for a deaf person who has reason may often understand by observing the movement of lips and the like. Therefore he said: ﴿"even if they"﴾, that is, by nature and disposition, ﴿"did not understand"﴾, that is, reason does not come to them at all, so they are in a state in which their hearing cannot be achieved, since it can only be achieved by hearing the sound that indicates the meaning and by understanding the meaning. What prevents the first is deafness; what prevents the second is lack of reason. Thus they became worse than beasts, for although beasts do not reason, they do hear. *Al-asamm* (the deaf) is one whose hearing is blocked by something that prevents perceiving sound. ﴿"And among them are those who look"﴾, staring or aiming their sight from afar, ﴿"at you"﴾. This is of the nature of *tadmin* (conveying one verb's sense through another), as was mentioned in ﴿"listen"﴾. It is reported from al-Taftazani that he said in his gloss on the *Kashshaf*: The reality of *tadmin* is that the verb is intended in its literal meaning together with another verb that suits it (p. 129), and this is common in Arabic speech, with the omission of a circumstantial element derived from the other verb, through the verbal indication. The mentioned verb must be taken as primary and its circumstantial element as secondary, because omitting it and indicating it by its complement shows that it is considered in the sentence, not that additional intention is directed to it. Among its examples: *aḥmadu ilayka Allāh* (I praise God to you), meaning "conveying His praise to you"; and *yuqallibu kaffayhi 'alā kadhā* (he turns his palms over regarding such-and-such), meaning "regretting it."

﴿"And do not let your eyes turn away from them"﴾ [al-Kahf: 28], meaning: passing beyond them to others.

﴿"And do not consume their wealth"﴾ [al-Nisa': 2] — combining them — ﴿"with your wealth"﴾ [al-Nisa': 2]. ﴿"Obscenity"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187] — reaching — ﴿"to your wives"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187]. ﴿"And do not resolve"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 235], meaning: upon the marriage contract while intending to conclude it. ﴿"They do not listen"﴾ [al-Saffat: 8] — lending the ear — ﴿"to the exalted assembly"﴾ [al-Saffat: 8]. ("God hears" — meaning responds to — "him who praises Him.") 

﴿"And God knows the corrupter"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 220] — distinguishing him — ﴿"from the reformer"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 220]. And those who take an oath to abstain — refraining from having intercourse with their wives.

Since the meaning is that you, O noblest of creation, intend by the looking of this one at you that he should look at the stupendous signs you bring, and thus be guided, while he does not benefit from his looking because of the veil placed over him, he was like the blind man who, in addition to lacking sight, lacks reason, so he has neither sight nor insight. He said, denouncing this: ﴿"Then can you guide the blind"﴾ (p. 130), that is, of eyes and hearts, ﴿"even if they"﴾, that is, by what they were created upon, ﴿"do not see"﴾, that is, sight and insight will not come to them at all, so their guidance is impossible. When he divided them into these two groups, he divided the last group into two, saying: ﴿"And among them"﴾, that is, among the deniers, ﴿"are those who"﴾. [p. 131] When these verses contained the various forms of their disputation over their falsehoods and their misguidance, and such conduct, from people who expect no gathering, no recompense, and no bliss beyond the bliss of this abode, is the conduct of one who is carefree, who lengthens his days in the world, and who is secure from the calamities of events, it was fitting that it be followed by the statement that on the Day of Gathering they will see such terrors that they will deem the duration of their stay in the world short. Having lost their worldly life through their contention, and their Hereafter through a punishment that cannot be endured and has no end, Exalted is He said, threatening these disbelievers who obstinately refuse to hear or to see, and joining it by conjunction to the first ﴿And the Day We gather them﴾ [Yunus 10:28], which is ﴿And the Day He gathers them﴾. That is: they will deem the duration of their stay in the world short on the Day of Gathering, because of the terrors and the long, violent convulsions that confront them. It is as if it were said: "Up to what limit?" And it was said: ﴿as though﴾, meaning as though they ﴿had not remained﴾ in their world. The clause is in the position of a circumstantial phrase (ḥāl) from the pronoun of "We gather them," which is explicit, meaning: likened to those who did not remain ﴿but an hour﴾, that is, a brief one, ﴿of the day﴾. His saying ﴿recognizing one another﴾ is a second circumstantial phrase, meaning: that hour did not benefit them more than that some of them recognized others in it, so that they would increase in regret on that Day, by being unable to help, support, and aid one another as they used to do in the world.

Since their state was this loss with which no trade is possible, and the hearer was awaiting a report about it, He said, marvelling at them in the place of "How much they lost!": ﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost﴾, meaning truly. The phrase ﴿those who denied﴾ is stated explicitly in place of a pronoun, to generalize and to attach the judgment to the attribute, [those who are] ﴿scornful of the meeting with Allah﴾, that is, the Sovereign, the Most High, because of what they took from the world of base and perishing things, and abandoned of the noble, enduring bliss that the Resurrection had been revealed to them to contain. Since the one who has denied once in his lifetime may later awaken and be guided, He said, joining it by conjunction to the relative clause: ﴿and they were not﴾, that is, by disposition and nature, ﴿guided﴾, indicating their folly regarding what they claim to have insight into, namely the matter of trade and knowledge of the varieties of guidance.

Since the report of the truthful one about the destruction of the enemies is soothing to the eye, and witnessing their destruction is more soothing still, the verse is linked to His saying ﴿They have lost﴾ [Yunus: 45]: ﴿Whether We show you﴾, meaning a great showing, ﴿some of what We promise them﴾, meaning in this world, with the greatness that is Ours, so that it is more soothing to your eye; ﴿or We take you in death﴾ before that, ﴿then to Us is their return﴾, so We will show you there what is more soothing to your eye and more gladdening to your heart. Thus the verse is of the *ihtibak* (the rhetorical device of omitting parallel elements): it mentioned the showing first as an indication of its omission the second time, and the death second as an indication of its omission the first time. The *thumma* (then) in His saying ﴿Then Allah﴾, meaning the One who encompasses everything, ﴿is Witness﴾, meaning of utmost witnessing, ﴿over what they do﴾ in both abodes, may be on its proper meaning, indicating the interval between the beginning of their return by death and its end at the Resurrection. The intended meaning of His saying ﴿Witness﴾ is not its apparent sense, but the punishment arising from that witnessing in the Hereafter, namely that Allah punishes them after their return. So He shows you what comes after them, for He is knowing of what they do.

(p-133) Since this verse contains a threat of punishment, either in this world or in the Hereafter, without specifying for him ﷺ either one of them, He followed it with what is applicable to both matters in relation to every messenger, indicating that the affairs of nations are not in a fixed order. Therefore He did not decisively specify either of the two abodes for the requital, and the matter was made dependent upon justice (al-qist): wherever He judges it, He places it there. So He, exalted is He, said [indicating that He spread the remembrance of Islam, which is faith in Allah, His angels, His books, His messenger, and the Last Day, from the time of Adam, peace be upon him, until the end of time, in a manner that never became obliterated in any age of the ages; so whoever abandons it deserves punishment, whether he was among those between Jesus and Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon them both, or not. So do not be deceived by what is said other than this]: ﴿And for every nation﴾, i.e., of the nations that passed before you, ﴿there is a messenger﴾ calling them to Allah. Then He made the explanation of the judgment concerning them a consequence of the coming of their messenger, saying: ﴿So when their messenger comes﴾ [i.e., to them] ﴿in this world with clear proofs and guidance; and in the Hereafter, in the place of standing, with the report of what they did to him in this world of denial or affirmation﴾, ﴿it is judged between them﴾ [i.e., in all matters, by what the removal of the preposition conveys in the easiest manner, without doubt, by what the passive voice conveys; and since the context called for intimidation more fittingly, He said]: ﴿with justice﴾, i.e., making manifest what was [hidden] of their deserving in the judgment, with justice, and with an equitable apportioning among all of them equally, giving each one of them the portion that befits him, [in hastening or delaying the punishment, as He did with you]. Since that does not necessarily imply permanence, He said: ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾ (p-134), i.e., no wrong will be newly inflicted upon them by Him, glorified is He, nor by anyone else.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 48:

When in these verses the threat of punishment in this world or in the Hereafter had preceded, Allah (Subhanahu wa Ta'ala) related their reply to that, as a continuation of His saying: ﴿And they say, "Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ [Yunus: 20]. So He said: ﴿And they say﴾, i.e., these polytheists, repeatedly renewing this saying and persisting in it, mockingly: ﴿When is this promise?﴾, i.e., of punishment in this world or in the Hereafter. They urged and incited one another with their saying: ﴿If you are truthful﴾, i.e., you and those who speak with your speech. Qawl (saying) is speech that is implied in the mention of it by narration, and there may be speech that is not expressed, so it has no mention and is not implied by narration; thus it is not a saying, since it is only a saying by virtue of its mention being implied by narration. This was stated by al-Rummani. [The word qawl is also used] to imply placing a thing in a container. Wa'd (promise) is news of what good will be given, and wa'id (threat) is news of what evil will be given. It may be intended in a general sense, as here, so that wa'd is applied to both meanings: the promise of reward to the one who does good and the threat of punishment to the one who does evil. Sidq (truthfulness) is reporting a thing as it actually is, and kadhib (falsehood) is reporting it contrary to what it actually is.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 49:

When their saying contained their urging him ﷺ to bring about what he threatens them with, He commanded him to disavow power over anything that God has not decreed for him, by His saying: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to your people who mock, ﴿I possess no power for myself﴾, let alone for others. And since the context concerns vengeance, He placed the harm first, alerting that His blessings are more numerous than His punishments, and that they are within His blessings, which they should bind with gratitude out of fear of their loss, let alone wishing for it. So He said: ﴿harm or benefit﴾.

Since it is observed that every living creature disposes of itself and others with some of that, He said: ﴿except what God wills﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in knowledge and power, that I should possess some of that. It is as if it were said: "Why do you not ask Him to will that and empower you over it?" So it was said: ﴿For every nation there is a term﴾. It is as if it were said: "And what happens with it?" So it was said: ﴿When their term comes﴾, they perish. And since cutting off their hope of respite in the term is among the severest of their punishments, He placed first His saying: ﴿they cannot delay it by an hour﴾, that is, from it, ﴿nor advance it﴾. Then He conjoined, to the whole conditional sentence, ﴿nor advance it﴾, so do not hasten it, for the fulfilment of the promise is unavoidable. The sīn (s) in both of them carries the sense of finding (wijdān), that is, the meaning from which the verb is derived does not exist for them, like: "istashkala al-shay'" and "istathqalahu" (he found it difficult/heavy). It is also permissible that the meaning be: they do not find delay or advancement even if they strive in seeking it, so the sīn then carries the sense of seeking (ṭalab).

Al-mulk (possession) is a power by which one is enabled to direct a thing with the most complete direction. Al-naf' (benefit) is the causing of pleasure through an act or a causing that leads to it. Al-ḍurr (harm) is the causing of pain through an act or a causing that leads to it. Al-ajal (term) is the appointed time for the occurrence of a matter.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verses 50–51:

Since the main purpose of their question was mockery, and its occurrence was a possibility, and it is the way of a sensible person to keep far from every possible danger, he (ﷺ) was commanded with another answer, from which the conjunction *waw* of coordination was dropped, lest it be thought that it suffices to be an answer only when joined to what precedes it. So He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to the one who considered Our threat of punishment slow to come, whether in this world or the next. And it could only occur after the seizing in this world, to inform them that what they seek is pure harm to them, with no benefit in it in any way, so it is something to which the intention of a sensible person does not turn. ﴿Tell me﴾, and this is from the sight of the heart, because it is followed by a clause of interrogation, ﴿if His punishment comes upon you﴾ in this world.

Since seizing by night is more painful and swifter, He placed it first and said: ﴿by night﴾, [that is] at night, suddenly, while you are sleeping, as an enemy does. Since victory by night does not necessitate victory by day in open confrontation, He said: ﴿or by day﴾, that is, openly, while you are awake. Will you then persist in your obstinacy and not believe? It is as if they had said: No. So let it be hastened upon them that they may see it. It was said: Indeed you do not know what you seek! Indeed no created being has the capacity for any kind of it, and none dares to speak such words except a criminal. ﴿What﴾, that is, which thing? It is also permissible that this be the answer to the condition. ﴿Do they seek to hasten﴾, that is, they ask for haste ﴿of it﴾, that is, of His punishment, and all of His punishment is hateful, and no part of it can be borne. ﴿The criminals﴾, since the way of God has continued that the one who denies does not believe except when its signs appear. But when it falls upon him with its full weight and settles on him with its burden, he then believes at a time when belief does not benefit him. ﴿And you will never find any change in the way of God﴾ [Fatir: 43]. This is the meaning of the delay in His saying: ﴿Then, when it befalls﴾, that is, His punishment, and everything contrary to it has ceased, ﴿do you believe in it?﴾. That is because their custom, like that of those before them, was to seek haste for the punishment when it was threatened, and God's way had been that when the deniers are struck by punishment, their belief is delayed after the arrival of its preliminaries and before they are uprooted by its great blows, because of the severity of their opposition and their settling into it. This happened to the earlier nations out of rebellion and insolence, like the people of Salih, when their faces changed into different colours on the first day, then the second, then the third, and they became certain of destruction, and bade one another farewell, and did not believe. And it has been the way that when they taste the touch of the punishment and sudden calamities seize them, its calamities distract them from obstinacy, and its terrors compel them to easy submission. Thus it was most fitting to place the rebuke for their haste immediately after the threat, and then to place the delay in belief, despite obstinacy, after having come to the edge of destruction and witnessed perdition. So it was as if it had been said: Tell me, supposing His punishment, which is no greater punishment, as the idafa to Him indicates, comes upon you, whether by night or openly, what will you do? Will you not believe? They said: No. So let it be hastened upon them that they may see it. It was thus fitting, since their haste came after this warning, to rebuke them for it, so it was said: ﴿What﴾, that is, what kind of it do the criminals seek to hasten, when there is no kind of it except that it is beyond capacity and beyond endurance? Indeed this is a hateful opinion. Is it, after your belief has been delayed from the signs of its blow and from witnessing the beginnings of its greatness and severity, that you produce belief in it when it falls? It will be said to you, when its calamities have compelled you to belief, and its afflictions have brought you to submission: ﴿Now?﴾ Do you believe in it, that is, because of it, after Our might has removed your strength and dissolved the resolve and vigour of your aspirations? ﴿And you had been﴾, that is, in a state as though you were formed upon it, ﴿seeking its haste﴾, that is, you were asking for its speedy coming with great insistence, even as though you were asking for the haste of something other than it, through denial and resolve to persist in obstinacy. Had it come and We had not accepted your belief from you, nor withheld Our punishment from you, but made you like yesterday that has passed away.
