Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 52:

Since what was mentioned is the worldly punishment, he followed it with what comes after it, to inform that their recompense is not limited to it. So he said: ﴿Then it will be said﴾, i.e., by whatever speaker it may be, in contempt, ﴿to those who wronged﴾, i.e., after your being pressed in the world and the barzakh (intermediate realm) with punishment and your being shaken by severe retribution: it will be said to you on the Day of Religion, because of your wronging through the signs and what you were commanded in them, by placing each of those things in other than its proper place: ﴿Taste the punishment of eternity﴾. The use of "thumma" (then) indicates the delay of that from the destruction in the world by remaining in the barzakh, or indicates that His punishment there is lower than the punishment of the Day of Religion. ﴿Are you recompensed?﴾ He built it for the passive because what is frightening is recompense in general. Since the interrogative of denial has the meaning of negation, and the meaning was "with anything," he made an exception from it, saying: ﴿except by what you were﴾, i.e., by your natures, ﴿earning﴾, i.e., in the world, from the resolve to persist in disbelief, (p-139) even if time extends, you would not be released from it by any of things, however great it may be. So your recompense is eternal abiding in the punishment, exactly matching the sandal to the sandal. And "al-adhab" (punishment): the continuous pain, and its root is continuity, and from it comes "al-udhuba" (sweetness) for its continuity in the throat. "Al-bayat" (the coming of a thing at night). And "al-dhawq" (tasting): seeking the taste with the mouth at the beginning of taking.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 53:

When what this verse contains of threat and clear warning had ended, God Most High informed that they had come to what is fitting for one who hears this: to give up that obstinacy and move toward the beginnings of submission, through His saying, Most High: ﴿And they ask you to inform them﴾, as a conjunction (ʿaṭf) to His saying, "And they say, 'When is this promise?'" That is: they ask you for information (inbāʾ), which is a great announcement about the reality of this weighty promise. It is possible that this request came from them in the manner of mockery, as the first one did, so the astonishment and rebuke in it would be even stronger after the proofs that have passed. ﴿Is it true?﴾ That is: Is this that you threaten us with real and established, or is it like magic, having no reality, as they had previously said? ﴿Say﴾, that is, in answer to them: ﴿Yes, by my Lord﴾, that is, the One who is good to me, who manages my affairs, and who confirms everything I bring. Since they were deniers, he emphasized his statement: ﴿Indeed it is true﴾, that is: it will certainly occur and be established, and it must come upon you.

Since a thing may be true while a person is able to avert it and so is not overawed by it, he said, negating this: ﴿And you cannot escape﴾, that is, from the one who threatens you, ﴿regarding what is intended for you﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 54:

When He had informed them of its reality, He also informed them of the wrongdoing that would come from them at the moment of seeing it, when they would be permitted to offer the ransom of everything on earth, at a time when ransom no longer benefits after abandoning what was commanded. This is among the easiest and most excellent of things, so He said: ﴿And if every soul that had wronged had everything that is on the earth﴾, that is, at the moment of witnessing it, ﴿it would surely offer it as ransom﴾, that is, it would make it a ransom for itself from the punishment. But this is not for them, and even if it were accepted from them, ﴿when they see the punishment﴾, they would submit. ﴿And they will conceal the regret﴾, that is, their remorse will intensify and they will not be able to speak, ﴿when they see the punishment﴾, because they will be struck dumb by the greatness of what has overtaken them, so their action will be the action of one who conceals, for they will not be able to bear weeping, complaint, or anything that the one who is distressed does. Al-istinba' (seeking information) is the request for news, just as al-istifham (questioning) is the request for understanding. Al-naba' is news about a certainty concerning a great matter. Al-haqq is a firm belief in the meaning according to what wisdom calls for, and everything built upon this belief is true on its account. Al-haqq in religion is what evidence attests to with confidence regarding matters whose path is knowledge, and strength regarding matters whose path is the predominant outcome; this applies to what admits of two matters, one of which is more akin to the principle that the text came with. Al-iftida' (ransom) is placing a thing in place of another to remove what is disliked; one says fadahu fidyah, and afdahu, and iftadahu iftida', and fada'ahu mufada'ah, and fadahu tafdiyah, and tafada minhu tafadiyan. Al-israr is concealing a thing within the self. Al-nadamah is grief over what one wished had not occurred, having brought it about. It is a rational state in which its bearer regrets what has happened from him and wishes he had not caused it.

When the preceding verses included the certainty of fulfilling the promise and justice in judgment, and they were concluded with His saying: ﴿And it will be judged﴾, that is, He will carry out the judgment in the easiest and most facile manner; since the judgment encompassed all their events, He omitted the preposition and said: ﴿between them﴾, that is, the wrongdoers and the wronged, and the wrongdoers and the greater wrongdoers, ﴿with justice﴾, that is, with equity. Since the occurrence of this does not negate the occurrence of wrongdoing at another time, He said: ﴿while they are not wronged﴾, that is, while the state is that they are not subjected to any wrong from anyone at all, whoever he may be, at any time.

Al-Biqa'i, Nazm al-Durar, on Surah 10, verse 55:

Since the motive that drives the kings of this world to lying, oppression and injustice is either incapacity or the desire to increase their dominion, He indicated His transcendence above that by saying, emphatically, driving them toward the manner of one who denies the content of the speech, because their act of worshipping idols is the act of one who denies it: ﴿Verily, to Allah belongs﴾, that is, the Greatest King alone, ﴿whatever is in the heavens﴾. He began with them because of their elevation in meaning and in sensible form, and their greatness. And since the context is one of freedom from injustice, the situation did not require emphasis by repeating the negation, so He said: ﴿and the earth﴾, that is, of substance and accident, mute and speaking. Nothing is outside His dominion, which would necessitate His resorting to injustice or breaking a promise in order to possess it. The conclusion is that only one whose dominion is incomplete acts unjustly; as for one to whom all dominion belongs, He is the Judge, the Just, since all things are equal in relation to Him. Only one of deficient power breaks a promise; as for one to whom everything belongs and from whose grasp nothing escapes, He is the Truthful in promise and the Just in judgment. In the verse there is also an increase in reproach and regret for the wrongdoing soul, since it is informed that what it would wish to ransom itself with is not its own, and it cannot reach it. Had it been able, it would not have been accepted from it (p-142), and acceptance is only for one who is content with a little of it, as a favour from Him toward it, in accordance with what He commanded through His messengers. On this basis, the sense may be: "If it were theirs, they would have ransomed themselves with it, but it is not theirs; rather it belongs to Allah." When His judgment by justice and His transcendence above breaking promises were thus established, He stated the content of that explicitly, emphasizing it against their denial, saying: ﴿Verily, the promise of Allah﴾, that is, of the One to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿is true﴾, because He is perfect in power and self-sufficiency, so there is no motive [for Him] to break it. ﴿But most of them﴾, that is, those whom you address while they claim subtlety of understanding and breadth of intellect, ﴿do not know﴾, that is, they have no knowledge, for they do not reflect upon the proofs We have set up, and so they do not submit to what We have commanded in the Law. Thus they remain in ignorance, counted together with the beasts.

"Alā" (ألا) is composed of the interrogative hamza and "lā"; it was originally for confirmation and reminder, and then became a means of alerting attention. "Inna" (إنّ) after it is pronounced with kasra because it is resumptive (isti'nafiyyah), by which attention is drawn to a meaning that is about to be begun; for this reason the imperative and supplication occur after it, unlike "law" (لو) and "illā" (إلا), which concern the future, so after them only the kasra of "inna" was permissible. "Amā" (أما) may mean "truly" (حقًّا) in the saying "amā innahu munṭaliq," and it indicates the present, so both readings are permissible for "inna" after it, as al-Rummani mentioned.

"Al-samāwāt" (السماوات) are raised layers, the first of which is a ceiling adorned with stars. It derives from "samā," meaning "to be high."

When it had been established that nothing lies outside His dominion, that He is absolutely capable, since no one can save from His punishment, that His knowledge encompasses His judgment with justice, and that His promise is true, because nothing compels Him to act otherwise, and when His sole power to give life and cause death had been established, it was established that He is able to restore creation as He was able to originate it. Therefore it was established that the return is only to Him. He drew attention to this by His saying: ﴿He﴾, that is, alone, ﴿gives life﴾, that is, as you acknowledge ﴿and causes death﴾, as you witness ﴿and to Him﴾, that is, not to anyone else, ﴿you will be returned﴾. This is because He promised this in His saying: ﴿To Him is your return, all of you, as a promise of Allah in truth﴾ [Yunus: 4], and in His saying: ﴿To Us is their return﴾ [Yunus: 46], and in His saying: ﴿Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true﴾ [Yunus: 53], and in other verses, and there is nothing that prevents Him from doing so. Life (al-hayah) is a ma'na (a real attribute) which necessitates the soundness of knowledge and power and [opposes] death. It inheres in all the parts of a living being, so that by its totality it becomes one living entity. The living (al-hayy) is the one who is fit to be capable, and the capable (al-qadir) is the one who is fit to be blamed and praised for what he does. Death is a ma'na which opposes life in the animal structure, and inanimateness (al-jamadiyyah) is not like that.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 10, verse 57:

When it was established that all of that is truth, distinct from magic, whose foundation is imagination (*takhyil*), he turned to those whose report was mentioned at the beginning of the surah in His saying: "Is it a wonder for people that We have revealed to a man among them...?" They said it is magic, so He said: ﴿O mankind﴾, that is, those who said that Our promise and its report are magic. Since there is a natural love between the spirits and the bodies, through attachment, the spirit takes pleasure in the desires of this worldly life, because of what is impressed upon it through the appearances of the senses. So the light of the intellect does not reach it, until the deficiencies return through the strength of attachment [p. 144], and so there arise in it blameworthy characters, which are spiritual diseases. So its Lord, who created it, arranged its affairs, and was good to it, sent a skilled physician, who is the Messenger (ﷺ), to treat these diseases. And He sent down His Mighty Book to describe the remedies. The soundest of medicine is to keep the patient away from the causes of the illness. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿There has certainly come to you an admonition﴾, that is, a great restraining warning against abandoning everything that occupies the heart away from God, of forbidden things and others, of everything that is not fitting. That is the Shari'ah (sacred law).

Since consuming what harms is of great danger, and yet it is pleasant to the soul because of the suitability of the deficiency between them, and since refraining from it is the hardest thing for the soul, He encouraged it to accept by His saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾, that is, the One who is good to you, who arranges your welfare through this Qur'an. And since the most appropriate course after dietary restraint is to take the medicine that removes the corrupt humours from within, He said: ﴿and a healing﴾, that is, a very great healing, ﴿for what is in the breasts﴾ of the afflictions of ignorance. That healing is attained by purifying the inner self after abandoning blameworthy characters, by adorning oneself with praiseworthy qualities, so that the inner self becomes sound from corrupt beliefs and deficient characters, just as the body is sound from base actions. This is the Path.

Since the spirit, when its mirror is polished and becomes receptive to the manifestation of lights upon it, [through the outpouring of] divine flashes, holy breezes and angelic gifts, because it is constantly shining, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said in what al-Tabarani narrated from Muhammad ibn Maslamah (may Allah be pleased with him): "Indeed your Lord has breezes of grace in the days of your time; so be alert to them," the hadith [p. 145]. The only thing preventing their descent into every heart is the lack of receptivity in some hearts, due to the accumulation of darknesses in them from the rust of disobedience and the religion of aversion and heedlessness. Thus such a heart is like rusted mirrors that do not receive the imprint of images. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and guidance﴾ to the truth, because it is a great light that leads its possessor, without fail, to the straightest path. This is for the truthful ones (*al-siddiqin*), and it is the Reality (*al-haqiqah*).

Since this light, when it increases in greatness and its radiance spreads, overflows, after reaching these spiritual degrees and divine ascents, upon the spirits of the deficient, like the overflow of light from the substance of the sun upon the bodies of the world, illuminating every receptive one who turns towards it, He said: ﴿and mercy﴾, that is, a great honour through the imamate, reaching perfection and radiance to a degree beyond which there is no increase. This is for the prophets, peace be upon them. And since no one benefits from their lights except those who turn towards them, and the benefit from them varies with the variation in degrees of turning towards them and attending to them, He said: ﴿for the believers﴾, those who followed him and who are firmly rooted in turning towards the guides and submitting to them, and that was the cause of their salvation. The Imam indicated this and said: These are intellectual degrees and demonstrative ranks, indicated by these four Qur'anic words, in a manner in which none of them can be delayed from its place or moved forward. This is in contrast to what they attributed to him (ﷺ) of magic, for that is a disease entirely and an error that leads to misery. And *al-maw'izah* (admonition) is an explanation that calls to righteousness by way of desire and fear [p. 146]. *Al-wa'z* (exhortation) is that which calls to humility, devotion and turning away from wickedness and sin. *Al-shifa'* (healing) is the removal of disease, and the disease of ignorance is more harmful than the disease of the body; its treatment is more difficult, its physicians fewer, and healing from it more exalted. *Al-sadr* (breast) is the place of the heart, and it is the most exalted place in a living being because of the nobility of the heart. *Al-huda* (guidance) is clarification of a meaning that leads to the truth, and it is an indication that leads to knowledge. *Al-rahmah* (mercy) is a blessing upon one in need.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 58:

When this was established, he urged them towards it, because of its distance from magic, given its steadfastness and the inability to shake it, let alone remove it; and because it is a healing, an admonition, a guidance and a mercy. Thus it encompasses all the degrees of nearness to God. He also made them renounce the worldly trash they were turning towards, because of its sharing with magic in the swiftness of change and transformation, through passing away and vanishing. So it is [deserving of] renunciation and turning away from it. Thus God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "In the bounty of God and in His mercy"﴾, to the end of the verse. It was most fitting that this be followed by His saying: ﴿He gives life and causes death﴾ [Yunus: 56], because of the swift departure mentioned from it. Also, the Qur'an gives life to the dead of ignorance: whoever turns to it, it bestows knowledge and wisdom upon him, so it is to the heart what life is to the body; and whoever turns away from it becomes in error and confusion and arrives at everlasting destruction. Thus turning away from it is causing death to him.

Abu Hayyan made the object of the preposition in "bi-fadlihi" (in His bounty) an omitted element, its estimated form being: ﴿Say﴾ so that they rejoice ﴿in the bounty of God﴾, that is, the Supreme King, ﴿and in His mercy﴾. Then he coordinated the restriction of joy to that: ﴿then in that﴾, that is, the very great matter alone, if they rejoice at anything at all, ﴿let them rejoice﴾. Thus these are two sentences. He said: this is more apparent. The benefit of the second is restricting joy to that, rather than to what they take pleasure in of worldly trash, (p-147) because spiritual felicities are superior to bodily felicities.

Then he stated the cause of joy, saying: ﴿It is﴾, that is, what has been spoken of of bounty and mercy, ﴿better than what they accumulate﴾, that is: than the trash of this world, even if it is the most noble of its goods, while they are constantly engaged in it through the succession of times; and the rational person chooses the superior for his effort. Bounty (fadl) is an increase in blessing; and joy (farah) is a pleasure in the heart at attaining the desired.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 59:**

When He described the Mighty Qur'an as a healing, together with what it carries that necessitates the straightness of paths, the soundness of laws, and the clarity of doctrines, and indicated that the intelligent person should single it out for joy because its traces remain, because of what it calls to, because of his renunciation of what they gather for its perishing, and because it calls to base moral qualities and thereby brings down one from the summit of lofty things, He indicated that just as they blundered in joy, singling out for it what perishes while turning away from what remains, so too they blundered in the path of gathering. They bound themselves by vow to [what they called] lawful and unlawful, forbidding themselves some of what He had made lawful. They withheld from themselves what they rejoice in, without any command from Allah, the Exalted. Thereby they diminished their share in this world through this prohibition, and in the Hereafter through their lying against their Lord in forbidding it, since they made it a religiously approved law, while it is in the utmost corruption, far from the truth, and falling short of the stages of rectitude. So the Exalted said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to these people who mock you, a mockery by which He judges against them that they have no intellects, mocking them and rebuking them with a rebuke that is in the most judicious of its places. He framed it in the form of a question, such that they [in the matter] are unable to answer at all except by acknowledging the fabrication: ﴿Tell me﴾, that is, inform me. He expressed the creating [of provision] by the word "sending down," as an alert that it is something whose attribution to their idols is impossible, since the causes of it do not descend from any place with which they have any connection whatsoever. So He said: ﴿what Allah has sent down﴾, that is, He who possesses the attributes of perfection, among which is absolute self-sufficiency, ﴿for you﴾, that is, specifically for you, ﴿of provision﴾, that is, whatever provision it was, ﴿and you have made of it﴾, that is, of that provision which He bestowed upon you, ﴿lawful and unlawful﴾, in the manner whose account has preceded in al-An'am and elsewhere, and the explanation of its corruption, though it is manifestly corrupt and plainly crooked. Then He began another matter, as emphasis on the denunciation against them, and said: ﴿Say﴾, that is: who permitted you to do that? ﴿Has Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, ﴿permitted you﴾, so that you may establish the authority for it? ﴿Or﴾ has He not permitted you in it, even though you attribute it to Him, because you have divided it into lawful and unlawful, while none makes lawful or unlawful except Allah? So you, ﴿against Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing everything in greatness and knowledge, ﴿are fabricating﴾, while you attribute the fabrication to Me in this Qur'an, which has overwhelmed thoughts, and in this law which has dazzled minds, and while you claim that you are the furthest of people from absolute lying and the purest of them in their skirts from it. The placing of the prepositional phrase first indicates an increase in the reproach against them, since they are the most disassociated of people from lying, and yet they have singled out Allah, assuming the concession to them, by deliberately lying against Him.

(p-148)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 60:

Since the proofs of the Resurrection that have already passed have made it as clear as the sun, and since their fabrication has been established by their inability to produce any authority from God permitting them to say it, he said, indicating (p-149) that the Resurrection is among the things that are known and whose denial is not permissible: ﴿And what do those who fabricate lies against God think, on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ That is, those who deliberately ﴿fabricate against God﴾, that is, the Supreme King, ﴿the lie﴾, that is, that it will not befall them ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾. That is: suppose you were not ashamed before Him and did not fear His consequences in this world, then what do you think will happen on that Day? Do you think that He will not call you to account, so that He would then have done what no lord does with his subject?

Since He, exalted is He, deals with them with forbearance while they persist in this disobedience, He said: ﴿Indeed, God﴾, that is, the One to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿is truly full of bounty﴾, that is, great bounty, ﴿toward mankind﴾, that is, with blessings, among them the sending down of Books in which He has detailed what He is pleased with and what He is displeased with, and the sending of Messengers, upon them be peace, to explain them in a manner that the minds of creation can bear, and among them the prolonging of their respite despite their evil deeds, so that gratitude to Him was obligatory upon them. ﴿But most of them﴾, that is, of mankind, because of the disorder of their inner selves, ﴿do not give thanks﴾, that is, no gratitude renews from them. So they do not follow His Messengers or His Books, and they stumble about blindly, so they do what angers Him, glorified is He.

And ﴿tahrim﴾ (prohibition): the establishing of the meaning of forbidding an act; ﴿tahlil﴾ (permission): the lifting of the meaning of prohibition by permission; ﴿shukr﴾ (gratitude): a right that becomes obligatory through a blessing, consisting of acknowledging it and acting upon what it calls for in proportion to its magnitude; and ﴿iftira'﴾ (fabrication) of a lie: its forging and embellishing, so it is more heinous than a lie in general.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 61:

When He had described the Qur'an with what He described it with, namely healing and what accompanies it, after establishing the proof of its inimitability (i'jaz), and had indicated that what they follow in religion is utterly confused, and that, being false, it is something every one of them can change for something better, since it is not founded on wisdom, He concluded all that with a warning to them against fabricating lies in legislating what Allah did not permit, while they claim the Qur'an is fabricated and they are unable to produce its equal (mu'arada), and with [a warning] that they have not given thanks for His blessings, the greatest of which is singling them out with this wise Reminder and upright law. He had repeated in all of that the command to him, ﷺ, to dispute with them: ﴿Say: I possess no power over myself﴾ [Yunus: 49], ﴿Say: Tell me, if His punishment comes upon you﴾ [Yunus: 50], ﴿Say: Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true﴾ [Yunus: 53], ﴿Say: By the grace of Allah﴾ [Yunus: 58], and so on.

﴿Say: Tell me, what Allah has sent down for you﴾ [Yunus: 59], ﴿Say: Has Allah permitted you?﴾ [Yunus: 59]. He, exalted is He, said, looking back to His words: ﴿It was not possible for this Qur'an to be fabricated﴾ [Yunus: 37], and so on, as consolation for him, ﷺ, as strengthening of his resolve, and as an increase in the warning to them, in continuation of what is implied as its sense: "Indeed We have sent down to them through your tongue that which is an honour for them and a blessing upon them, and which is in the utmost remoteness from any falsehood whatsoever, for every part of it is in its most firm place and its best, and falsehood cannot approach it in any way, while they meet His blessing with disbelief." ﴿And you are not﴾ [you] ﴿engaged in any affair﴾, i.e., whatever affair it may be, ﴿nor do you recite from it﴾, i.e., from the Qur'an spoken of throughout this whole surah, which, as has preceded, they denied without any basis for doubt, ﴿any portion of Qur'an﴾, i.e., little or much, ﴿nor do you do any deed﴾, i.e., all of you, obedient or disobedient, ﴿but We are witnesses over you when you are engaged in it﴾, i.e., acting by the comprehensiveness of Our knowledge and the agency of Our hosts, acting as a witness acts. This is an announcement that you are under Our eye in all these exchanges and other of your affairs, and that I know your management and am able to support you. All of this is from My Book, before which powers are diminished and thoughts stand back from matching it, because it is wise, being from Me; so it is exalted above any opposition at all, in wording or in meaning, let alone alteration, let alone producing its like, let alone something better than it, owing to the soundness of its matter and the harmony of its rulings, which make it a healing and a guidance [and a mercy]. Whatever is like this is from Me with certainty and by My permission beyond doubt, because I know the immersing in it and the separating from it, and all the matters that occur from you, from them, and from others.

Since perhaps someone might suppose, from the implication of "We" (kunna) and "witnesses" (shuhudan) regarding the hosts, that He, glorified is He, needs them, He negated that with His words: ﴿And not﴾, i.e., while the situation is that He is not ﴿hidden﴾, i.e., not absent [or concealed] ﴿from your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who nurtures every creature by His general bounties and you by His particular blessings and most noble gifts. He went to the extreme in negation and said: ﴿of the weight of an atom﴾, i.e., the weight of a very small ant, and the place of its weight and its time. Since "fi" (in) is measured by the standard of the people of the earth, it was more fitting to put it first, so He said: ﴿on earth﴾. And since the context did not leave room for the plural, as will come in Saba', He said, being satisfied with the singular that indicates the genus: ﴿nor in heaven﴾, i.e., whatever is above the earth, whatever it may be.

Since rigidity may lead some dullards to take the "atom" (mithqal) literally and to be ignorant that what is meant by it is emphasis, He said, conjoining to the sentence from its beginning, and it is in the nominative (al-ibtida') whether we read the two r's with the reading of Hamzah and Ya'qub or put them in the accusative according to the rest: ﴿nor less than that﴾, i.e., than the weight of the atom, ﴿nor greater﴾. When He brought this comprehensive and encompassing beginning, He informed about it with His words: ﴿but﴾, i.e., nothing of that is except that it exists ﴿in a Book﴾, i.e., a comprehensive one, ﴿clear﴾, i.e., evident in itself and making clear everything in it, [and what completes this place will come in Saba']. In this there is a warning to them and a steadying of him, ﷺ. And it becomes apparent from this that what follows "illa" (except) is a circumstantial clause (hal) of the agent: meaning, He does not do any thing except that you are before Our eyes. Thus it is established that the Qur'an is by His knowledge, so if anyone were to fabricate it against Him, He would have allowed it.

Al-ifadah (immersing): entering into the work in a manner of pouring into it, which is spreading oneself in the work, taken from the overflow of a vessel when what is in it pours out from its sides. Afadtum: you dispersed, like the dispersal of water that spills from a vessel. Al-‘uzub (absence): the departure of meaning from knowledge, and its opposite is presence. Al-dharr: the tiny ants, which are very light in weight, and its mithqal: its weight.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 10, verses 62–63:**

When it had preceded that He, glory be to Him, has all-encompassing knowledge, and it was known, from the arrangement of conditions (p-153) that what cannot be contained, and whoever (or whatever) the earth cannot contain merely by their names, is in a Clear Book (*kitab mubin*), meaning that whatever is uncovered from it is found without concealment and without any need for searching, that He has complete power, after it had preceded that they are two groups: one truthful in His command, and one who fabricates against Him; and that He bestows favour upon people by not hastening (punishment) and by deferring it until the Resurrection; and He warned the fabricator of the consequences of his affair, both in this world and in the next, and gave hope to the obedient, it was a fitting point at which someone might say: "I wish I knew, with certainty, what the detailed condition of the two groups will be in both abodes?" So it was answered that the friends (of God) are successful and the enemies are destroyed, so that every obedient person may roll up the sleeve of his effort (*tashammir ʿan saʿid jiddihi*), and exert the utmost of his striving in attaining the sincere ones and avoiding the side of the fabricators, by His words, exalted be He, emphasising their belief that they (the enemies) will destroy the party of God, and their denial, to the utmost degree of denial, that they could escape them:

﴿Surely the friends of God—there is no fear for them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ That is, those who take as their friend, through obedience, the One than whom nothing is more mighty or greater, [and He takes them as friends]. ﴿There is no fear﴾, that is: a fixed, lofty (fear) ﴿upon them﴾, that is: of anything that may confront them. ﴿Nor do they grieve﴾, that is: in their inner selves, there is not renewed for them a grief over something lost; because their hearts are attached to God, glory be to Him, so no fear or grief affects them in a way that cuts their hearts apart, as it befalls others. He explained them by His words: ﴿those who believe﴾, that is: they brought into being this quality that validates deeds, and with it is the completeness of the *quwwa ʿilmiyya* (the cognitive power, i.e., the power of knowledge), ﴿and who were﴾, that is: a state that became for them a disposition and a character, ﴿mindful of God﴾, that is: they bring about *taqwa* (God-consciousness), which is the completeness of the *quwwa ʿamaliyya* (the practical power, i.e., the power of action) in faith and deeds, and they renew it. For no one can truly estimate God as He ought to be estimated. The answer concludes with His words: ﴿Indeed, those who fabricate lies against God will not succeed﴾ [Yunus: 69], and so on. What God explained the friends by is beyond any increase in its excellence. And it is related from ʿAli, may God be pleased with him: "They are a people with faces yellowed from vigil, eyes dimmed from weeping, and bellies hollowed from hunger." It was also said: "The friend (*wali*) is one who does not show off and does not feign piety," and how few are the friends of one whose character is this.

It is authentically related from the two Imams, Abu Hanifa and al-Shafiʿi, as al-Shaykh Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi transmitted from them in the introduction to his commentary on *al-Muhadhdhab* and in *al-Tibyan*, that each of them said: "If the scholars are not the friends of God, then God has no friend." This applies to the scholar who acts upon his knowledge, as I have explained when commenting on His words in Surat al-Zumar: ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [al-Zumar: 9].

When it had preceded that He, glory be to Him, has all-encompassing knowledge, and it was known, from the arrangement of conditions (p-153) that what cannot be contained, and whoever (or whatever) the earth cannot contain merely by their names, is in a Clear Book (*kitab mubin*), meaning that whatever is uncovered from it is found without concealment and without any need for searching, that He has complete power, after it had preceded that they are two groups: one truthful in His command, and one who fabricates against Him; and that He bestows favour upon people by not hastening (punishment) and by deferring it until the Resurrection; and He warned the fabricator of the consequences of his affair, both in this world and in the next, and gave hope to the obedient, it was a fitting point at which someone might say: "I wish I knew, with certainty, what the detailed condition of the two groups will be in both abodes?" This applies to the scholar who acts upon his knowledge, as I have explained when commenting on His words in Surat al-Zumar: ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [al-Zumar: 9].

When he had negated fear and sorrow for them, he added to that, saying [clarifying his taking them as allies after having explained their taking him as their ally]: ﴿For them﴾, i.e., exclusively, ﴿is good news﴾, i.e., complete, ﴿in the worldly life﴾, i.e., that their religion will prevail, their condition will become renowned, their enemy will be humiliated, and their deeds will not be accepted [and through true dreams]. ﴿And in the Hereafter﴾, [it is good news] that they are the happy ones and their enemies are the wretched, and that the angels will receive them: ﴿This is your day which you were promised﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103]. Since the prevailing condition of the people of God in this world is hardship, especially at the beginning of Islam, a listener to this might be inclined to say, "Would that I knew whether this happiness will be fulfilled!" So it was said, "Yes," and it was emphasized by negating the genus, because the tyrants deny this [for them], seeing that their might is behind a humiliation that contains no evil, by the falsehood of the arrogant, through deception, rumor-spreading, and assault: ﴿There is no changing﴾, i.e., in any way whatsoever, ﴿of the words of God﴾, i.e., the Supreme King who encompasses everything in knowledge and power. His saying ﴿That﴾, i.e., this exalted matter, ﴿is﴾, i.e., exclusively, ﴿the great triumph﴾ is in the place of explanation and disclosure of the content of this good news. Fear (khawf) is the agitation of the heart from what is anticipated of harm; its counterparts are jaza' (anxiety) and faza' (alarm), and its opposite is security (amn). Sorrow (huzn) is the heart's agitation and heaviness of concern over what harm has occurred, from the word huzn (rough, stony ground), and its opposite is joy (surur); both alternate in the state of the living person who remembers the beloved. Good news (bushra) is the first report by which its joy appears in the surface of the face.

(p-155)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 65:

When the good news of the removal of fear and grief together from the awliya' (the friends of God) had been mentioned, it is known that the meaning is: this good news is for the awliya', and you are their head, so do not fear. Thereupon He joined to it His saying: ﴿And let not their speech grieve you﴾, [that is] such as their saying that they will overcome, and their denial of you, their mockery of you, and their threats against you. For that is speech by which they intend to change the words of God, the Self-Sufficient, the All-Powerful, and far is that from the weak, poor one; how much more so from the Exalted, the Great! This is what the reasoning given for this prohibition points to, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, all might﴾, that is, victory, dominance, and perfect majesty, ﴿belongs to God﴾, that is, the Supreme King, in its entirety, ﴿all of it﴾, meaning: He will humble them and grant might to His religion. The purpose of this is consolation concerning their speech with which they harm him.

When the verse began with their saying, He concluded it with hearing it and knowing it, and restricted both to Him, because the attributes of every described being are insignificant in comparison with His attributes. So He said: ﴿He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, that is, He alone is the one who hears their words with perfect hearing, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, that is, the one whose knowledge encompasses their inner thoughts and all their states. He is the one whose power reaches everything, so He will requite them according to what is due. This is a reason for His exclusive possession of might, since He is singled out by these two attributes, and they are negated from others; and whoever is devoid of them is below the dumb animals, so how could he have might? Might is the capacity to overcome every tyrant in a way that cannot be attacked or wronged. The meaning is that He will make you mighty against whoever opposes you. The prohibition in ﴿And let not ... grieve you﴾ is, in wording, directed at the speech, and in meaning at the cause that leads to being harmed by the speech. The "inna" here is pronounced with a kasra for resumption (isti'naf), by reminding of what negates grief, not because it follows a verb of saying, since it is not a report from them. It has also been read with a fatha, in the sense of "because" (li-anna).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 66:

When the verse was concluded with the all-encompassing scope of His hearing and knowledge, after restricting might to Him alone, it was as if it had been said: "Might is not complete except through power." So He affirmed His exclusive possession of dominion, which cannot exist except through power. He said, emphasizing what their associating partners entail of denial of the content of this statement: ﴿Surely to Allah belongs﴾, i.e., the One who possesses complete encompassing. Since some people had associated partners with some of the stars, He gathered them together and said, expressing with the particle used for rational beings a clarification of what the earlier expression, using the particle for others, had conveyed: ﴿whoever is in the heavens﴾, i.e., all of them. He began with them because their dominion indicates dominion over the earth by way of priority. Then he explicitly mentioned them in His saying, emphasizing what preceded: ﴿and whoever is on the earth﴾, i.e., all of them, (p-157) are His servants, their kings and those below them, His governance is executed over them, and they are submissive to what He wills. This is also a second justification for His saying: ﴿And let not their saying grieve you﴾ [Yunus: 65], or for the exclusivity of might. He expressed with "man" (مَن), which is used for rational beings, while the intended meaning is everything in existence, because the context is the negation of might from other than Him, and rational beings are more worthy of it, so negating it from them is negation from others by way of priority. Then they were given precedence due to their nobility over others. For this reason "má" (ما), which is for non-rational beings, is used in a context where it is more appropriate, and then the general sense is intended by it, giving precedence to the majority that does not reason over the minority. Then He negated that He has any partner in this by His saying, conjoining it to what is implied: so He has no partner in what the polytheists claimed of either of them or of one of them: ﴿And those who call upon﴾, i.e., with utmost effort, ﴿besides Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses all greatness, ﴿partners﴾ in reality. It is also permissible that "má" (ما) be a relative pronoun, belittling the partners by expressing them with the particle for what does not reason, and conjoined to "man" (مَن): ﴿do not follow﴾, i.e., they do not follow in that which is the foundation of the foundations of religion, where certainty is required, namely their calling upon them as partners. ﴿except conjecture﴾, i.e., what is erroneous, given that even if it were correct they would be mistaken in it, since they were content at the root with conjecture. Then He alerted to the error by His saying: ﴿and they are only guessing﴾, i.e., they only estimate that and say what has no reality at all. Ittiba' (اتّباع, following) is seeking to catch up with the first, according to the state of affairs. These people followed the one calling to the worship of idols and conducted themselves with him in what he called to, (p-158) and their conjecture in worshipping them is only based on a weak resemblance, such as intending to increase the exaltation of God and exalting the imitation of forefathers. It is also permissible that "shuraka'" (شُرَكاءَ, partners) be an object governed by both "yattabi'" (يَتَّبِعُ) and "yad'una" (يَدْعُونَ).

Then He, glory be to Him, established His exclusive possession of a comprehensive attribute of knowledge and power, as confirmation of His exclusive possession of might and His singularity in unity. And whoever associates others with Him is a guesser (kharis) with no knowledge in any respect, given the abundance and clarity of the proofs of His oneness. So He said: ﴿He is the One who made for you﴾, i.e., He alone, ﴿who made﴾, i.e., by means of the revolving of the spheres which He perfected, ﴿for you﴾, i.e., as a favour from Him, ﴿the night﴾, i.e., dark, ﴿that you may rest therein﴾, as rest for you and as a sign of His glory's power over bringing into being and annihilation, and as a comfort for those who love their Lord. ﴿And the day﴾: he attributed to the cause the description of the effect, so He said: ﴿giving sight﴾, i.e., so that you may move about in it. He omitted the description of the night and mentioned its purpose, the reverse of what He did with the day, so that what is affirmed indicates what is omitted; the verse is therefore of the type called ihtibak (mutual omission).

And since these signs are so manifest that one needs nothing more than hearing them, He said: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people﴾, i.e., the great matter, ﴿for a people﴾, i.e., who have the capacity to strive toward what they want, ﴿who hear﴾, i.e., who have sound hearing. In this there are clear proofs that He alone is exclusively possessed of might, so there is no partner for Him, because a partner must necessarily share with his partner some of the actions, the states, or the ownership. When all of that is absent, the absence of partnership is too evident to require any proof. It is also possible that the meaning is: signs for a people who see with the sight of reflection (i'tibar) (p-159) and hear with the hearing of contemplation and remembrance; but He omitted "they see" because of the indication of ﴿giving sight﴾ upon it. The context of negating partners adds to this [clarity and] beauty, for it indicates that they neither hear nor see at all, so how could they reflect and ponder? Those who worshipped them are therefore in a more complete state than they are.

They said, "God has taken a son" — that is, he undertook to take one through causation, as we are accustomed to. "God" — that is, the One named by this name, which requires that He possess all perfection, so that He is in no way in need of anything. "A son" — as an explanation of His saying, "They follow nothing but conjecture" [Yunus: 66]. This is apt for being an expression of wonder at those who claimed it of the angels, or of 'Uzayr, or of the Messiah, or others.

When He marveled at them in this, because it contradicts what it implies of deficiency, given what is established for God Most High of perfection, as has passed, He exalted His noble self above it, saying: "Glory be to Him" — that is, He is exalted above every trace of deficiency, with complete exaltation. Then He gave the reason for His exaltation above it and explained it with His saying: "He is" — that is, alone — "the Self-Sufficient" — that is, free of need for a son and other than him, because He is a single being, exalted above parts, components and similarity. Then He explained His self-sufficiency with His saying: "To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens" — and since the context of the argument requires emphasis, He repeated "what" and said: "and whatever is on the earth," of the silent and the speaking. So He is self-sufficient by owning all of that, so that nothing of it could be a son to Him, for a son is not owned, and the lack of ownership is a deficiency incompatible with self-sufficiency. (p-160) Perhaps He expressed it with "what" because self-sufficiency is focused on the silent, while the term also includes the speaking.

When He had clarified with decisive proof and manifest, radiant evidence the impossibility of His having a son, He rebuked them by denying that they had any kind of argument for this, saying: "You have no authority" — that is, no proof — "for this" — that is, this taking — and he went to the extreme in negation, saying: "from any authority," that is, proof. Proof was called "authority" because the hand of the one holding to it is raised over others. Then He increased their rebuke by denouncing them, saying: "Do you say" — that is, repeatedly — "about God" — that is, the Supreme King [in the manner of elevation] — "what you do not know?" Because whatever has no proof for it [in the principles of jurisprudence] is ignorance, so how much more so what evidence has established to be contrary to it. And "sultan" means the overpowering proof, because one prevails through it over the soundness of a matter and the opponent is subdued by it; its origin is the one who rules over subjects by the bond of governance.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 69:

When he had first stated that their saying was a lie, and rebuked them for it directly, he followed it with something that points to their being deserving of being turned away from, in a context that threatens those who lie. So he said, turning away from addressing them, emphasizing (the point) because their audacity in doing this indicates denial of being held accountable for it: ﴿Say﴾, i.e., to those who claimed that God has a son and who forbade what He had provided them of the sa'iba (a free-roaming she-camel) and the like: ﴿Indeed, those who invent lies﴾, i.e., who deliberately do so, ﴿against God﴾, i.e., the Supreme King, ﴿the lie, will not prosper﴾.

Then he explained their failure to prosper by His saying: ﴿A brief enjoyment﴾ [for them], and He made it indefinite to indicate its scantiness, as He said in another verse: ﴿A little enjoyment﴾ [al-Nahl: 117]. He emphasized this by His saying: ﴿in the world﴾, because it is an abode of departure, and whatever is headed toward cessation, dissolution and vanishing is little, even if its duration is long, its periods extended, and its span great, and its number exceeds counting. Then He explained their condition after the transfer by His saying: ﴿Then﴾, i.e., after that respite granted to them, however long it lasts, ﴿to Us﴾, i.e., according to what We possess of greatness, not to other than Us, ﴿is their return﴾ by death, whereupon ﴿We will make them taste a severe punishment﴾, though it is less than the punishment of the Hereafter. ﴿Then We will make them taste﴾ on the Day of Resurrection ﴿the severe punishment, because﴾ i.e., because of what ﴿they used to﴾ i.e., a state that has become their innate disposition ﴿disbelieve﴾. The "inna" must be pronounced with a kasra after the verb of saying, because it is a report of something whose informing is being newly begun, just as it was done with the lam of initiation (lam al-ibtida') for this reason.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 71:**

When their demand for the bringing of the signs they proposed had come before, and the indication had passed that their being carried in the ship is among the greatest of signs, even though, through their familiarity with it [with it, they had] forgotten this, and the verses interlinked as has preceded, until this [passage] made clear that the enjoyment of those who fabricate lies is brief, as a warning against the severity of the punishment and the greatness of the seizing, He followed that with the story of the people of Noah, because they were the longest-lived of the wrongdoing nations and the most numerous in count. Then they were seized with the most severe seizing, so their traces vanished, their markers and landmarks were effaced, and they became as though they had never existed at all, nor had uttered a saying (p. 162) or done a deed. So the Exalted said, linking to His statement ﴿Say: Indeed, those who﴾ [Yunus: 69], consoling His Prophet ﷺ and his Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, because when a calamity is general it becomes lighter, and warning the disbelievers so that they might return or lighten their harm to them: ﴿And recite﴾, that is, read in continuous succession and with authority, ﴿to them the news of Noah﴾, that is, his great report, reminding of the first existence of the ship, and that it was then a strange sign, breaking the usual order, wondrous, and that the people of Noah were not benefited by it, nor did their fabrication and obstinacy avail them, despite the lengthening of the period and the distance of the spans. Rather, their affair came to an end, with a harsh seizing and a punishment ﴿as if they had not stayed but an hour of the day, recognizing one another﴾ [Yunus: 45], along with the deliverance of their messenger and the frustration of what they had hoped for. He remained among them for what no prophet had remained among his people, nor any messenger among his nation: a thousand years less fifty years, and none believed with him except a few. ﴿When he said to his people﴾, that is, after he had called them to Allah and prolonged his calling to them, and they were given enjoyment in the world abundantly and were granted a long respite, yet that only increased them in aversion. ﴿O my people﴾, that is, O you whose opposition to me is grievous and whose displeasure hurts me, because of their negligence toward the right of their Lord despite their capacity for obedience. ﴿If it has been grievous to you﴾, that is, it has been hard and great, a hardship that has become a natural disposition, ﴿my standing﴾. Since the custom of preachers and orators is to stand during the sermon, he said ﴿my standing﴾, that is, my standing up. Perhaps he singled out this verbal noun because it suits the place and time of standing, so the report of his dislike of it, on account of the standing that occurred, is more indicative of his dislike of standing (p. 163). ﴿and my reminding﴾, that is, of you, ﴿by the signs of Allah﴾, that is, of the One who possesses majesty and honour. This does not hold me back from striving against you with what is grievous to you from that, out of fear of you, because Allah has commanded me to do so, and I fear His punishment if I abandon it. I am not concerned with your dislike of that, out of fear of the consequence of your intention to harm me. ﴿Then upon﴾, that is, then I am upon ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom all might belongs, alone, ﴿I have relied﴾. The placing of this in the position of the response is a metonymy of the cause (majaz mursal, a figurative usage in which a part or cause stands for the whole or effect), namely reliance, for the effect, namely the absence of fear. It is a notice to them of the greatness of Allah and their insignificance, because they turned away from the signs while knowing them, as indicated by the expression "reminding," and this indicates their obstinacy in falsehood. The one who acts in falsehood is not to be feared, because falsehood has no permanence. This is shown by His statement: ﴿So resolve upon your affair﴾, that is, concerning harming me by destruction or otherwise. Determine it, intend it, and be firm about it. The waw in His statement ﴿and your partners﴾ has the meaning of "with," to show that he does not fear them even if their partners are living beings, whoever they may be, and their word is one without any division among them in any respect.

Since the one who conceals his affairs may miss some of his aims by the condition of concealment, he informed them that he would not object to them, whether they reveal or conceal. So he said: ﴿Then let not your affair be﴾, that is, after the reluctance and the long time spent in consultation, ﴿upon you a cover﴾, that is, something hidden, concealed from you, some part of which is hidden because you keep it from me, so that I would not strive to oppose you. So do not do that, but proclaim it to me openly (p. 164) [openly], for there is no opposition from me except to Allah, to whom secrecy and openness are equal. The expression "then" indicates deliberation and mastery of the affair, for security against any opposition to it by some power or strength from Him. ﴿Then carry out﴾ [what you intend, that is, finish it decisively, reaching its object] ﴿to me﴾.

Since this was apparent in the execution but not explicit, he made it explicit in His statement: ﴿And do not give me respite﴾, that is, for any moment at all. All of this serves to show his disregard for them, relying on Allah, for nothing overpowers Him, and what they worship avails nothing.

Then he attached to that his statement: ﴿But if you turn away﴾, meaning: you have imposed upon yourselves turning away from the truth after your inability to destroy me, and your knowledge did not benefit you that the One who protected me, while I am alone, from you—though you fill the earth—belongs all might entirely, and that among His friends are those about whom His true promise has gone before, that "there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve." ﴿Then I have not﴾, meaning: your turning away was not due to any negligence on my part, because I have driven the matter in the way He loves, ﴿asked you﴾, meaning: for a moment of time, and he went to the extreme in negation and said: ﴿any reward﴾, meaning: for my calling you, which would be lost to me by your turning away, and you would not accuse me of it in your supplication.

And since it is absurd that a rational person would do something without a purpose, he clarified his purpose by his statement, resuming: ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾, meaning: I am not seeking anything except from Allah, the One who possesses the attributes of perfection. Then he joined to it another purpose, which is following the command out of fear of harm befalling (p-165), so he said: ﴿And I have been commanded﴾, meaning: by the Supreme King, to whom no one else has any command. He used the passive form to indicate that He is the one who commands, and to increase the encouragement toward what is commanded, and to give it prominence by making it the principal element of the speech through placing it in the position of the subject, so he said: ﴿that I be﴾, meaning: a state that I take on as a character, so that I never depart from it; and since he was in the position of excusing himself for suddenly confronting them with the warning, he expressed it with Islam, which is the outward acts, so he said: ﴿among the Muslims﴾, meaning: those firmly established in the attribute of submission with utmost sincerity, having for me what they have and upon me what is upon them; I and they are equal in Islam, and I have no doubt in it of which I could be accused, that I should surrender to whatever befalls me for the sake of Allah, and that does not turn me away from carrying out His command. The summary is that in his calling them he was not in a position of suspicion, nor did he ask them for any worldly purpose that would increase for him if they accepted and decrease for him if they turned away, nor did he bring anything of his own so that it could be thought he had erred in it, nor did he take a course with it by which it could be suspected that he was enslaving them to follow him; rather, he informed them that he was the first to comply with what he commanded them and to submit to what he called them to, and to whatever befalls him for the sake of Allah.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 73:

When his words did not turn them away from their error, he made the following statement a consequence of this, informing about their persistence: ﴿So they denied him.﴾ That is: none of these clear proofs and decisive evidences increased them in anything except aversion, and at the end of the period they were upon the same denial they had been upon. ﴿So We saved him﴾ — that is, a great salvation, by what We possess of dazzling majesty, because of his obedience to Our commands and the sincerity of his reliance upon Us. ﴿And those with him﴾ — that is, from the wise and others. ﴿In the ship,﴾ as We had promised Our friends, and We made (p-166) that a sign for the worlds. ﴿And We made them﴾ — that is, despite their weakness, by what We possess of majesty — ﴿successors﴾ — that is, in the earth after those whom We drowned. So whoever acts in obedience as they acted is worthy that We reward him as We rewarded them. ﴿And We drowned﴾ — that is, by what We possess of perfect might — ﴿those who denied﴾ — that is, treating Our signs lightly and with contempt ﴿Our signs,﴾ just as We threatened those who fabricate lies against God.

Since this was a dazzling matter from which whoever has insight is admonished, he made a consequence of it the command to the one of highest understanding of creation to look carefully, indicating that no one other than him is to draw true lessons from it. So He said: ﴿Then look﴾, and He indicated that he is fit to have his affair investigated by the interrogative particle, and He increased the matter in greatness by mentioning the state, so He said: ﴿how was﴾ [that is, a state that was as if it were innate] ﴿the end﴾ [that is, the final outcome of the matter of] ﴿those who were warned﴾ [that is, those who were immersed in this description, namely those whom the messengers warned, but they were not fit for good tidings because they did not believe], so that we would know that whomever We warn in such a way, and whom We intend to be wretched among them, the sending down of a sign or the clarification of proof does not benefit him. Tawakkul (reliance): deliberately placing a matter in the hands of one who manages it, relying on him in his management. Ghumma (distress): the narrowness of a matter that necessitates sorrow. Tawalli (turning away): going away from a thing. Ajr (reward): the benefit deserved through action. Islam: submission to the command of God by obeying Him, since it is the best thing that servants can acquire.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 74:

Since the stories of those who came between him and Musa, peace be upon them, contained nothing suited to the aim of this surah except what they shared with the people of Nuh (Noah), namely that the signs did not benefit those whose wretchedness God had willed among them, He mentioned it, omitting what was beyond it, and said, exalted is He: ﴿Then﴾, meaning, after a long period, ﴿We sent﴾, meaning, by Our greatness. Since sending did not occupy the whole span of the interval, He introduced the preposition and said: ﴿after him﴾, meaning [the people of] Nuh, ﴿messengers﴾, such as Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut and Shu'ayb, upon them be prayers and peace.

Since it might be thought that a people would not reject their own human messenger, or that if they rejected him they would not persist in rejection, especially if he brought them what they demanded of extraordinary signs, He said: ﴿to their people﴾, meaning, so their people were taken by surprise with denial, ﴿and they came to them﴾, meaning, as a consequence of their reliance on Our greatness, they came to them ﴿with the clear proofs﴾ so that their denial would be removed and they would believe. ﴿But they were not﴾, meaning, as a consequence of that, the opposite of what they had been commanded and the evidence for it had been established, namely that in no way whatsoever of existence were they ﴿to believe﴾, meaning, acknowledging, ﴿in what they had denied﴾, meaning, treating it with contempt, ﴿at first when it came to them.﴾ Since their denial occurred over part of past time, He introduced the preposition and said: ﴿before﴾, meaning before the coming of the clear proofs, ﴿because We had sealed their hearts﴾. Abu Hayyan said: the negation came accompanied by the lam of denial (lam al-juhud, the emphatic negating particle), to show that their belief lay within the realm of impossibility and impediment, and he ended.

It is permissible that the intended meaning is: before the coming of the messengers to them, and the denial was attributed to them because their fathers had denied when they altered the correct religion that the messengers had brought them, and they were content with what their fathers had innovated, considering it good; or because there remained among them remnants upon remnants of what the messengers had prescribed, so they would admonish them regarding what they innovated, but they neither heeded nor listened, just as Qass ibn Sa'ida, Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Waraqa [ibn Nawfal] and others existed before the prophet (ﷺ) was sent. But the first meaning is preferable, and God knows best.

Since He established that they did not benefit from the signs, He built what follows upon a question that might arise in one's mind: did creation continue to be like this among those who came after them? So it is as if it were said: yes! ﴿Thus﴾, meaning, just as We sealed their hearts with this great seal, ﴿We seal﴾, meaning, We bring about the seal and renew it whenever We will, by the greatness We possess, ﴿upon the hearts of the transgressors﴾ in every age, for everyone who deliberately exceeds the bounds in what is not lawful for him,

This is as when Moses, peace be upon him, came to Pharaoh and called him to God, and he denied him. Moses informed him that he had with him a sign confirming him. Pharaoh said to him: "If you have come with a sign, then bring it, if you are among the truthful." When Moses brought it to him, Pharaoh persisted in his denial, and whenever he saw a sign, his denial increased. Pharaoh's kingdom had grown strong, his authority had become great, he had risen in his arrogance, and his tyranny over the weak had lasted long. So his wealth and his monuments were obliterated, while his tales and his reports remained. For this reason, God, glorified is He, made the story plain, saying, [indicating the impression]: ﴿Then We sent﴾, that is, after a long time had passed since We destroyed them, We sent ﴿after them﴾, that is, after those messengers, ﴿Moses﴾. Because the span of time was not so extended as to exhaust the sense of distance, He used the preposition and said ﴿after them﴾. (p-١٦٩) ﴿Moses﴾ And likewise We sent ﴿Aaron﴾ as a support for him, because the agreement of two is stronger in what they establish and firmer in what they convey. Since it had become fixed in minds from what had passed that the custom of nations is to deny one who comes from among them out of envy and jealousy of him, one might have supposed that if the Messenger had come to other than his own people, the matter would have been different. So He made clear that the situation is one in both the near and the distant, and He said, placing first ﴿to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾, that is, the nobles of his people, for the common folk follow them, ﴿with Our signs﴾ [that is] which cannot be fully grasped in their greatness, because they are attributed to Us. Yet We set a seal upon their hearts. ﴿But they were arrogant﴾, that is, they sought greatness and refused to accept the signs, and they produced what indicates rejection, due to his being sent to them after that. ﴿And they were﴾, that is, by nature and disposition, ﴿a guilty people﴾, that is, their nature is to sever what should be joined and to join what should be severed. Therefore they dared to be arrogant. Along with this there is also a strong relevance to what preceded in the words of the disbelievers: "This is clear magic," in attributing magic to Moses, peace be upon him, and in explaining the reality of magic in its vanishing and the failure of its practitioner in his corruption, and other secrets that are too subtle for thoughts. Added to this is the relevance linking the destruction of the Copts and the people of Noah through the sign of drowning, and that the sight of the signs and the witnessing of the clear proofs did not benefit anyone from either group. Rather, none believed in Moses except a small offspring of his people after those astonishing miracles and manifest proofs. Then Pharaoh pursued them after the bonds of their confinement had been loosened and the strength of his tyranny had dissolved, and he witnessed the blows that would crush mountains, (p-١٧٠) and he entered the sea in pursuit of them with a force that heroes could not approach, by what the Possessor of Majesty had decreed for him. He did not believe until the punishment came upon him, at which point faith in the unseen, which is the condition of faith, is lost. So his belief did not benefit him, despite his striving in it and his repetition of it, because its condition had been lost, in response to the prayer of Moses, peace be upon him. Furthermore, the Children of Israel were on one path before the coming of Moses, peace be upon him. They did not differ except after knowledge had come to them and the way had been made clear to them. For this purpose, Aaron, peace be upon him, is mentioned here, because among the greatest aims of the surah is the prohibition of demanding signs from one who, upon their coming, prepares to reject faith. This is a sign that the word from two is more emphatic. Yet despite this, he did not believe one whom the All-Powerful had decreed to be wretched. All of this urges contentment and submission, and entrusting the matter to the Wise Lord. Whatever He commands is to be accepted, and whatever He turns away from is left, with the questioning about it abandoned, in hope that He will arrange it in the best arrangement and decree it in the most gentle of decrees.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 76:

When Allah, glorified is He, informed of their arrogance, He made clear that it resulted in their disparaging His miracles without reflection, rather with the utmost haste and rush, as indicated by the fa' (fa, "then/so," which marks immediate consequence) and the context. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿When the truth came to them﴾, i.e., to Pharaoh and his chiefs (mala' — the council of nobles), ﴿the truth﴾, i.e., one that is thoroughly true (al-haqqiyyah, "truthfulness"). Then He increased its greatness by His saying: ﴿from Us﴾, i.e., in accordance with the greatness that is ours, by which they knew that it was from us and not from the two messengers. ﴿They said﴾, i.e., without reflecting on it or considering its matter, but rather (p-171) out of obstinacy, and as an indication of their arrogance, emphasizing what they knew of people's acceptance of it: ﴿Indeed, this is evident magic﴾, just as the people said, those whom Allah, glorified is He, informed of at the beginning of the surah, concerning this Qur'an and what accompanies it of resurrection (al-ba'th).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 77:

When they spoke, it was as if it were said: "Then what did he (Moses) answer them?" So He informed that he rejected them, by His saying: ﴿Moses said﴾. Since their repeating that statement was more deserving of denunciation, He expressed it with the present tense (al-mudari'), which indicates that they repeated it in order to erase what had been established in people's hearts of his greatness: ﴿Do you say of the truth﴾. He also drew attention to the fact that they hastened to denial without consideration or hesitation, by His saying: ﴿when it has come to you﴾, meaning: this statement which you have uttered, namely that it is sorcery. For the word "qawl" (saying) is applied to what is disliked; you say: "So-and-so said about so-and-so," meaning he disparaged him, and "so-and-so fears the qalah" (ill talk), and among people there is "taqawul" (mutual gossip). Then he repeated the denunciation by His saying: ﴿Is this sorcery?﴾, meaning: that which is in the utmost firmness and opposed to sorcery in all its attributes, so that you should say such a thing about it. Thus the verse is of ihtibak (a rhetorical device of mutual omission): the mention of "saying" in the first part indicates the omission of its like in the second, and the mention of "sorcery" in the second part indicates the omission of its like in the first.

Since the implied sense is: "Do you say this while you have already seen its success?", he built upon it His saying: ﴿And sorcerers do not prosper﴾, meaning: they do not attain what they seek at any time, ﴿the sorcerers﴾ [i.e., those who are proficient in it], because the outcome of their affair is imagining and deception in falsehoods, so success is far from them. It is also permissible that this sentence be taken as coordinated (ma'tufah) with His saying: ﴿Is this sorcery?﴾, because that interrogation carries the meaning of negation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 78:

When he (peace be upon him) denied them what manifestly distinguished the clear difference, he made clear what he had brought, namely that it is the most firmly established of things and distinct from magic, since magic has no stability whatsoever. They turned away from answering him and resorted to reporting something that implies they do not acknowledge its truth, because acknowledging it would entail abandoning the loftiness they hold, and they would not abandon it. They also led the weak to think that his purpose (peace be upon him) was arrogance, explaining their own arrogance in refusing to follow him by something that indicates there is no obstacle preventing them from it except pride. So God, may He be exalted, said, relating about them: ﴿They said﴾, i.e., denying it to him, giving two reasons: imitation (taqlid) of their forefathers, and greed for leadership (ri'asah).

Since he was the principal in the prophethood, and his brother was a follower, they made the pronoun singular and said: ﴿Have you come to us﴾, i.e., you, O Musa, ﴿to turn us﴾, i.e., to kill us and divert us, ﴿away from what we found our fathers upon﴾. They said, relying on imitation and not ashamed of abandoning evidence: ﴿our fathers﴾, in the worship of idols and the belief in nature, so let us say that as well. ﴿And that there may be for you both﴾, i.e., for you alone and your brother, [without us], ﴿grandeur﴾, i.e., through kingship, ﴿in the land﴾, i.e., the land of Egypt, which, because of its many benefits, is as if it were the whole earth. ﴿And we are not﴾, i.e., they also said: we are not ﴿believers in you both﴾, and they exaggerated in the negation, and astonishment overcame them, so they expressed it with what indicates that the matter had overwhelmed them; they knew that it was true but did not submit, so they said: ﴿believers﴾ (p-173), i.e., deeply rooted in faith. Thus it is coordinated with "Have you come to us", i.e., they said that and they said this; or it is coordinated with something like: "We will not bring you to this aim." They singled him out first with the denial concerning his coming, so that he would be weakened and his brother would withdraw from assisting him, and they associated his brother with him second, as an emphasis on that aim and a cutting off of his hope.

Al-ba'th (sending forth) means releasing someone in a matter in which he proceeds, and it is the opposite of releasing from a fetter. Al-mala' are the group who are the notables of the tribe, because their awe fills hearts at the sight of them. Al-istikbar is seeking greatness without entitlement. The mujrim is one who has acquired a great evil, from the verb jarama al-tamr (he cut the dates), when he cut them; so crime (jurm) necessarily cuts off good from its doer. Al-sihr is the presentation of a miracle by way of trickery, and clear exposition with hidden cause is likened to it. Al-haqq is that which deserves praise, whose call is urgently made by wisdom, whose benefit is great, and whose harm lies in abandoning it. Al-kibriya' is the entitlement to the attribute of greatness at its highest degree; it is an attribute of praise for God and of blame for servants, because it is incompatible with the attribute of servanthood.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 79:

When they had confused the matter by ascribing to him what they themselves were characterized by, they desired to increase the confusion by [saying] things that give the impression that what he brought was sorcery which could be countered, so as to keep the people back from following him. Thus God, Exalted is He, said, relating [their words] and linking them to His saying ﴿They said, "Have you come to us..."﴾ [Yunus: 78], ﴿And Pharaoh said﴾, desiring to contend with what Musa, peace be upon him, had brought: ﴿"Bring me every learned sorcerer."﴾ That is, one who has reached the utmost in the knowledge of sorcery, lest any part of sorcery be missed through the absence of some of it. [The reading of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i with the form fa''al (ʿAllām/sahhār pattern, "sahhār" in the intensive form), indicating an increase, is in keeping with their claim, less than the context of the poets, as has passed in al-A'raf.]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verses 80–82:

Since the implied sense is: "they obeyed his command and gathered them," the fa' in His words ﴿When the magicians came﴾ indicates the closeness of their gathering; that is, all of those from among them in the land of Egypt. ﴿Moses said to them﴾, removing this misapprehension, ﴿Throw down﴾ all ﴿that which you are about to throw﴾; that is, those who are firmly skilled in the craft of casting it. This indicates that what they have brought is not worthy of being given any attention. ﴿So when they had thrown﴾; that is, the casting took place from them with their ropes and their staffs [following his words], and by their magic they made the eyes of the people imagine what shook their minds. ﴿Moses said﴾, disapproving of them: ﴿What you have brought is﴾ [sorcery]. Then he made clear that he did not ask about it out of ignorance, but out of contempt and disapproval. He increased the clarification of both matters with his words: ﴿the sorcery﴾. Because it is also an interrogation, whether the hamzah is cut and lengthened, as in the reading of Abu 'Amr and Abu Ja'far, or made a hamzat wasl, as in the reading of the rest, the hamzat al-istifham is understood. The definite article is either for a specific reference (al-'ahd) or for the reality (al-haqiqah), and the latter is closer. It is also permissible, in the reading of the majority, for it to be a predicate of a sentence intended to restrict, meaning: it is the sorcery, not what you attribute to me. Then he resumed explaining what he belittled it with, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses comprehensive knowledge and power, ﴿will surely nullify it﴾; that is, soon, by a promise that admits no failure. Then he gave the reason for that by what he had made clear, that it is corruption, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿does not set right﴾; that is, at any time, ﴿the work of the corrupters﴾, that is, those who are wholly immersed in corruption; in that their work will not benefit and will not endure. Then he joined to it the explanation of His setting right the work of the righteous, saying: ﴿And Allah will establish﴾; that is, He will confirm with a great confirmation, ﴿the truth﴾; that is, the thing for which steadfastness is a necessary attribute. Since it was in the context of belittling them, this was indicated by repeating the all-encompassing greatest Name. He pointed to what He has of the lofty attributes with His words: ﴿by His words﴾, that is, the eternal ones, which possess the steadfastness of the Greatest. He increased the greatness with His words: ﴿though the criminals dislike it﴾; that is, the wholly immersed in severing what Allah commanded to be joined. So it was as he, peace be upon him, said: "Their sorcery was nullified, their plotting came to nothing, and the truth prevailed," as explained in Surat al-A'raf.
