When He, glorified is He, related that Musa, peace be upon him, made clear what he made clear of the falsehood of magic and that it is corruption, so that what he brought was established by its opposition to it, He informed, as consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ) and to wean him from seeking a response to the proposals (of his opponents), that nothing resulted from that at the outset, immediately after the nullification of their magic and without delay, except the faith of some weak people, not many. So the Exalted said: ﴿So none believed﴾, i.e., following ﴿Musa﴾, i.e., because of what he did, so that it is known that signs are not a cause of guidance except for whomever We wish it for. He made clear that the young are quicker to accept with His saying: ﴿except a few offspring﴾, i.e., their youths, [they] being fit for blessing to be sown among them, ﴿from among his people﴾, i.e., the people of Musa, who had the ability to take action in pursuing what they wanted. It is apparent that they were orphans, and most of them, as Mujahid said, ﴿in fear﴾, i.e., great fear, ﴿of Pharaoh and their chiefs﴾, i.e., the nobles of the people of the offspring. Since the denial of the chiefs was only because of Pharaoh's desire to strip them of their leadership, the fear was confined to him, so He indicated that by the singularity of the pronoun and said: ﴿that he would persecute them﴾. He followed it with what clarifies their excuse, saying emphatically, placing Quraysh in the position of those who deny, because of their denial that the weak companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) would be victorious over them due to their exaltedness: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh was haughty﴾, i.e., dominant and overpowering, established through what We put him to trial with, namely the people's obedience to him, ﴿in the land﴾, i.e., the land of Egypt, which, with the abundance of its amenities, is as if it were the whole earth. ﴿And indeed he was among the extravagant﴾, i.e., the foremost in transgressing limits, outwardly and inwardly. When you join this verse to His saying: ﴿and that the extravagant are the companions of the Fire﴾ [Ghafir: 43], it becomes an evident syllogism yielding a clear, definite conclusion: that Pharaoh is among the companions of the Fire. This refutes the people of ahl al-wahdah (the proponents of Wahdat al-Wujud, the doctrine of the unity of being) in their claim that he believed, so that they make sins easy in people's eyes and thereby make lawful the creeds of the people of religion.

When Allah mentioned their fear and their excuse, He followed it with what necessitates their tranquility, which is trust in Allah (tawakkul), the One whom whoever is mindful of (raqaba) finds every great thing diminished in his sight. So He said: ﴿And Moses said﴾, i.e., to whoever believed in him, preparing them for the fact that Paradise is not attained except through great hardship, "People are tested according to the measure of their faith." ﴿O my people﴾, thus he sought their sympathy by reminding them of kinship, and he stirred them toward lofty matters by reminding them of the strength that was within them. Then he roused and inflamed them to steadfastness by his saying: ﴿If you have believed in Allah﴾, i.e., as a state that is firm in its steadfastness, like a disposition that does not depart. He strengthened them by mentioning the Greatest Name and what it indicates of the attributes. He answered the condition with his saying: ﴿then upon Him alone﴾, i.e., solely, because of what you know of His greatness, to which nothing besides Him submits ﴿rely﴾, and let the effect of reliance appear upon you in the form of tranquility, steadfastness and calm. ﴿If you are﴾, i.e., as a settled state, ﴿Muslims﴾, combining the affirmation of the heart with the submission of the limbs. The response to this condition is what the preceding past tense indicates in his saying: ﴿upon Him have you relied﴾. ﴿They said﴾, i.e., immediately, as the particle fa' requires: ﴿Upon Allah﴾, i.e., the One to whom all greatness belongs, alone, ﴿we have relied﴾, i.e., we have entrusted all our affairs to Him. ﴿Our Lord﴾, i.e., O You who originated us and who bestows favor upon us. ﴿Do not make us a trial﴾, i.e., a place of mixing with what inclines and turns [hearts], ﴿for the wrongdoing people﴾, i.e., do not let us be afflicted by Your being thought of as indifferent toward us, so that they would increase in aversion from Your religion, supposing that we are upon falsehood; and do not empower them over us in a way that tempts us away from our religion, so that they would suppose they are upon the truth. ﴿And save us by Your mercy﴾, i.e., by Your honoring us, ﴿from the disbelieving people﴾, i.e., the powerful ones, ﴿who are disbelievers﴾, i.e., those who are most deeply engaged in concealing the proofs. In this supplication of theirs there is an indication [that] the matter of religion is more important than the matter of the self.

(p-178) When they agreed to make their reliance on Him manifest and entrusted their affairs to Him, He followed this with what would increase them in tranquillity about settling in the land of the enemy, indicating indifference to him. It is related that they had places of worship (mutaʿabbadāt) where they gathered. When Musa (peace be upon him) was sent, Firawn (Pharaoh) destroyed them. So God Most High commanded that they be made in their houses, lest the disbelievers observe them. Thus He said, Exalted is He, connecting it to His saying: ﴿And Musa said﴾ [Yunus: 84] ﴿And We revealed﴾, i.e., by what We possess of supreme majesty, ﴿to Musa and his brother﴾, i.e., the one who asked for his support and assistance, ﴿that you two should settle﴾, i.e., take, ﴿for your people in Misr (Egypt)﴾, which is the area between the sea and the far end of Aswan and Alexandria, ﴿houses﴾ that will be a place of return for them, to which they return and in which they take refuge. ﴿And make﴾ [i.e.] you two and those with you of your people ﴿your houses a qiblah﴾, i.e., a place of prayer, so that you may worship in them, concealed from the enemies, as a lightening of the causes of dispute. ﴿And establish the prayer﴾, i.e., with all its limits and pillars, remaining hidden from those who would harm you, combining the two instruments of victory: patience and prayer, and training oneself in the religion and firming it in the heart.

Since the gathering in what preceded was greater, more honoured and more magnificent, and since it was obligatory upon the community, just as it was obligatory upon the imam to gather in it, and since attributing the glad tidings to the Sovereign rather than to the bearer of the Law would have been more firm for His command, more manifest for His greatness, more firmly fixed in the hearts of His companions and more comforting to their eyes, He used the singular in His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾ (p-179), i.e., those firmly established in faith, from your brother and others.

When he concluded with the glad tidings for those whose faith was shown by their Islam, through an act that indicates the contemptibility of the enemy's affair, and when the destruction of the one who hates (al-mushani') is among the greatest of glad tidings, and when the misguidance of Pharaoh and his people through adornment and wealth was a leading-astray of others, Moses, peace be upon him, asked for the removal of all of that, for relief from their evil. So Almighty God said, relating of him: ﴿And Moses said﴾, that is, after his long supplication to Pharaoh, his displaying of the miracles before him, his prolonged arrogance against God's command, and his tyranny over the weak among His servants. Since he was among the greatest of those chosen (ahl al-istifa'), he dropped the particle [of address], following their practice (tasannan bihim), and by the attribute of beneficence he indicated that the destruction of their enemies is the greatest beneficence toward them. So he said: ﴿Our Lord﴾ [that is], O You who are beneficent to us, ﴿indeed You﴾ (the emphasis is for the ignorant who deny that the gift of the greatest King could be a cause of humiliation) ﴿have given Pharaoh and his chieftains﴾, that is, the nobles of his people, despite what they are in of disbelief and pride, ﴿adornment﴾, that is, great ornaments with which they beautify themselves, of jewelry, clothing and other things, ﴿and wealth﴾, that is, abundant wealth of gold, silver and other things, ﴿in the life of this world﴾. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with him and his father, that there were for them, from Fustat of Egypt to the land of Abyssinia, mountains containing mines of gold, silver, chrysolite and ruby. Then he clarified its end for them, saying, beginning with the address by the Name of the Lord, so that He would protect him and his followers from the like of their condition: ﴿Our Lord﴾, that is, O You who originated us, who are beneficent to us and who manage our affairs, ﴿so that they may lead astray﴾ (p-180) themselves and lead others astray ﴿from Your way﴾, that is, the broad path which You laid out for reaching Your mercy.

When he had made clear that their final outcome is misguidance, he supplicated against them, again beginning with the address by the Name of the Lord, a third time, because that is one of the signs of acceptance, as was indicated at the end of Al 'Imran, and as an indication that there is no righteousness for them without their destruction and the destruction of that [wealth]: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate﴾, that is, bring about the obliteration (tams), which is the leveling between the obliterated thing and other things, such that it has no benefit ﴿over their wealth﴾.

Since he had seen from them such arrogance against God, such denial of His signs, and such torment of His friends, that nothing would quench his anger except the continuation of their wretchedness in this world and the next, and since he knew that God's power to keep them in disbelief, together with ruining them by stripping their wealth, is like His power to do so by drawing them on through wealth, he said: ﴿and harden﴾, that is, a hardening that is apparent to everyone, by what the word (al-fakk, 'loosening') indicates, being exalted ﴿over their hearts﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: seal them and prevent them from faith. And He answered the supplication with His words: ﴿so that they will not believe﴾, that is, so that the consequence of that hardening is their not believing, when they see the beginnings of the punishment through the obliteration ﴿until they see﴾, that is, with their own eyes, ﴿the painful punishment﴾, where faith will not benefit them. Then they would be combining the humiliation of the souls which was demanded of them today, so that the enduring might would benefit them, [with] the intensity of anger, by placing a thing in other than its proper place, which produces the continuation of their humiliation through punishment. This verse alerts that contentment with a particular disbelief (p-181) does not necessitate approval of disbelief as such. Imam al-Halimi said in his book Shu'ab al-Iman, called al-Minhaj: "And when a Muslim wishes for the disbelief of a Muslim, this is of two kinds. One: that he wishes it for him as a friend wishes for his friend a thing he finds good, so he loves that he should have a share in it; this is disbelief, because approving of disbelief is disbelief. The other: that he wishes it for him as one wishes for his enemy a thing he finds abhorrent, so that he must fall into it; this is not disbelief. Moses, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, after Pharaoh had exhausted him, wished that Pharaoh and his chieftains would not believe, so that the punishment would be due upon them. He went further and supplicated to God, may He be blessed and exalted, and God did not reject that from him, knowing that his severity toward Pharaoh and his harshness toward him was because of what he saw of his insolence and tyranny, and that it was this which moved him to that. So whoever is in his position, has his ruling." Al-Zarkashi related this from him in the letter "tha'" of his Qawa'id, approving of it. It is also related from him that he said: "And if there were in the heart of a Muslim, against a disbeliever who had become Muslim, resentment, and the Muslim grieved over that and wished that he would return to disbelief, he would not become a disbeliever, because his finding disbelief repugnant is what moved him to wish it, and his finding Islam good is what moved him to dislike it." It is related from Shaykh 'Izz al-Din ibn 'Abd al-Salam that if an enemy of a person is killed unjustly and he rejoices, does he sin? If he rejoices that God was disobeyed in it, then yes; but if he rejoices that he was freed from its evil, then there is no harm, because the two causes of rejoicing differ. End.

This is supported by what al-Bayhaqi related in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa with his chain from Miqsam, as a mursal (a report whose chain omits the companion), that "the Prophet ﷺ supplicated against 'Utba ibn Abi Waqqas on the day of Uhud, when he broke his front tooth and wounded his face, saying: 'O God, do not let the year pass over him until he dies a disbeliever!'" So the year had not passed over him before he died a disbeliever in the Fire. The question that contentment with disbelief is disbelief was related by the two Shaykhs (al-Rafi'i and al-Nawawi) from al-Mutawalli, and they were silent about it. But Shaykh Muhyi al-Din said in Sharh al-Muhadhdhab: "That is excessive. The detail mentioned from al-Halimi and Ibn 'Abd al-Salam is what is relied upon." The matter is in the Rawda's original text, for he said: "If he says to a Muslim, 'May God strip him of faith,' or to a disbeliever, 'May God grant him faith,' it is not disbelief, because it is not contentment with disbelief, but rather a supplication against him for intensifying the matter and the punishment." I say: Qadi Husayn mentioned in al-Fatawa a weak opinion that if he says to a Muslim, "May God strip him of faith," he becomes a disbeliever. And God knows best. He related the two opinions from al-Qadi in al-Adhkar and said: "Supplication with that is a sin."

Al-Biqa'i said: When He, glory be to Him, reported the supplication of Moses, peace be upon him, He reported its answer by saying, in a resumed clause (*mustaʾnifan*, beginning a new sentence): ﴿He said: "Your supplication has been answered, you two."﴾ Since this position was the place where an answer was expected, He opened it with its particle (*ḥarfihi*), saying: ﴿قَدْ أُجِيبَتْ دَعْوَتُكُمَا﴾, "Your supplication has been answered." The passive form (*al-binaʾ lil-mafʿul*, the passive voice) is more indicative of power and has a greater effect on the soul than naming the agent through inference. He used the dual to inform that Aaron, peace be upon him, was with Moses, peace be upon him, in this supplication, because he was with him like one thing; there was no disagreement from him toward him at all, even though he was absent. This is like the case when the Prophet (ﷺ) pledged allegiance on behalf of ʿUthman, may Allah be pleased with him, at the Umrah of al-Hudaybiyah, striking one of his hands upon the other while he was absent on the errand of the Prophet (ﷺ). Likewise, the Prophet (ﷺ) set aside a share and reward for him at the Battle of Badr, though he was absent.

Since obedience and awaiting relief, even if its time is long, are the greatest causes of an answer, He made the following a consequence of that, saying: ﴿فَاسْتَقِيمَا﴾, "So remain steadfast," that is: remain firm in worship, humility and submission to your Lord, just as Noah, peace be upon him, remained firm in that, and his time was very long, and his harm was severe, yet he did not grow weary. And since patience is difficult, He emphasized His statement: ﴿وَلَا تَتَّبِعَانِّ﴾, "and do not follow," through haste or lapse from gratitude, ﴿سَبِيلَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾, "the way of those who do not know."

When He commanded patience, which is the fruit of knowledge, He followed that report of the answering of the supplication with His saying: ﴿And We brought across﴾, meaning: by Our greatness, We acted in granting them passage in the manner of one who contends with another and outdoes him. By attaching the preposition *bi* (with) to them, He indicated His companionship with them, as a sign of His approval of their deed, and so He said: ﴿the Children of Israel﴾, meaning: Our servant, the one sincere to Us, ﴿across the sea﴾. This informs that He had commanded them to leave Egypt and fulfilled for them what He had promised, while Pharaoh and his chieftains were destroyed for following them in their rashness and their lack of patience, the path of one who has no knowledge. He delivered the Children of Israel through their patience and their humility. The shift (*iltifat*, a change of grammatical person) from the third person to the first person is because this crossing, its antecedents and its consequences, display the marks of greatness, the force of commands, and the execution of judgments. Then He explained how the answering of the supplication became manifest, by saying, as a consequence of the crossing: (p-184) ﴿So Pharaoh and his hosts pursued them﴾, meaning: they set out in pursuit of them, that is, they drove themselves to follow them, which is traveling in their tracks. *Atba'ahu* means that he overtook him after having been ahead of him. It is said: *tabi'ahu* for good, and *ittaba'ahu* for evil. When this was understood, He stated it explicitly, saying: ﴿in rebellion﴾, meaning: transgressing the truth and treating them with contempt, ﴿and enmity﴾, meaning: wrongdoing and exceeding the bounds.

Since the doer of this was worthy of turning back from the difficult course he had taken, He marvelled at his persistence, and so He said, joining it by conjunction to what is implied, [and he continued] persisting in this: ﴿until﴾. Since seeing the sea part away from the places of their passage was a likely sign that the water would return to its place and he would drown, He used the particle of certainty, saying: ﴿when the drowning overtook him﴾, meaning: it overpowered him and encompassed him, ﴿the drowning﴾, that is, death by water, just as Moses had asked [regarding] that he would not believe until he saw the painful punishment. ﴿He said: I believe﴾, meaning: I bring forth the belief of one who calls me away from denial. Then he gave the reason for his belief by saying, in the recitation of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i (*qira'a*, a canonical mode of recitation) with the *kasra*, as an appositive of "I believe" emphasising the intensity of his distress: ﴿that He﴾, and [in the recitation of] the majority, with the preposition *bi* implied as a causal particle; meaning: acknowledging that ﴿there is no god but He﴾ in whom. It is also permissible that "I believe" governs "that He" and what follows it, meaning: "I believe" the negation of divinity from everything other than the One I have excepted, lest I worship it or turn back from Him.

Since the one destined to perish had now become certain, and knew that there is no salvation except through truthfulness, he wished to inform (p-185) of the utmost extent of his truthfulness, and so he said: ﴿I believe﴾, meaning: I bring forth assent, acknowledging ﴿in Him the Children of Israel﴾, thereby specifying it so as to remove any ambiguity. Then he said: ﴿and I am of the Muslims﴾, thus repeating his acceptance of what he had been called to, which he had refused out of arrogance. He expressed it in a form that indicates a claim of firm establishment in it, as an explanation that he had become humbled to such a degree that none of that arrogance remained with him, and that this did not benefit him because its condition had lapsed. Thus his humiliation was joined to the shame that he would receive in the *barzakh* (the intermediate state) and what follows it. The single instance would have been sufficient for him had the condition been present. The Exalted further increased his humiliation by despairing him of success, through a saying spoken by way of the state of affairs, or by Gabriel, peace be upon him, or by the Angel of Death, or by another of the angelic hosts, peace be upon them: ﴿Now?﴾, meaning: will you respond to what you were called to at this time, when responding will not benefit you, because belief in the unseen, which alone can properly bear the name of belief, has been lost? ﴿And you had already﴾, meaning: while the state is that you ﴿disobeyed﴾, that is, with disbelief, ﴿before﴾, that is, throughout the entire period of the call that preceded this moment. Disobedience to the king necessitates seizure and wrath, however it occurs, so how much more so when it is through disbelief! ﴿And you were﴾, meaning: by a natural disposition, ﴿of the corrupters﴾, that is, the foremost in corruption and in causing corruption.

Disobedience to the king necessitates seizure and wrath, however it occurs, so how much more so when it is through disbelief! ﴿And you were﴾, meaning: by a natural disposition, ﴿of the corrupters﴾, that is, the foremost in corruption and in causing corruption.

Then He reinforced it, in place of the mockery of the enemies, by means of His words, which are a consequence of what that rebuke contained of humiliation through destruction. This indicates that the water surrounded him and kept rising little by little until the period of reproach was prolonged: ﴿Today We shall save you﴾, that is, with a great salvation.

Since that was pleasing, and since what conveys joy is a grief to the enemies (inkā'), He said, indicating that this counts as the taking of his soul: ﴿in your body﴾, that is, without a soul, while it is complete and nothing has been diminished from it, so that no confusion enters into your recognition. ﴿So that you may be﴾, that is, a state that is at the utmost firmness, ﴿a sign for those who come after you﴾, that is, those who will be later than you in life, from the Children of Israel and others, ﴿a sign﴾ that you are a weak, contemptible servant, not a lord, let alone one who is exalted, and so that they may know that whoever disobeys the King is seized, even if he is the strongest of people and has the most soldiers. Some of the atheists have claimed belief in this verse, intending by it to dissolve the binding principle that Pharaoh is among the greatest of unbelievers by the consensus of the adherents of the religions, which Allah protects against, so as to make it easy for people to become bold in sins. He also claimed that there is no explicit text in the Qur'an stating that he is among the people of the Fire, and he went astray from the clear statements in the Qur'an on this in more than one place, and from the fact that His words, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed Pharaoh was haughty in the land, and indeed he was among the transgressors﴾ [Yunus: 83], together with His words, exalted is He: ﴿And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾ [Ghafir: 43], constitute a definitive analogy, self-evident in its text, that he is among the people of the Fire. The verse, as you see, is evidence for His words: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if His punishment comes upon you by night or by day﴾ [Yunus: 50] — the verse. Had Pharaoh been like Quraysh... but how, when there is no comparison between them and him in the severity of arrogance that accompanies the multitude of hosts, the sway of the word through the magnitude of the king, the might of authority, and the strength of wealth and helpers. It has been narrated that Jibril, upon him be peace, had brought him a legal ruling concerning a slave who grew up in the favour of his master, then denied his favour, rejected his right, and claimed lordship over him. Pharaoh therefore wrote that the punishment of the slave who departs from the obedience of his master, who denies his bounty, is that he be drowned in the sea. When drowning overcame him, Jibril, upon him be peace, handed him his own writing, and he recognized it.

Since Pharaoh and his people did not act in accordance with what they saw of the signs, their state was the state of those heedless of them. So the sense is: indeed they were heedless of the signs that came to them. ﴿And indeed many﴾ — He emphasized it, because such a thing, by its remoteness from the right, should not be believed to befall anyone — ﴿of the people﴾, that is, those who have not reached the limit of the first teeth of the people of faith, because of the agitation (nawas, which is turbulence) and self-complacency they have, ﴿are heedless of Our signs﴾, that is, in view of the greatness they possess. ﴿Reform﴾ is the straightening of action toward what benefits instead of what harms. ﴿Establishing the truth﴾ is making it manifest and establishing it by clear proofs, until the one who attacks it returns exhausted and its opponent is routed. ﴿Israf﴾ is going to extremes in exceeding the truth. ﴿Fitnah﴾ is trial, and it is a dealing that brings the hidden matters to light. ﴿Najah﴾ is deliverance from what is feared, and its counterpart is safety. They attached najah to mercy, because it is a bestowal upon the one in need of what the souls of servants aspire to, so it is in the strongest form of calling to righteousness. ﴿Wahy﴾ is casting a meaning into the soul in concealment; inspiration (iyha'), allusion (ima') and indication (isharah) are its counterparts, and it is not permissible to describe anything by wahy except a prophet. ﴿Tabawwa'﴾ means he took, and its root is return; so al-mutabawwa' is the dwelling, because one returns to it to remain in it. ﴿Tamas﴾ is the effacing of a trace, so it is a change into decay and obliteration. ﴿Ijabah﴾ is the agreement of a call with what was requested through it, because it fell upon that attribute. ﴿Da'wah﴾ is the request for an act in the form of a command, and it may also be in the past tense. ﴿Mujawazah﴾ is going out beyond the limit from one of the directions. ﴿Bahr﴾ is the wide resting place of water, such that one in its midst cannot perceive its two edges, and it is derived from breadth. ﴿Ittiba'﴾ is catching up with the first. ﴿Baghy﴾ is seeking elevation without right. ﴿Al-an﴾ is the separator between the two times, past and future, and although it indicates the present, it is built as "dha" is built. The ﴿badan﴾ is the dwelling of the animal spirit in its form.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 93 (part 1 of 3):

When Exalted God mentioned the outcome of the affair of Pharaoh and his people, and that they did not benefit from the clear signs that came to them, despite their being plainly explained and in some cases accompanied by severe trials and tests, until the last of them, when he saw the beginning of destruction through the parting of the sea, did not restrain him from his obstinacy, out of heedlessness of its outcome. He concluded this by reporting the abundance of heedlessness, indicating that this disposition is also found among non-Copts. He followed this with mention of the final outcome of the affair of the Children of Israel, regarding what He bestowed upon them after the deliverance of blessings, which necessitates certain knowledge that there is no god but Him, and that whoever opposes Him is at risk of destruction. (p-189) And that they, despite witnessing the signs that were sent down concerning them to Pharaoh, were given signs specific to them, fulfilling God's promise to their forefathers, containing the utmost of kindness and honour toward them. And that they were under the hand of Pharaoh on a single path, with no disagreement among them, and they did not differ and become sects in beliefs and factions in religions, until the clear knowledge from God came to them. The thing that should have united them upon God instead scattered them onto the path of Satan, because of the corruption of their inner selves and the evil of their hearts, adhering to the visible that passes away, being rigid with the perceptible that perishes, and forgetting the unseen that endures and the known that is certain. All of this is because We decreed it, so the affair follows what We will, not what He commands and forbids. So this was the greatest deterrent against seeking signs and supposing that they would necessitate turning back from misguidance. Thus God said: ﴿And We certainly settled﴾, that is: We settled, by the greatness We possess, before which necks are cut short and the keenest thoughts fall short in counting it, ﴿the Children of Israel﴾ in a dwelling worthy of their returning to it from which they had departed. This is what is meant by His words: ﴿a settlement of truth﴾, that is: in the Holy Land, because Our promise to them concerning it had already preceded. It is the custom of the Arabs that when they praise a thing, they attribute it to truth, because it, along with its stability, is beloved to every soul, and it confirms what is hoped for from good.

Since a dwelling is not pleasant except with provision, and since expressing it by "settlement" implicitly indicates provision by necessary implication, He stated it explicitly, saying: ﴿and We provided for them﴾, that is (p-190) by the greatness We possess, ﴿with good things﴾, that is, sensory ones, pleasant and desirable, of fruits, grains, milk, honey and others, and immaterial ones, of the law, the Book and the knowledge, as We had previously promised their forefathers. Since they, like others, when they are upon matters they agree upon, draw close in them and conform, and when they are upon limits that were set for them by the one who did good to them alone, they do not remain long before they differ, God rebuked them for that, saying: ﴿So they did not﴾, that is: as a consequence of Our truthfulness to them in the promise, they did not ﴿differ﴾, that is: they did not create the discord that leads to making each one of them turn his companion behind him and over his back. He also disdained it ﴿until knowledge came to them﴾, which necessitates their uniting upon one word, because of its precision, so that its followers are of one heart. It is as if it were said: What then is done to them? Neither do they benefit with their intellects, nor do they return to the truth that has come to them? So it was said, emphasizing against the Arabs' denial of resurrection: ﴿Indeed your Lord﴾, that is, the one who does good to you, through the prophets' charge concerning you, your description in their books, and your being made the bearer of the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿will judge between them﴾.

Since this is a great threat, He increased its terror and magnitude by saying: ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is, the Day which is the greatest of days, ﴿concerning that in which they used to differ﴾, that is, concerning their innate actions. He will distinguish truth from falsehood, and the sincere from the heretic, and settle each one in his abode.

He mentioned some of what is in the Tawrah (Torah) concerning the favour bestowed upon them with the Holy Land: (p-191) He said in the course of the Fifth Book (Deuteronomy): "Your eyes have seen all the great works of God which He did. Therefore keep all the commandments which the LORD your God commands you today, that you may enter and possess the land to which you cross over to possess it, and that you may prolong your days in the land which the LORD swore to your fathers to give them and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey. For the land which you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt from which you have come, where you sowed your seed and watered it by your foot, like a vegetable garden. But the land which you cross over to possess is a land of hills and valleys, and drinks water from the rain of heaven. It is a land which the LORD your God cares for; the eyes of the LORD your God are always on it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year. And it shall be that if you diligently obey My commandments which I command you today, to love the LORD your God and serve Him with all your heart and all your soul, then I will give the rain for your land in its season, the early rain and the latter rain, that you may gather in your grain, your new wine, and your oil. And I will give grass in your fields for your livestock, that you may eat and be full. Take heed to yourselves, lest your heart be deceived, and you turn aside and serve other gods and worship them, lest the anger of the LORD be aroused against you, and He shut up the heavens so that there will be no rain, and the land yield no fruit, and you perish quickly from the good land which the LORD gives you. Therefore you shall lay up these words of mine in your heart and in your soul; and you shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes. And you shall teach them to your children, speaking of them when you sit in your house, when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up. And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates, that your days and the days of your children may be multiplied in the land which the LORD swore to your fathers to give them. If you carefully keep all these commandments which I command you, to do them, to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, and to hold fast to Him, then the LORD will drive out all these nations from before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and mightier than yourselves. Every place on which the sole of your foot treads shall be yours: from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, as far as the western sea shall be your territory. No man shall be able to stand before you; the LORD your God will put the fear and dread of you upon all the land on which you tread, as He has said to you. Behold, I set before you today a blessing and a curse: the blessing, if you obey the commandments of the LORD your God which I command you today; and the curse, if you do not obey the commandments of the LORD your God, but turn aside from the way which I command you today, to go after other gods which you have not known. And it shall be, when the LORD your God brings you into the land which you go to possess, that you shall put the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal. Are they not on the other side of the Jordan, behind the road to the going down of the sun, in the land of the Canaanites who dwell in the plain opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?" — and in another copy: "the plain of Mamre" — "for you are to cross over the Jordan to go in to possess the land which the LORD your God is giving you, and you shall possess it and dwell in it. And you shall observe to do all the statutes and judgments which I set before you today." — End.

*[p. 193]* In the Book of Joshua son of Nun, peace be upon him: After the death of Moses, the servant of God, God said to Joshua son of Nun, the attendant of Moses, peace be upon them both: "My servant Moses has died. Now arise, cross this Jordan, you and all this people, into the land which I am giving to the children of Israel. Every place that the sole of your foot treads upon I have given to you, as I said to Moses my servant. From the wilderness and this Lebanon up to the great river, the River Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, no one shall stand before you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not leave you nor forsake you. Be strong and of good courage, for you shall cause this people to inherit the land which I swore to their fathers to give them. The book of this Law shall not depart from your mouth. You shall meditate on it day and night, so that you may observe to act according to all that is written. Then your ways shall prosper, and then you shall be guided. Have I not commanded you? Be strong and of good courage; do not be afraid or dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go."

He commanded Joshua's officers of the people, saying: "Pass through the midst of the camp and command the people, saying to them: Prepare food for yourselves, for after three days you will cross this Jordan to enter and possess the land which the Lord your God is giving you. Remember the word which Moses, the servant of God, commanded you, saying: The Lord your God gives you rest and has given you this land. Your wives, your children and your livestock shall dwell in your cities which Moses, the servant of God, gave you beyond the Jordan. But you shall cross over armed before your brethren, until God gives rest to your brethren as He has given you rest, and they too inherit the land which your Lord is giving them. Then you shall return to the land of your possession which Moses, the servant of God, gave you beyond the Jordan, toward the rising of the sun [and you shall cross over, your hearts fortified, until God gives rest to your brethren as He gave you rest, and they too inherit the land which your Lord is giving you; then you shall return to the land of your possession which Moses, the servant of God, gave you beyond the Jordan]." They answered Joshua, saying: "All that you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go. Just as we obeyed Moses in everything, so we will obey you. Only let the Lord be with you as He was with Moses. Whoever disobeys your command and does not heed your words in all that you command him shall be put to death. Only be strong and of good courage."

*[p. 194]* Joshua son of Nun sent two men secretly from among the unbelievers as spies, saying: "Go, look at the land, all of it, with Jericho." They went and entered the house of a harlot woman named Rahab, and lodged there. It was reported to the king of Jericho: "Behold, men from the children of Israel have come here tonight to spy out the land." The king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying: "Bring out the men who have come to you, who entered your house, for they have come to spy out the whole land." The woman took the two men and hid them, and said: "Indeed, men came to me, but I did not know where they were from. And at the closing of the gate in the darkness, the men went out. I do not know where they went. Pursue them quickly, for you will overtake them." Then she brought them up to the roof and hid them among the stalks of flax. The people pursued them on the road to the Jordan toward the fords (in another copy: toward the shallows), and they shut the gate after those who pursued them had gone out. Before they lay down, Rahab went up to them on the roof and said to them: "I know that the Lord has given you the land, and that the terror of you has fallen upon us, and all the inhabitants of the land have melted before you. We have heard that the Lord dried up the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you utterly destroyed. When we heard, our hearts melted, and no spirit remained in any of us because of you. For the Lord your God, He is God in heaven above and on earth beneath. Now, swear to me by the name of God, since I have shown you kindness, that you also will show kindness to my father's house, and give me a sure sign, that you will spare my father, my mother, my brothers, and all who are attached to them, and deliver our lives from death." They said to her: "We will give our lives in place of yours to die, if you do not tell this news of ours. When God gives us the land, we will deal with you kindly and faithfully." She let them down by a cord through the window, for her house was built into the city wall, and she lived in the wall. She said to them: "Go to the mountain, lest the pursuers meet you, and after that go on your way." They said to her: "We are innocent of this oath of yours by which you have bound us, unless you do what we tell you. Behold, when we enter the land, tie this cord of scarlet thread in the window from which you let us down, and bring your father, your mother, your brothers and all your father's house into the house. Whoever goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood shall be on his own head, and we are innocent. And whoever is with you in the house, his blood shall be on our heads if any hand touches him. But if you tell this news of ours, then we are free from your oath by which you have bound us." She said: "As you have said, so be it." She sent them away, and they departed, and she tied the scarlet cord in the window.

*[p. 195]* They went to the mountain and remained there three days, until the pursuers returned, and did not find them. The two messengers returned, came down from the mountain, crossed the Jordan, came to Joshua son of Nun, and recounted to him everything that had happened to them. They said to Joshua: "Indeed, the Lord has delivered all the land into our hands, and all its inhabitants have melted before us." Joshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Kafrayn, and came to the Jordan, he and all the children of Israel, and they lodged there before they crossed. After three days, the officers passed through the midst of the camp and commanded the people, saying: "When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God and the Levitical priests carrying it, you shall set out from your place and follow after it. Yet there shall be between you and it a distance of about two thousand cubits by measure. Do not come near it, so that you may know the way you should go, for you have not passed this way before." Joshua said to the people: "Sanctify yourselves, for tomorrow God will do wonders among you." Joshua said to the priests: "Take up the ark of the covenant and pass before the people." So they took up the ark of the covenant and went before the people. The Lord said to Joshua: "This day I will begin to exalt you in the sight of all Israel, so that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with you." Joshua said to the children of Israel: "Come here, and hear the words of the Lord your God."

Joshua said: "By this you shall know that there is a living Mighty One in your midst, and that He will surely drive out before you the nations: the Canaanites, the Perizzites (in another copy: the Hittites, named after Heth their ancestor), the Hivites (that is, the eloquent and fluent, and in another copy: those gathered to the tribe), the Girgashites, the Amorites (that is, the chiefs), and the Jebusites (that is, the mighty and overpowering). Behold, the ark of the covenant, the lord of all the earth, passes before you into the Jordan. [Now] take for yourselves twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man from each tribe. When the soles of the feet of the priests bearing the ark of the covenant, the lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan that flow down from above shall be cut off, and shall stand as a single heap, as if held in a wineskin."

When the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, the priests who bore the ark went before the people. When they came to the Jordan [and it was overflowing all the days of harvest, the Jordan was split], the water that flowed down from above stood up as if in a wineskin on one side, and receded very far from the town of Adam which is near Zarethan, and what flowed toward the Arabian Sea, which is called the Sea of Salt, was split, grew dry, and was cut off. The people crossed opposite Jericho. The priests who bore the ark of the covenant stood dry in the midst of the Jordan until all the people had crossed the Jordan. When all the people had crossed, the Lord said to Joshua: "Summon twelve men from the people, one man from each tribe, and tell them: Take from here, from the midst of the Jordan, from beneath the feet of the priests, twelve stones, carry them with you, and set them down in the place where you will lodge tonight." Joshua commanded them [accordingly], and each man was to carry his stone on his shoulder. They took them to the place where they lodged and set them up there. The stones which they had taken from the Jordan, from beneath the feet of the priests who bore the ark, remained there, set in place, until this day. The priests who bore the ark were standing until all the words which the Lord commanded Joshua to relate to the people had been completed, just as Moses had instructed Joshua. The people hurried over the crossing and crossed. When all the people had crossed, and the priests who bore the ark had crossed before the people, the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh, who were armed before their brethren, as Moses had commanded, crossed over, forty thousand strong, passing before the Lord to the plain of Jericho for battle.

*[p. 199]* On that day Joshua was magnified in the eyes of all the children of Israel, and they revered him as they had revered Moses all the days of his life. The Lord said to Joshua: "Command the priests who bore the ark of the testimony to come up out of the Jordan." He commanded them, and when they came up, the water of the Jordan returned to its places as soon as the soles of the priests' feet were set on the bank, and it flowed on the banks of the Jordan as it did before. They came up from the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month (I say: this is Nisan, according to what some learned Jews have said), and camped at Gilgal, on the eastern edge of Jericho. As for the twelve stones which they had taken from the Jordan, Joshua set them up in Gilgal. Joshua said to the children of Israel: "When your children ask you tomorrow, saying: What are these stones? Tell them: Israel crossed this Jordan on dry ground, for the Lord your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before them until they crossed, just as the Lord your God did to the Sea of Suph, which He dried up before us until we crossed it, so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the hand of the Lord is mighty, and that you may fear the Lord your God all the days."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 93 (part 3 of 3):

When all the kings of the Amorites [who were on the western side of the Jordan] and all the kings of the Canaanites [who were] on the shore of the sea heard that the Lord had dried up the water of the Jordan before the Children of Israel until they crossed, their hearts melted, and no spirit remained in them, out of fear of the Children of Israel. At that time the Lord said to Joshua: "Make for yourself a sword of flint and circumcise the Children of Israel a second time." So he circumcised the Children of Israel a second time at the Hill of the Foreskins [p. 200]. The reason Joshua circumcised them was that all the males who had been born in the wilderness when they came out of the land of Egypt had not been circumcised, because all the men of war who were fighting men had perished in the wilderness, since they had not obeyed God their Lord; and they were all uncircumcised. So the Lord swore concerning them that they would not see the land which He had promised their fathers He would give them, the land flowing with milk and honey. Their sons who came after them, whom Joshua circumcised, were the ones who were uncircumcised. When he had circumcised all the people, they remained in their places in the camp until they were healed. The Lord said to Joshua: "Today I have rolled away from you the reproach of the people of Egypt." He named that place Gilgal. The Children of Israel encamped at Gilgal and kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, in the evening, in the plain of Jericho. They ate of the produce of the land after the Passover, and on that day they ate unleavened bread and roasted grain. The manna ceased for the Children of Israel from that day, since they ate of the produce of the land, and the manna did not descend upon the Children of Israel after that day. They ate of the produce of the land and the crops of the land of Canaan that year.

While Joshua was in the plain of Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing opposite him, with his sword drawn and held in his hand. Joshua went to him and said: "Are you for us or for our enemies?" He said: "I am the commander of the armies of the Lord; now I have come to you." Joshua fell on his face to the ground, prostrating, and said: "What does my lord say to his servant?" He said: "Take off your sandals from your feet, for the place where you stand is holy." Joshua did so. The Children of Israel had besieged Jericho, and none of its people could enter or leave. The Lord said to Joshua [p. 201]: "Behold, I have delivered into your hand Jericho, its king and all its warriors. Let all the fighting men go around the city; circle the city once a day, and do this for six days. Seven priests shall carry seven trumpets and shout before the Ark. On the seventh day you shall circle the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the horns. When the trumpets sound and you hear their voices, all the people shall shout with a loud voice, and the wall of the city will fall in its place, and the people shall go up, each man straight ahead." Joshua called the priests and said to them: "Carry the Ark of the Lord, the covenant of the Lord, and let seven priests carry seven horns and blow them before the Ark of the Lord." Then he said to the people: "Go around the city, and let the armed men pass before the Ark of the Lord." So seven priests carried seven horns and shouted before the Ark of the Lord. They did not cease blowing the horns, and those who carried the Ark followed the trumpeters, and the armed men marched before the priests who were shouting with the horns, and they marched before the Ark. Joshua said to the people: "Do not shout, do not let your voices be heard, and let no word come out of your mouths until the day I tell you to shout." So the assembly circled the Ark once each day, as Joshua had commanded them [p. 202]. When the seventh day came, they rose at dawn and surrounded the city as was their custom, but on that seventh day they went around it seven times. In the seventh circuit the priests blew the horns, and Joshua said to the people: "Shout, for the Lord has delivered the city into your hands. But let this city and everything in it be devoted to the Lord; none of you shall touch it. Spare Rahab the harlot, that is, the innkeeper (al-qindiqaniyya), as some of their learned men informed me, and this is supported by the description of her earlier as al-sawwaqa, and God knows best, and spare everyone who is with her in her house, because she hid the two spies whom we sent. As for you, guard yourselves from what is forbidden, and do not defile yourselves by taking what is forbidden, lest you make the camp of the Children of Israel forbidden." So they blew the horns, and when the people heard the sound of the trumpets, they all cried out with one very loud shout, and the wall of the city fell, and the people went up into the city, each man straight ahead. They captured it and killed everyone in it, men and women, elders and children, oxen, donkeys and sheep; they killed them with the sword. As for the two men who had spied out the land, Joshua said to them: "Go into the house of the harlot woman, that is, the innkeeper, as before, bring her out, and bring out everyone who is with her in the house, as you swore to her." They did so and brought them out, outside the camp of the Children of Israel, and they burned the city and everyone in it with fire. Joshua spared the harlot, her parents and everyone with her. Joshua swore in that time and cursed, saying: "Cursed be the man before the Lord who rises and rebuilds this city of Jericho." The Lord was with Joshua, with His help and His victory, and his report spread through the whole land. But the Children of Israel committed a sin and took of what was devoted, because Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, slaughtered and took of what was devoted and hid it in his tent. So the anger of the Lord burned against the Children of Israel. Then Joshua sent men to Ai, which is near Beth-aven, east of Bethel, to spy it out. They said to him: "Two or three thousand will suffice to take it, since its people are few." So they went up and fought them at the city gate, and the Children of Israel fled, and many of them were wounded. [The text then relates the story of Joshua's prostration and distress, and God Most High informing him that his people had committed ghulul (misappropriation of booty); then He commanded him to cast lots until the one who had the ghulul, who was Achan, came out. His ghulul was a Babylonian carpet, two hundred dirhams of silver, and an ingot of gold weighing fifty dinars. Joshua brought him out together with everything he had.] This has been discussed in al-Baqara at: ﴿Those are the ones who have bought the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter﴾ [al-Baqara 2:86], and it was mentioned earlier in al-Ma'ida concerning the conquest of some lands of Jerusalem by another miracle. They continued in this way, conquering one town after another and killing their giants one after another, and they witnessed in that wondrous affairs and marvelous decrees that will remain through the passing of ages and the course of eras. Meanwhile, every little while they disbelieved [p. 204] and broke covenants and did not give thanks, as is explained in the Book of Joshua son of Nun. Part of it has already been mentioned in al-Ma'ida at the words of God Most High: ﴿So they became blind and deaf﴾ [al-Ma'ida 5:71], and so on. All of this came after knowledge had reached them that admits no doubt, no suspicion touches it, and no ambiguity approaches it. Blessed is He to whom all command belongs. None can lead astray whom He guides, and none can guide whom He leads astray.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 94:

Since what preceded, from the verses of this clear surah, is that the one whose wretchedness is willed does not benefit from witnessing the signs, this served as the reason for negating doubt about them and establishing certainty in their contents, through the proofs that had already passed concerning those contents, until it concluded that by censuring the one who acted as a doubter after the knowledge that necessitates certainty had come. The Prophet (ﷺ), as had passed at the end of the surah before it, was the most compassionate of creation, especially toward the Arabs, and especially toward his own people among them. The divine command had come from the Divine Presence to him in a way that agreed with his nature, namely exerting effort in gently dealing with them. This was fitting to stir human nature toward wishing that they be answered in what they proposed. Asking for that after weaving away from him was, in general, an act of doubt. So it was intended to turn the self away from it entirely, even by merely passing thought through the mind. Thus it was said, as a consequence of what came before: ﴿So if you are﴾, that is, O most merciful of creation, ﴿in doubt﴾. This speech was not intended in its literal sense, and God knows best, but rather to strengthen certainty, to emphasize it, to firm it up, and to confirm it, by [indicating] that this is a matter that has been resolved upon and concluded, so it admits of no reconsideration. That is because the meaning is that their steadfastness in wretchedness (p-205) is a matter known only from Us. That is by one of two means: either through the trustworthy one, Jibril, with what he brings of revelation from Us, fresh and tender, preserved from others, so there is no distortion or alteration in it; or through the People of the Book, from their prophets. In the latter case there is a descent by two degrees, together with allowing corruption and alteration, and this is what no one of lofty aspiration and noble soul would accept. So the meaning is: We have already informed you that the signs do not increase the one decreed to wretchedness except in misguidance, and We are aware of that. ﴿And none informs you like the One who is All-Aware﴾ [Fatir: 14]. So do not seek My answering them in what they propose to you, hoping they will believe, for they will not believe in that. ﴿So if you are﴾, that is, at any time, ﴿in doubt﴾, that is, even if slight, ﴿about what We have sent down﴾, that is, with Our majesty, reaching you through the intermediary, ﴿to you﴾ regarding that, ﴿then ask﴾, that is, because of that doubt, ﴿those who read﴾, that is, consistently in that, ﴿the Scripture﴾, that is, the heavenly one, from the Jews and the Christians, for they have a great degree of comprehension of the soundness of what We have sent down to you. Whoever among them believed, or was just, is worthy that the one who consults him about it should increase in faith. Since they were some of those given the Scripture in the past, he affirmed the preposition, saying: ﴿from before you﴾, though they are far from that news by stages, so do not incline to asking anyone other than Me. This is the content of His statement, exalted is He, emphasized and coming with the particle of expectation (p-206), because each of the two matters is in its most fitting place: ﴿The truth has certainly come to you﴾, that is, the established one, complete in its establishment [and it is the enforcement of justice among them]. He increased it in honor and in encouraging it by saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾, that is, the One who has bestowed favor upon you by choosing you for this. Therefore it was brought in the manner of explanation of it without a conjunction. When it was established that it is the truth, that is, the most firmly established, there followed from it distance from wavering on the part of the one to whom it came, so it was fitting to follow it with His statement: ﴿So do not be﴾, He emphasized it because it is worthy that no one turn away from it in any way, ﴿among the doubters﴾, [that is] the heedless of the signs of God, [so that you seek the bounty for the people of justice]. Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with him and his father, said: "No, by God! He did not doubt for the blink of an eye, nor did he ask any of them."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 95:

When he was forbidden from that, nothing remained of what the rational division required except obstinacy on the part of one who is capable of it, as the Children of Israel did after knowledge had come. So He followed the prohibition against the like of their condition with His words: ﴿And never be (one)﴾, that is, in any way whatsoever, and what is meant by this is his followers, ﴿of those who denied﴾, that is, who did the deed of one who denies, treating with contempt ﴿the signs of Allah﴾, that is, those signs than which there is nothing greater, by attributing them to One than whom there is nothing greater, ﴿and so you would be﴾, that is, in a firm state, ﴿of the losers﴾. Rather, remain upon what you are upon of certainty, tranquility, trust in Allah and composure. This and similar expressions, in which the wording is made harsh, indicate the great nearness of the one addressed [even if the intended party is other than him] and his lofty station and subtle distinction, as its explanation has already passed from the Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali, may Allah have mercy on him, in Surah Bara'ah at His words, exalted is He: ﴿Allah pardon you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 43], and so on. And the harshness of the wording in it (p-207) is a great discipline for his followers.

Shakk (doubt) is standing between two contradictories, and it is from the shakk of a stick, in what penetrates it, because by that doubt one stands between its two sides. Al-inzal (sending down) is the transferring of a thing from a height to a lower place. Al-imtira' (disputing) is seeking to create doubt despite the evidence being apparent, from mary al-dar' (milking the udder), which is stroking it so that it yields milk.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 10, verses 96–97:

Since what has preceded of these verses, and what is of their kind, requires that the signs will not avail them, this is made explicit by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those against whom the word has been justified﴾, meaning: that it was necessary and established, ﴿against them﴾, meaning: that they are wretched. He expressed it with the name that conveys kindness (*al-ism al-mufhim lil-ihsan*), to inform that He did not make the punishment obligatory for them except as a kindness to him (ﷺ), by what he suffers from dealing with them and other wisdom. So He said: ﴿the word of your Lord﴾ [Hud: 119], meaning the One who is kind to you in all your affairs, ﴿will not believe﴾, meaning: there is no acceptance from them, because belief has been renewed [for them]. ﴿Even if every sign should come to them﴾, and its relation to His saying: ﴿The truth has certainly come to you﴾ [Yunus: 94] is the relation of ﴿The truth has certainly come to you﴾ [Yunus: 94] to ﴿So if you are in doubt﴾ [Yunus: 94], the verse, in the clarification derived from omitting the conjunction. When the speech is on one meaning, it is like a single word, so it was named by it. ﴿Until they see the painful punishment﴾, meaning: at a time when faith will not benefit them, because its condition has passed, just as it did not benefit Pharaoh for this reason. ﴿The way of Allah concerning those who passed away before, and you will not find any change in the way of Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 62].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 10, verses 96–97:

Since what has preceded of these verses, and what is of their kind, requires that the signs will not avail them, this is made explicit by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those against whom the word has been justified﴾, meaning: that it was necessary and established, ﴿against them﴾, meaning: that they are wretched. He expressed it with the name that conveys kindness (*al-ism al-mufhim lil-ihsan*), to inform that He did not make the punishment obligatory for them except as a kindness to him (ﷺ), by what he suffers from dealing with them and other wisdom. So He said: ﴿the word of your Lord﴾ [Hud: 119], meaning the One who is kind to you in all your affairs, ﴿will not believe﴾, meaning: there is no acceptance from them, because belief has been renewed [for them]. ﴿Even if every sign should come to them﴾, and its relation to His saying: ﴿The truth has certainly come to you﴾ [Yunus: 94] is the relation of ﴿The truth has certainly come to you﴾ [Yunus: 94] to ﴿So if you are in doubt﴾ [Yunus: 94], the verse, in the clarification derived from omitting the conjunction. When the speech is on one meaning, it is like a single word, so it was named by it. ﴿Until they see the painful punishment﴾, meaning: at a time when faith will not benefit them, because its condition has passed, just as it did not benefit Pharaoh for this reason. ﴿The way of Allah concerning those who passed away before, and you will not find any change in the way of Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 62].

(p-208) Since this is the place where one might say: "Signs are only sought for the faith that is hoped to result from them," the response is introduced by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then why was there not a town﴾, that is, "Why did it not happen?", ﴿that believed﴾, that is, whose people believed upon the coming of the signs or upon seeing the causes of punishment, ﴿so that its faith benefited it﴾ [that is, its faith resulted in its benefit] ﹙﴿its faith﹚﹚. Since the meaning of "why" (lawla) is negation, the implied sense is: "But no town among them believed except at the moment the punishment struck, as Pharaoh did. Had he believed upon seeing the sea split open, or when it was in the middle and before it closed over him, it would have been accepted; but he believed only after it had poured over him and touched him. That is the time when faith does not benefit, because the condition of faith in the unseen has been lost." ﴿Except the people of Jonah﴾: when they believed, they believed at the signs, while the obligation still remained, and that benefited them. This is shown by His saying: ﴿When they believed﹚, which indicates that the punishment had already overshadowed them. ﴿We removed﴾, that is, by Our majesty, ﴿from them﴾, that is, at the time of their faith, ﴿the punishment of disgrace﴾, that is, the one that would have brought upon them, had it descended, the humiliation of both abodes, ﴿in the life of this world﴾, that is, He did not seize them at the time they saw it. ﴿And We granted them enjoyment﴾ [that is] a great enjoyment ﴿for a time﴾, which is until the end of their appointed terms, each one of them at his own appointed time. What I have mentioned concerning the meaning of the verse was transmitted by the judge Abu Muhammad Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Bastī in his chain-attested tafsir, from Ibn Abi Umar, who said: Sufyan al-Thawri said: (p-209) ﴿Then why was there not a town that believed﴾ — he said: "So no town believed." This is the explanation of the meaning of the speech. As for "lawla," it here means "hallā" (why not), and it has several uses: exhortation (taḥḍīḍ) and reproach (ta'nīth), that is, rebuke (tawbīkh); here it is for rebuke. It may also be interrogative with the sense of "lawla," and both meanings necessarily entail negation. Benefit (naf') is the attainment of pleasure through an act or through what leads to it, like a bitter medicine that leads to pleasure. Disgrace (khizy) is that a person be exposed, and it is the lowering of rank because of the distress that befalls him; its original root is fatigue.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 99:

Since what came before may have led one to believe that the faith of such people is impossible, this verse comes in a position of guarding against that impression, while also clarifying. The Messenger's ﷺ eagerness for their faith is of no benefit, and his exertion in removing doubts and establishing proofs only takes effect by the will of Allah Most High, for His granting them success and guidance. Had that alone been sufficient, they would have believed through this surah, for it removed their doubts, made clear their misguidance, and, through the two stories of Nuh and Musa (upon them both be peace), established their weakness and the feebleness of their defenses. Allah Most High then said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed﴾, meaning the faith of people, ﴿your Lord﴾, that is, the One who is good to you, by the coming of those who come forward because He knows the good in them, and the turning away of those who turn away because they lack receptiveness to good, ﴿they would all have believed, everyone on earth﴾ of the disbelievers.

Since this is apparent in all of them, He stated it with emphasis, because the context requires it, so He said: (p-210) ﴿all of them together﴾, meaning gathered at one time, not differing about anything of it. But He did not will that, and you, out of your eagerness to carry out My commands and My charge to you to be gentle with My creation, in accordance with the good with which I have disposed you, desire that. ﴿Will you then compel the people﴾, meaning those whom Allah did not will to have faith [along with what He has made them to have of instability] ﴿until they become﴾, meaning in a natural state ﴿believers﴾, meaning firmly established in faith. Placing the interrogative particle before the noun rather than the verb indicates that the act, which here is compulsion, is possible without that noun, which here is Allah alone [the One able to transform natures], for His power overcomes everything and His will takes effect in everything, with the indication that the occurrence of what contradicts His will is impossible and cannot be achieved by anyone other than Him Most High, whether by compulsion or otherwise. Will (mashī'ah) is a meaning by which the act becomes willed; it is taken from "shay'" (thing). The purpose of the verse is to lighten what afflicts the Prophet ﷺ of grief, out of his eagerness for their faith.

﴿And it is not﴾, i.e., it is not fitting or possible, ﴿for any soul﴾, i.e., one soul or more, ﴿to believe﴾, i.e., for faith to arise from it at any time, ﴿except by the permission of Allah﴾, i.e., by the will of the Sovereign King, to whom belong creation and command, and by His enabling it. He makes steadfastness and tranquility, which are necessary for faith, the faith that is farthest of all things from magic, ﴿upon those who use their intellects﴾, so they adhere to the noble morals that are the fruits of faith. ﴿And He places defilement﴾, i.e., agitation and instability, which entail denial, which is most similar to magic, because it is imagining [what] (p-211) has no reality, and filth, ugliness, anger, and the punishment that arises from it.

Since what is in this surah of proofs has reached, in clarification, a degree where one needs nothing beyond bare reason, He said: ﴿upon those who do not reason﴾, i.e., they have no intellect, so they do not benefit from the signs. They claim to be the most intelligent of people, yet they fall into the vices of character while claiming to be the farthest of people from them. So let not your soul go after them in regret; and "the soul" (nafs) is the essence of a thing, such that if everything else in it were nullified, that thing would not be nullified, and its self (nafs) and its essence (dhat) are one.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verses 101–102:

When what preceded of the prohibition against giving ear to them in their demand for signs had been established, and it was concluded by tying the matter solely to God's will, it was as if it were said: "What is to be said to them when they demand?" So He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is: O noblest of creation, to them, without being concerned about their affair, and alerting them to the refutation of the doctrine of predestinarianism (jabr), whose adherents cling to verses like this one, because the divine will is hidden and the servant is commanded to exert effort in obedience with the power and capacity he has been given.

When He had commanded this reflection, which might lead some to think that man has an independent power, He alerted them to the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah, who hold the doctrine of acquisition (kasb), which is, as Imam Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "a matter between two matters: neither predestination nor delegation (tafwid)." So He said, instructing: Indeed, whoever has been judged to be wretched, nothing benefits him: ﴿Look﴾ [that is] with your eyes and your insight, so that by benefiting from reason you may leave the category of cattle. The Imam said: If a human being reflected on the manner of Allah's wisdom in creating the wing of a gnat, his thought would cut off before reaching the first level of those wisdoms and benefits. Therefore He left it vague in His saying: ﴿what﴾, that is, whatever ﴿is in the heavens and the earth﴾, that is: of the signs and clear proofs which you have removed from the category of signs through your familiarity with them, though upon reflection they are among the greatest of extraordinary things. The Imam said: So it is as if He, glorified is He, alerted to the universal principle so that one may be mindful of its divisions. Abu Hayyan, drawing on the Imam, said: The path to knowing Him, exalted is He, is through reflection on His creatures. In the upper world there are the movements of the spheres, their measures and configurations, the stars, and what pertains to them of benefits and advantages; and in the lower world there are the conditions of the elements, minerals, plants, and animals, and especially the condition of man. End of quotation.

[Since the signs within them are of the utmost clarity of indication, He, glorified is He, alerted that holding back from faith after being alerted to the manner of inference is obstinacy, and so He said]: ﴿And not﴾, where it is negating or interrogative, ﴿avail the signs﴾, that is: even though they are of the utmost clarity, ﴿nor the warners﴾, that is: the warnings, or the messengers who warn, ﴿to a people﴾, that is: even if they have strength, ﴿who do not believe﴾, that is: because they have been judged to be wretched. This was a cause for threatening them with His saying: ﴿So do they await﴾, that is: with all their strength in denying the Messenger and holding back from faith, ﴿but﴾, that is: days, that is: events, ﴿like the days﴾, that is: events, ﴿of those who passed away﴾. Since the people of those terrifying days were some of those who came before, He brought the prepositional phrase and said: ﴿before them﴾, that is: of the nations who denied, namely the Copts, the people of Noah, and whatever nations lay between them, [that is] of the rights of the Word upon them, so We will bring Our might upon them, then We will save you for your faith, just as We used to bring it upon those when they denied Our messengers, then We save the messengers and those who believed in them in truth; this is incumbent upon Us, for justice among the servants.

Since reference has already been made to the fact that the Word was realized against the disbelievers, through their unbelief and the filth which is punishment, He increased the threat by adding, in a parenthetical form, what their action caused, the behavior of one who awaits punishment, in His saying: ﴿Say: Then wait﴾, that is: with all your effort, for what you see befalling you because of what has been established among you of what used to befall those of old in the days of Allah. The warning was intensified by His resuming speech, emphasizing their denial, with: ﴿Indeed I﴾, and He informed them of the justice of the matter by His saying: ﴿am with you among those who wait﴾.
