Since the passage is a discussion that continues from the previous verses, the text is translated as it stands.

When the implied sense was: "Indeed, in the days of those who passed away, We used to inflict the abomination upon the deniers," he followed it with an explanation of what was done to the messengers and their followers when He destroyed the wrongdoers, namely His words: ﴿Then We deliver﴾, meaning a great deliverance [and We deliver them with a great deliverance]. He expressed it in the present tense, to narrate and depict past circumstances, to warn them against the like of them, and to inform them that He does the same with this Messenger (ﷺ) and his followers, may Allah be pleased with them. By the particle of delay (thumma, "then") he indicated the length of the period of trial and the great rank of the deliverance. He omitted the counterpart of the deliverance, because the context after the verse ﴿Unquestionably, the friends of Allah...﴾ [Yunus: 62] (p-214) looks more toward good tidings than toward warning. ﴿Our messengers﴾ [meaning] those whose greatness derives from Our greatness, ﴿and those who believed﴾, meaning in the messengers, and who were with them in their time, even if they were at the lowest degrees of faith. This honours the messengers, for they are on the way to firmness through their companionship with them. Then he joined to this, as an honour to the firm and an encouragement to the like of their condition, His words: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning just as it was incumbent upon Us to destroy the disbelievers with this great destruction, ﴿as a right incumbent upon Us﴾, meaning by what We have made obligatory upon Our Supreme Majesty, ﴿We shall deliver the believers﴾, meaning those who are steadfast in faith [even if they were] after the death of the messengers, [with a great deliverance, and We deliver them with a great deliverance. The verse is therefore of the ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which corresponding elements are omitted from each of two parts) with respect to what the two recitations, the one with lightening and the one with doubling, point to]. Or this may be built upon a question from someone who might say: "Are the rights of salvation exclusive to the messengers and those with them?" It was answered: No, rather ﴿thus﴾ [meaning] the rights ﴿as a right incumbent upon Us﴾ [in accordance with Our greatness] ﴿We shall deliver the believers﴾ in every age, even if there is no messenger among them, because the cause is the attribute of firm faith. Accordingly, the kaf (the particle "thus") is the mubtada' (subject) and "nunji" (We shall deliver) is its khabar (predicate).

Al-nazar (contemplation): seeking the meaning with the heart through remembrance, just as the perception of a sensible object is sought with the eye. Al-ghina (sufficiency): the obtaining of what excludes harm and the attribute of deficiency; its opposite is need. Al-nudhur (warnings): plural of nadhir (warner), from al-nidhara, which is informing about the place of fear so that safety may be attained thereby. Al-intizar (waiting): remaining steady in anticipation of what the condition will become. Al-mathal (likeness): if it is of the same kind, it is that which fills the place of another (p-215) in the senses; if it is of a different kind, then what is meant is that which contains a meaning by which it approaches the other, like its approach to its own kind, such as the comparison of the works of the disbeliever to a mirage. Al-najah (deliverance) is from al-najwah, which is rising up out of destruction.

When the weaning from inclination toward those who ask for signs had already been mentioned, and their asking for them was only in the manner of doubt (even if it was not in that manner, it is generally the act of one who doubts), and answers to them had already been given, and this was concluded with their threat and with the good news for the believers, which necessitates their steadfastness, it was perfectly appropriate that He followed the command with another answer indicating his (ﷺ) steadfastness, and that he is the one who makes his religion manifest, whether or not those who are pleased are pleased and those who are displeased are displeased. This is because the exposition had reached its goal in His saying, ﴿Say: "O people"﴾, that is, those who are in the realm of agitation, whose aspirations have not raised them to the rank of steadfastness, ﴿if you are﴾, that is, in a state that is like a natural disposition, immersed ﴿in doubt﴾ existing ﴿concerning﴾ the matter of ﴿my religion﴾, seeking, after the intellect has taken charge of pointing to it, the sending down of signs for its descent. So I am not in doubt about the soundness of my religion and the falsehood of your religion. Therefore present it to your intellects and consider what wisdoms it contains, keeping in mind what your religion has of the revelation that was explained earlier in His saying, ﴿Say: "Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision"﴾ [Yunus: 59], and similar to it. ﴿Then I do not worship﴾, that is, now or in the future, ﴿those whom you worship﴾, that is, now or after now, ﴿besides God﴾, that is, the Supreme King, since they have no power over anything of my harm. So do not hope that doubt will arise in me because of the doubt that arises in you. Thus, I do not worship anything other than God at all.

Since the negation of worshipping other than Him is not explicit in affirming worship of Him, He said: ﴿But I worship God﴾, that is, the One who combines the attributes of perfection, with continuous worship. Then He described Him with what necessitates caution toward Him and indicates the perfection of His power: ﴿who takes you in death﴾, by extracting your souls, which nothing you possess can equal. So do not hope, when He wills to take them, to attempt to direct any defense against that. In this description, together with what it contains of instilling fear, there is an indication of the proof of origination and return. It is as if it were said: the One who brought you into existence from nothing, as you acknowledge, will after this bringing into existence cause you to cease to be, and you will be humbled. Thus it is established with certainty that He is able to restore you after this annihilation, by way of greater priority. So beware of Him, that you may worship Him as I worship Him, for He has commanded me to do so, and you know the peril of a king when he is disobeyed.

He said, ﴿if you are in doubt﴾, although they openly declare the falsehood of his religion, because they are in the position of those who doubt, due to their agitation upon the arrival of the signs. Or because among them there are those who doubt, so the term was applied to them, since it is closer to the realm. Doubt is standing between a meaning and its opposite, and its opposite is conviction, for conviction is certainty in the soundness of a meaning without its opposite. He expressed it with ﴿min﴾ ("from/concerning") to indicate that their act of doubt began from the religion. Had He expressed it with ﴿fi﴾ ("in"), it would have implied that they entered into it, being in doubt, and doubt concerning the religion. The vessel of a thing's vessel is a vessel for that thing. He omitted the conjunction to indicate that each answer from among them is sufficient on its own.

When He established what is fitting by way of the intellect, He followed it with what came in transmitted report, to confirm and necessitate it, by His saying: ﴿And I have been commanded﴾, that is, with a firm and binding command from One for whom no one has any command alongside Him, [and He magnified the one commanded by making it the principal of the speech, placing it in the position of the subject, so He said]: ﴿that I should be﴾, that is, constantly, with a natural disposition, [and since the context concerns what may admit doubt regarding an inward matter, He expressed it with faith, which belongs to the heart, so He said]: ﴿among the believers﴾, that is, those firmly established in this attribute. ﴿And that you should set﴾ [that is] O Messenger, ﴿your face﴾, that is, your whole self, in sincere devotion that has no admixture, ﴿to the religion﴾. Thus He connected first the word ﴿an﴾ ("that") in the sense of a command [i.e., "that I should be", not "be"], and second with its own wording [which is ﴿aqim﴾ ("set")], combining both styles. Both are in the sense of a verbal noun. He specified the second for this with its length, because it is like an elaboration of the first, so the address in it is more emphatic and more delightful. His saying ﴿ḥanīfan﴾ ("upright") is a circumstantial clause from the subject of ﴿aqim﴾, and its meaning is: submitting, inclining toward the proof, as I have explained in al-Baqarah, that is, combine faith in the heart with submission through the limbs. ﴿And do not be﴾, that is, at any time, ﴿among the polytheists﴾, who are opposed to the attribute of submission, with harshness, rigidity, hardness, and severity.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 106:

When He forbade him from shirk (associating partners with God), He reinforced this with something that serves as a justification for it, namely the folly that it entails: submitting to what has neither harm nor benefit. This is expressed in the words of the Most High: ﴿And do not invoke﴾ [i.e., at any rank among the ranks that exist] ﴿besides Allah﴾, i.e., the One in whose hand is every thing, ﴿that which neither benefits you﴾, i.e., if you do any such thing, then His punishment comes upon you, ﴿nor harms you﴾, i.e., if you remain upon obedience to Us, with Our help. ﴿But if you do﴾, i.e., something of what We have forbidden you, ﴿then indeed you, at that time﴾, if you invoke that other [for that reason], ﴿would be among the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., those who go to excess in placing the supplication where it does not belong, because whatever is of this nature is at the furthest remove from the station of divinity;

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 10, verse 107:

[Then] He, exalted is He, said, connecting it to His words: ﴿If you do so﴾ [Yunus: 106], ﴿And if Allah touches you﴾, i.e., He who has no repeller for His command, ﴿with harm﴾, i.e., any harm whatsoever, in any manner whatsoever, even if it is very apparent, as indicated by the use of the explicit noun; ﴿then there is no remover of it﴾, i.e., at all, in any way whatsoever, ﴿except Him﴾, because He wills it, and what He wills cannot be other than it. So do not look to anyone else to grant you relief from it by good. He expressed it with "touch" because it is the more fearful. ﴿And if He intends for you﴾ [i.e., any intention at all] ﴿good, then there is no﴾, i.e., it will certainly reach you, for ﴿repeller﴾ is not possible for it. He alerted that nothing is obligatory upon Him, glorified is He, by placing in the position of the pronoun His words: ﴿for His bounty﴾ [i.e.] from whomever He intends it for, as some of the tyrannical followers of worldly kings do in repelling some of what they intend, but rather He is such that no one speaks except by His permission, so do not fear other than Him. Thus the verse is of the type of ihtibak (an interlocking elision): He mentioned "touch" first as evidence of His intention second, and "intention" second as evidence of its omission first. He did not make an exception in the case of intention as He did in the case of removal, because repelling what is willed is impossible. He expressed the good with "intention" (p-219) and the harm with "touch", alerting that he ﷺ is intended for good in essence and for harm incidentally, as a consolation to his heart, given what was repeated in this surah of the announcement of the realization of punishment upon the defiant and the despair of the wrongdoers. When this was established, the placement of His words, clarifying the state of that bounty, was fitting: ﴿He afflicts with it﴾, i.e., with that bounty or with what preceded of good and harm, ﴿whomever He wills﴾, i.e., whoever he may be, of low or high rank, and He explained the cause of their being subjugated with His words: ﴿of His servants﴾. All of this is an indication that what made turning away from their objects of worship necessary by their detachment from them necessitated turning toward Him by His being established and His being exclusively His. He ended the verse with His words: ﴿And He is the Forgiving﴾, i.e., the one who conceals sins most thoroughly, ﴿the Merciful﴾, i.e., the one who is most abundant in honoring, indicating that His granting good cannot be except as bounty from Him after the concealment of sins and mercy toward weakness. So He is deserving of being worshipped. Al-mass (touch): the gathering of opposites without deficiency; its counterpart is al-mutabaqa (correspondence), and al-mujama'a (conjunction) its opposite is al-mubayana (contrast). Al-kashf: lifting of a veil. He made harm as if it were a barrier preventing man's perception and a veil over him.

When the commands, prohibitions, and answers in this surah became numerous, because of what they proposed out of obstinacy (*ta'annut*), and it ended by stating that whoever calls upon other than Him is firmly rooted in wrongdoing with no protector from it, He concluded that with a reply informing them that the benefit of obedience returns only to them, and the harm of aversion falls only upon them. So Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "O mankind, there has come to you the truth"﴾, that is, the ultimate end of everyone who has the capacity for movement and agitation [p. 220]. ﴿The truth﴾, that is, the complete truth, through this Messenger (ﷺ) and this Book. That is a great good with which Allah has favoured you. He increased the desire for it by His saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾, that is, the One who is good to you. ﴿Whoever is guided﴾, that is, as a consequence, whoever is guided, meaning believes in Muhammad (ﷺ) and acts by what is in the Book, ﴿then he is guided only for himself﴾, [that is], because he followed the established truth and abandoned the vanishing falsehood, so he saved himself from the Fire and made Paradise necessary for himself. ﴿And whoever goes astray﴾, that is, disbelieves in both or in any part of them, ﴿then he strays only to his own loss﴾, because he abandoned what remains and clung to what is not in his possession at all, since it is perishing; so he deceived himself. ﴿And I am not﴾, and since the context is about negating his authority over them, and that this belongs to Allah, the Exalted, the placing of their pronoun first was more important, so He said: ﴿over you a guardian (*wakil*)﴾, one who is required to protect you from what leads to destruction and to prevent it from you, as a *wakil* is required to do.

Since most of what precedes this verse consisted of admonition and reminder to them, He concluded it with a command to the Messenger (ﷺ) concerning what he himself should do, whether they respond or do not respond. So He said, in continuation of His saying ﴿Say: O mankind﴾ [Yunus 10:104], ﴿And follow﴾, that is, with all your effort, ﴿what is revealed to you﴾. The verb was made passive (yuha, "is revealed") because that came after his infallibility (ʿiṣma) had been established and it was known that everything that reaches him comes from Allah. Thus it was more apt for the command to follow everything that comes to him from Him, glorified is He, and it also indicates that he does not speak out of desire. ﴿And be patient﴾ in conveying the message, despite the great harm and severe danger that befall you in this, (p-221) from the misguidance of those who do not accept guidance, their turning away, their coldness, and their harm. ﴿Until Allah judges﴾, that is, the Supreme King judges between those of your community who went astray and those who were guided. ﴿And He is﴾, that is, He alone is, ﴿the best of judges﴾, because He delivers judgment in its most fitting, proper, best, and most just places, and He is the One who knows the hidden secrets. So act yourself according to what you are commanded, give good news, warn, inform, and call to Allah with all that He has commanded you, and leave those who are called until He commands you concerning them with His command.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is narrated that when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered the Ansar and said: "Indeed, you will find after me favoritism (athara), so be patient until you meet me." Abu Hayyan and others followed him in this. If it is authentic, then its secret, and Allah knows best, is that when this verse made known that whoever follows revelation will be tested with what calls for patience, and made clear that whoever follows it more fully will be tested more severely, the Ansar, may Allah be pleased with them all, were most deserving of this description over others, in that they were the first tribe that faith united, and in that they were the easiest to lead and the most gentle in disposition, although they had no prior companionship with the Prophet (ﷺ) nor experience of his circumstances that would obligate them to follow him as obligated for one who was of his paternal kin, the Quraysh, who mixed with him, found familiarity with him, and saw from him the lofty qualities of character and noble traits that strengthen one's motive to follow him. Since this was so, the Prophet (ﷺ) singled out the Ansar, may Allah be pleased with them, for this matter. Their preference in this regard is in both of the two mentioned respects, so it should not be supposed that they are preferred over the Muhajirun. Rather, the Muhajirun are more excellent, because they combined support with emigration, and because most of them had close kinship to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and precedence in Islam, which is a considerable share. This is what appeared to me of its relevance, on the assumption of its authenticity. What is in the Sahih from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: "The Prophet (ﷺ) wished to grant the Ansar land from Bahrain, so the Ansar said: 'Not until you grant our brothers the Muhajirun the like of what you grant us.' He said: 'You will see after me favoritism, so be patient until you meet me.'" In this is that the cause was their eagerness for fairness, and it indicates that the one who is fair receives little fairness from people, which is an established observation.

Al-wahy (revelation) is the casting of a meaning into the soul in concealment. Here it is what the angel brings to the Prophet, peace be upon them both, from Allah, the Exalted, and he casts it to him in a manner specific to him, without anyone else among people seeing that. Al-sabr (patience) is swallowing the bitterness of refraining from what is desired until the time when indulging in it is appropriate, and it is aided by knowledge of its outcome, much reflection on the report by which it is attained, and habituating oneself to patience in one trait, which makes patience in another trait easier, for good calls to good; so a person's firm establishment in one trait becomes for him a disposition that calls him to what resembles it. Glorified is He, He concluded the surah with what He began it with: the command concerning the Book and the indication toward guidance to what benefits from the fruit of its revelation, which is acting upon what it indicates or points to, until the Wise One who sent it becomes manifest in judging, in this world or in the Hereafter, with what cannot be averted, of what His true promises have made manifest in His perfect words. This very thing is the beginning of the surah that follows it, so the conclusion of this surah was a middle point between its beginning and the beginning of the one after it, and in this is the return of the ending to the opening, and a following-up of what was made to follow. And Allah is the Granter of success.
